pages.description: Wild and Scenic Rivers were designated by Congress for their outstandingly remarkable scenic, recreational, geologic, fish and wildlife, historic, cultural or other similar values. Alaska's Unalakleet River is one.
pages.text: A way to survive on Alaska’s west coast | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn A way to survive on Alaska’s west coast Jul 30, 2025 You might have heard of Unalakleet, a village marking the first coastal checkpoint for mushers in the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race. But Unalakleet, an Iñupiaq word meaning “place where the east wind blows,” is also the name of a river managed by BLM Alaska. The Unalakleet River on an overcast day. Photo by Stolf Short (BLM). Unalakleet River is one of six Wild and Scenic Rivers managed by BLM Alaska. These rivers were designated by Congress due to their outstandingly remarkable scenic, recreational, geologic, fish and wildlife, historic, cultural or other similar values. It is the BLM’s responsibility, in cooperation with other federal agencies, to preserve these rivers so they can be enjoyed by present and future generations. Starting in the rolling Nulato Hills, Unalakleet River flows west across miles of active, scenic tundra until it reaches the coastal village of Unalakleet. Eighty-one miles of the river are designated as Wild (not technically Scenic), though the westernmost portion of the river is on Native land and is not managed by BLM Alaska. BLM conducts breeding bird surveys on the Unalakleet to monitor populations, including Mergansers like these. Photo by Craig Townsend (BLM). For thousands of years, Unalakleet National Wild River has connected coastal Iñupiaq and Yup’ik peoples with Athabascan groups in interior Alaska. A relatively short overland trail called Kaltag Portage connects Unalakleet River with the Yukon River, making it an efficient way to travel in an area mostly without roads. In the 19th century, Russian merchants used the river and its portage to move people and goods. Reindeer herders from Lapland settled along the river and prospectors followed shortly after, looking for gold on the Seward Peninsula. The prospectors eventually brought a mail route, a telegraph line, and cabins along the river that can still be seen today. The biggest draw of Unalakleet National Wild River is its fishery, which provides subsistence, commercial, and recreational opportunities for residents and visitors. All five species of Pacific salmon—Chinook, Chum, Coho, Pink, and Sockeye—are found in the Unalakleet, contributing to salmon runs that exceed 100,000 fish. Annual salmon runs provide the bulk of the local community’s income. In addition to salmon, arctic grayling, Dolly Varden, arctic char, and whitefish are found in the river year-round. Other recreational opportunities include summer hunting of trophy-size brown bear and moose in the Nulato Hills or watching Iditarod mushers race 35 miles along Unalakleet River on their way to Nome. An Iditarod musher running his team between the Kaltag and Unalakleet checkpoints. Photo by Bob Wick (BLM). Unalakleet River supports the subsistence lifestyle of many villages in the area. In the fall, powerboats are the main mode of transportation for subsistence hunting of moose along the river. In the winter, trapping beaver, fox, lynx, marten, muskrat, and wolf provides cash for residents. When things start warming up in the spring, subsistence lifestyles are supported by hunting and gathering the eggs of local waterfowl. In the remote west coast of Alaska, Unalakleet National Wild River stands out as an invaluable resource for fishing, recreation, and subsistence. Plan a visit to see it for yourself at Unalakleet Wild and Scenic River | Bureau of Land Management. pages.description: He has been showing support for injured veterans in Ukraine and praising the country's resilience.
pages.text: Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine 6 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Sean Coughlan Royal correspondent, Lviv, Ukraine Press Association Prince Harry made an emotional visit to meet injured war veterans inside Ukraine The Duke of Sussex has received an enthusiastic welcome in a surprise visit to Ukraine to support injured war veterans, meeting Ukrainian competitors taking part in his Invictus Games. There were emotional scenes as he was applauded by injured service men and women in Lviv, where he told his audience: "You're going to win the war." Prince Harry spent two days at events for veterans, with a press blackout for security reasons until he had left Ukraine, as the country continues to face missile attacks from Russia. Ukraine has more than 150,000 injured war veterans and the prince visited projects supporting their treatment and rehabilitation. Press Association Prince Harry met Kostiantyn Vlasenko, who was airlifted by a drone from the front "Ukraine now is experiencing elements of war that no other country has experienced before," he said - with technology advancing in areas such as drone warfare, but also in protecting cities and providing treatment. A mobile phone app is where Ukrainians look for air raid warnings, telling them the direction, timing and type of any incoming missiles. At the Superhumans Center near Lviv, Harry was shown how growing numbers of injured veterans receive groundbreaking treatment. International experts used to come to help Ukraine, he said, but "now that has flipped," with Ukraine having the greater expertise with trauma injuries to share with others. Mykhailo Damaskin, pictured with his dog Stitch, has received experimental treatment to walk That included an innovation for Mykhailo Damaskin, a Ukrainian air assault forces veteran, who was so seriously injured in fighting in Kherson he was never expected to walk again. In an experimental treatment he had a spinal cord stimulator implanted in his back, which allows him to walk, but has to be re-charged every 12 hours. He cannot feel his feet and controls his steps using his eyes. He needs to be plugged in and charged up to be able to move - and jokes that he is "like a demo model of a Tesla". "My goal is to go to the Invictus Games. I promised my father before he was killed that I'd be part of the team to represent Ukraine internationally. "I'll prove to every guy with spinal cord injuries that life goes on after injury," said Mykhailo. At the Superhumans Center Prince Harry sat at the bedside of Konstiantyn Vlasenko, who was airlifted from the front line by a drone last month in a rescue that was a first of its kind. He had been alone for more than 200 days and had stayed at his position, despite losing both his feet. In a moving encounter, Prince Harry told him he represented the spirit of resilience of Ukraine. And he described the injured veterans as "role models", promising his audience: "The rest of the world will continue to support you." Along with all the determination, it was an inescapably poignant sight too, with so many families and children at the medical facility visiting the growing numbers of badly injured war casualties. Injured veterans took part in a game of wheelchair rugby Blast damage from missiles on an historic building in Lviv At a noisy sports centre, Prince Harry arrived to watch a wheelchair rugby match taking place, with some thunderous collisions between the players. He was welcomed by the competitors in what he has called his Invictus "family" and soon the visit turned into something approaching a group hug, with Harry disappearing into a sea of selfies and handshakes. pages.description: Democrats' numbers in state legislature no longer tiny enough to share just one pizza after ending Republican super-majority
pages.text: Arizona's 'one-pizza' Democrats taste success as GOP shares slice of the pie | Arizona | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Democrats were on track to win four seats in the state senate and at least four in the house of representatives. Photograph: Parker Haeg/Demotix/Corbis Democrats were on track to win four seats in the state senate and at least four in the house of representatives. Photograph: Parker Haeg/Demotix/Corbis Arizona This article is more than 14 years old Arizona's 'one-pizza' Democrats taste success as GOP shares slice of the pie This article is more than 14 years old Democrats' numbers in state legislature no longer tiny enough to share just one pizza after ending Republican super-majority Rory Carroll in Los Angeles Thu 8 Nov 2012 15.58 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Arizona Democrats are the "one-pizza caucus" no more. Their numbers in the state legislature – paltry enough to share a single pizza, went the joke – have surged and ended the Republican super-majority. Democrats were on track to win four seats in the state senate and at least four in the house of representatives in the wake of Tuesday's election, eroding GOP control over one of the south's most conservative states. Democrats hailed it as a "correction" to GOP overreach. "It's a beginning we can build upon," said one blogger . The Republican advantage in the senate shrank to 17-13, giving Democrats some muscle in looming fights over Medicaid expansion and the state's much-criticised immigration laws. However, in a tight vote, the surviving Republican senators on Wednesday promptly dumped their president, Steve Pierce, whom some had blamed for the senate's failure to pass additional bills against illegal immigration. They replaced him with the harder-line Andy Biggs, reflecting an ideological split between moderates and conservatives. Moderates gained some leverage with the election of John McComish as majority leader and Adam Driggs as majority whip. "Biggs' win suggests that the ideologues will run amok at the Capitol next year. However, the wins of McComish and Driggs suggest that some see the value in a more balanced crop of leaders, so there is hope yet," wrote Laurie Roberts, an Arizona Republic columnist . She doubted pragmatic Republicans would be able to restrain their more radical colleagues. "Why … do I feel like de-kookification just took a major hit?" Andy Tobin rebuffed a challenge from a more conservative Republican rival to keep his job as speaker of the house of representatives. Jan Brewer, the GOP governor who came to national prominence after backing the immigration laws, was not up for re-election. Joe Arpaio, America's self-styled "toughest sheriff", survived a close race to win an an unprecedented sixth term as Maricopa county sheriff. The American Civil Liberties Union and the justice department have filed lawsuits accusing him of civil rights violations and racial discrimination for his sweeps against undocumented immigrants. In a victory speech, the 80-year-old Arpaio, who has served as sheriff for two decades, said in his coming term he would try to explain his policies to Latinos. "I would hope to get together with the Latino community, if I could ever have them talk to me without screaming and threatening me." However, Arpaio, who denies wrongdoing, also said he had a message for President Barack Obama. "He's gone after me from the White House, the department of justice, the FBI, I can go on and on. But I will continue to enforce all the laws, including illegal immigration. Nothing changes." He also promised to run again in 2016. "This is my message to the media: you're going to have to put up with me for another eight years." Process of Working with Areas to Attain and Maintain NAAQS (Implementation Process) Process of Setting and Implementing NAAQS Standards - setting, reviewing, and revising the standards Designations - determining whether areas meet the standards Implementation - attaining and maintaining the standards When EPA establishes a new national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS) or revises an existing standard for a criteria air pollutant , it sets in motion a series of actions aimed at ensuring that air quality throughout the country meets those standards. EPA must designate areas as meeting (attainment) or not meeting (nonattainment) the standard. The Clean Air Act requires states to develop a general plan to attain and maintain the standards in all areas of the country and a specific plan to attain the standards for each area designated nonattainment. These plans, known as State Implementation Plans or SIPs, are developed by state and local air quality management agencies and submitted to EPA for approval. The SIPs serve two main purposes: Demonstrate that the state has the basic air quality management program components in place to implement a new or revised NAAQS. Identify the emissions control requirements the state will rely upon to attain and/or maintain the primary and secondary NAAQS. SIP Development Process Within 2 years after setting a new NAAQS or revising an existing standard: With input from the states and tribes, EPA must identify or "designate" areas as meeting (attainment areas) or not meeting (nonattainment areas), the standards. Designations are based on the most recent set of air monitoring or modeling data characterizing an area. Within 3 years after setting a new NAAQS or revising an existing standard: All states must submit state implementation plans (or plan revisions) to show they have the basic air quality management program components in place to implement a new or revised NAAQS, as specified in Clean Air Act section 110. These plans are often called "infrastructure SIPs." Learn more about Infrastructure SIP requirements . See Guidance on Development and Submission of Infrastructure State Implementation Plans for National Ambient Air Quality Standards (PDF) (62pp, 533k) Within 18-24 months after designations: Due dates for nonattainment area SIPs are based on the area designation date and vary by pollutant and area classification. SIPs for areas designated as nonattainment for sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), coarse particle pollution (PM 10 ), fine particle pollution (PM 2.5 ), and lead (Pb) are generally due no later than 18 months from the date of designation. SIPs for ozone (O 3 ) and carbon monoxide (CO) nonattainment areas are generally due 24 months or more from the date of designation, depending on the severity of the air pollution problem and the contents of the SIP. Each nonattainment area SIP must outline the strategies and emissions control measures that show how the area will improve air quality and meet the NAAQS. In addition, the Clean Air Act mandates that areas adopt certain specified control requirements. Learn more about SIP requirements for nonattainment areas. States must develop SIPs with public input, formally adopt SIPs into state law, and submit SIPs by the Governor's designee to EPA. After reviewing submitted SIPs, EPA proposes to approve or disapprove all or part of each plan. The public has an opportunity to comment on EPA's proposed action. pages.title: Lessons from a Creek | Bureau of Land Management Lock
pages.description: Alaska Native Science and Engineering Program students met and learned from BLM specialists who work on public land management, fire and fuels, biology, and hydrology.
pages.text: Lessons from a Creek | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Lessons from a Creek Jul 14, 2025 Alaska offers countless things for residents and visitors to marvel at, whether it’s snowcapped mountains, northern lights, or hulking glaciers. For students lucky enough to grow up in Alaska, the state’s extraordinary natural resources also make for an endless supply of learning opportunities. Earlier this month, the BLM partnered with the Alaska Native Science and Engineering Program (ANSEP) to provide an immersive learning experience for ANSEP high school students at the BLM’s Campbell Creek Science Center (CCSC) in Anchorage. Over the course of three days, students had the chance to meet with and learn from BLM specialists in fields critical to public land management, ranging from fire and fuels, biology, and hydrology. Since ANSEP students begin earning college credits as early as eighth grade, exposure to these specialized fields may help them decide what path to take once they reach university. Anchorage District Fuels Manager Jared Hammatt and Fire Management Specialist Ben Seifert were first up at bat. They spoke to students about how factors like weather, fuels, topography, and even insect outbreaks can factor into fire conditions for boreal forests like the kind that covers much of Alaska. Awareness of these influencing factors allows wildland firefighters to work through fire season more efficiently. Later in the day, fish biologist Sarah Hanchett arrived to explain the basics of her job, the importance of stable fish habitat in Alaska’s watersheds, and how BLM restoration projects are benefitting fish and the Alaskans that depend upon them. On the second day, a trio of BLM hydrologists arrived at CCSC, equipped with waders, depth rods, and a printed PowerPoint. Ben Stratton is the soils and water resources program lead for the Aquatic Resources Program, and BLM hydrologists Robin Welling and Charley Palmer contributed their expertise to the lesson. Students and hydrologists walked down to Campbell Creek to take advantage of the weather and shed some light on why hydrologists are so vital. In a state like Alaska, with over 12,000 rivers and 3 million lakes, their work is especially important. From left to right, BLM hydrologists Ben Stratton, Charley Palmer, and Robin Welling give a presentation on the basics of hydrology and how it relates to the lives of all Alaskans. Photo by Jordan Oldenburg, BLM. Their presentation covered the basics of hydrology and familiarized students with common terms like erosion, deposition, bankfull flow, and fluvial geomorphology. They also explained the two Qs that hydrologists concern themselves with: Quality and Quantity. With the creek running quickly behind them, each hydrologist took turns stepping up to give examples of what they might do in a typical workday. Stratton talked about how water in our streams is connected to our drinking water. Welling shared how the BLM monitors river health using a strategy called AIM – Assessment, Inventory, and Monitoring –pointing to real-world examples like the Platinum mine site. Palmer showed pictures and explained how to tell the difference between bars and islands in a river, as well as other features. Ben Stratton with a model that demonstrates Lane's Balance. Photo by Jordan Oldenburg, BLM. Back at CCSC, students got a hands-on lesson with a model of Lane’s Balance. This model shows how rivers change based on their slope, sediment, and amount of water. pages.title: Hull man and wife who fled Ukraine return to a warzone British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: John Holmes and his wife explain why they have returned to Ukraine after initially fleeing.
pages.text: Hull man and wife who fled Ukraine return to a warzone Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live 'Friends think we're idiots for returning to Ukraine' 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kevin Shoesmith East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire John Holmes Liliya Holmes and her British husband John pictured in Odesa, Ukraine When Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, John Holmes – a British national – and his Ukrainian wife Liliya fled the port city of Odesa, fearing for their lives. But after four years in the UK, the draw of home has proven too strong and they have returned to Ukraine's third largest city, undeterred by the sustained threat of air raids. "Friends of ours thought we were idiots for going back to Ukraine," reflects John, 74. "But returning is something we felt we needed to do. "Yes, it's dangerous. Yes, there are drones flying overhead. Yes, you can hear the explosions. But you just have to get on with life as best you can. "Home is Ukraine." During their time away, the pair sought sanctuary in Hull , East Yorkshire, where John was born and raised and has a property. He met Liliya, 64, in Ukraine and had been living there for 30 years until the invasion. "We had built a good life here," he says. John Holmes The Holmes say debris, which they believe to be from a Russian drone, landed on their property near Odesa During their four years in the UK, Liliya made several short trips back to Ukraine to visit family. John says: "After the fifth trip, I turned to her and said, 'maybe we should both go back together'. "We're now back. We're very happy to be back, too." The pair, who run a shipping company, have an apartment in Odesa city centre, close to their offices, and another property in a village about 20 miles away. Due to attacks on Odesa, John and Liliya are choosing to spend most of their time in the village, but even there they are subjected to frequent air raid warnings. "Every night you can hear the drones passing overhead," says John. "We've had bits of Russian drone land in our garden after they've been intercepted." Kevin Shoesmith/BBC The couple pictured in Hull in March 2022 John and Liliya say they have been buoyed by the stoicism of Ukrainians who they have encountered since their return in May this year. "Life goes on," says Liliya. "It has to. The war has become part of life. "Children are going to school in air raids. "People are trying to keep busy. We work. We plant strawberries. We watch television. Anything to distract ourselves from what is happening." John adds: "They are an incredible group of people. I have nothing but admiration for them." Ukrainians are braced for another cold winter, with frequent blackouts and disruptions to heating supplies. John and Liliya say they are fortunate to have gas central heating, which has not been affected so far. They recognise others have not been as fortunate. 'People are fatigued' The couple's business, like many others, has been severely impacted by the war. "Very little is going out of Odesa," he says. "Before the war, a lot of grain was exported [out of the port]. Now, because of Russian attacks, it's going down to the Danube. "We're staying afloat, with Greece providing us a bit of work." John says he and Liliya have been paying close attention to trilateral peace talks between Russia and Ukraine, mediated by the US. The talks concluded in Abu Dhabi earlier this week without a major breakthrough , though both sides confirmed plans for a large-scale prisoner of war exchange involving roughly 1,000 to 1,500 people. John says: "Ukrainians are showing real resilience, but overall they are fatigued with the war and continual attacks. Kemoklidze)曾因干燥方式不当，导致榛子受到由真菌产生的有毒物质污染，损失2万美元。如今，得益于联合国粮农组织提供的培训和资助，他使用一台以废弃坚果壳为燃料的烘干机，不仅保护了自己的收成，还帮助邻里烘干他们的作物。该倡议由欧盟和瑞典资助，将食品安全技能与设备改良相结合，以此减少损失、守护农民的生计。 可持续发展目标13：气候行动 , 世界粮食计划署 应对饥饿的气候行动 《 联合国气候变化框架公约 》缔约方会议第三十一届会议汇聚各国代表，共商气候变化应对之策。粮食署借此呼吁加大投资促进早期预警、气候抗御力和饥饿预防工作。 气候变化 , 联合国人口基金 气候危机中守护母亲 干旱、洪水和冲突威胁着索马里妇女的健康。人口基金正在加强建设气候适应型医疗卫生机构，并提供必要的孕产妇保健和保护服务。 可持续发展目标12：负责任消费和生产 , 联合国环境署 服装中隐藏的化学品 在阿根廷，一项由 环境署 支持的倡议正帮助纺织企业追踪有害化学物质，提高产品透明度，并通过数字产品护照，让回收利用更加安全。 可持续发展目标13：气候行动 , 联合国贸易和发展会议 联通市场，助力气候行动 联合国贸易和发展会议在《 联合国气候变化框架公约 》缔约方会议第三十一届会议上发布了一个全球网络，旨在加强碳市场建设、提高透明度并动员气候投资，特别是发展中国家的气候投资。 精彩继续 联合国的作用 由于《宪章》赋予的权利及其独特的国际性质，联合国可就人类在21世纪面临的一系列问题采取行动，包括： 维护国际和平与安全 保护人权 提供人道主义援助 促进可持续发展 捍卫国际法 维护国际和平与安全 第二次世界大战结束后的1945年，联合国宣布成立，并将 维护国际和平与安全 确立为主要目的之一。联合国为维护国际和平与安全所开展的活动主要涉及：预防冲突、促成冲突各方达成和平、维持和平及创造让和平延续发展的环境。 保护人权 “人权”一词在《 联合国宪章 》中出现了七次，促进和保护人权被确定为联合国工作的重要目标和指导原则。1948年，《 世界人权宣言 》将人权列入国际法范畴，此后，联合国通过法律文书和实地工作大力推动保护人权工作。 提供人道主义援助 正如 《联合国宪章》 所述，联合国的宗旨之一是“促成国际合作，以解决国际间属于经济、社会、文化及人类福利性质之国际问题”。第二次世界大战后，联合国在满目疮痍的欧洲大陆首次开展了国际合作，以帮助欧洲进行重建。如今联合国为国际社会所依重，在超出国家主管当局应对能力之外的自然和人为灾害地区协调 人道主义救济行动 。 促进可持续发展 自1945年起，联合国的主要优先事项之一是“促成国际合作，以解决国际间属于经济、社会、文化及人类福利性质之国际问题，且不分种族、性别、语言或宗教，增进并激励对于全体人类之人权及基本自由之尊重。”提升人们的福祉仍是联合国的主要关注点之一。全球对发展的理解在不断改变，如今各个国家达成共识，认为能促进繁荣、增加经济机会、提升社会福祉和改善环境保护的 可持续发展 为改善世界各地人民的生活提供最佳的路径。 捍卫国际法 《 联合国宪章 》序言中设立了如下目标：“创造适当环境，俾克维持正义，尊重由条约与国际法其他渊源而起之义务，久而弗懈”。自设立该目标以来，发展、尊重 国际法 一直是联合国工作的重点。联合国通过众多途径（包括法院、法庭和多边条约）和安全理事会推进该项工作。在国际和平与安全受到威胁时，安全理事会在必要时会批准维和行动，实施制裁或授权使用武力。作为国际条约的《联合国宪章》赋予安全理事会这些权限。严格来讲，《联合国宪章》是国际法文件，联合国各会员国必须遵守。《联合国宪章》确立了国际关系的主要原则，包括在处理国际关系时确保各会员国之间的主权平等，并限制使用武力等。 系统机构 联合国有六个主要机关： 大会 、 安全理事会 、 经济及社会理事会 、 托管理事会 、 国际法院 和 秘书处 ，均设立于1945年联合国成立之时。 大会 大会是联合国的主要审议、决策和代表性机关，由联合国全部193个会员国组成，是唯一具有普遍代表性的机关。 安全理事会 根据《联合国宪章》，安全理事会负有维护国际和平与安全的首要责任。安理会有15个理事国（五个常任理事国和十个非常任理事国），每个理事国有一个投票权。《宪章》规定，所有理事国都有义务履行安理会的决定。 经济及社会理事会 经济及社会理事会是就经济、社会和环境问题进行协调、政策审查和政策对话并提出建议，以及落实国际发展目标的主要机关。 托管理事会 托管理事会于1945年根据《联合国宪章》第十三章设立，对由7个会员国管理的11个托管领土实行国际监督，并确保管理国采取适当措施为托管领土的自治或独立做好准备。 国际法院 国际法院是联合国的主要司法机关，位于荷兰海牙的和平宫，是联合国六大主要机关中唯一设在美国纽约之外的机关。 秘书处 秘书处由秘书长和在世界各地为联合国工作的数万名国际工作人员组成，负责处理大会和其他主要机关委任的各项日常工作。 更多联合国作用介绍 工作重点 遴选下一任秘书长 联合国下一任秘书长任命程序已启动，并本着透明与包容原则举行了候选人互动对话。欢迎通过联合国网络电视观看。日程安排： 费里敦·哈迪·西尼尔利奥卢 （11月6日）， 拉娜·扎基·努赛贝 （10月27日）， 伊沃内·阿巴基 （8月20日）， 米歇尔·巴切莱特·赫里亚 （4月21日）， 拉斐尔·马里亚诺·格罗西 （4月21日）， 玛丽亚·费尔南达·埃斯皮诺萨 （6月15日）， 蕾韦卡·格林斯潘·马尤菲斯 （4月22日）， 奥拉拉·奥图努 （8月19日）， 卡罗琳·罗德里格斯

pages.title: GOP Senator Jeff Flake attacks 'reckless, outrageous and undignified' Trump | Republicans | The Guardian
pages.description: The Arizona senator joined a list of high-profile Republicans, including Bob Corker, who have opted to retire amid the turmoil of Donald Trump’s presidency
pages.text: GOP Senator Jeff Flake attacks 'reckless, outrageous and undignified' Trump | Republicans | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation 1:24 Senator Jeff Flake announces he won’t seek re-election – video Republicans This article is more than 9 years old GOP Senator Jeff Flake attacks 'reckless, outrageous and undignified' Trump This article is more than 9 years old The Arizona senator joined a list of high-profile Republicans, including Bob Corker, who have opted to retire amid the turmoil of Donald Trump’s presidency Jeff Flake’s speech: ‘Anger and resentment are not a governing philosophy’ Sabrina Siddiqui in Washington Wed 25 Oct 2017 04.01 EDT First published on Tue 24 Oct 2017 16.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Arizona senator Jeff Flake has launched an extraordinary attack against Donald Trump and the “complicity” of the Republican party as he announced his decision to leave the Senate. Flake, a key Republican critic of Trump, said he was retiring at the end of his term in 2018 because there was no room for him in the party under the current president’s stewardship. He then delivered an emotional appeal from the Senate floor against the state of affairs under Trump, bemoaning that his Republican colleagues had “given in or given up on core principles in favor of a more viscerally satisfying anger and resentment”. Jeff Flake: conservatives face a crisis. We must now tell and expect the truth Read more “It is time for our complicity and our accommodation for the unacceptable to end,” Flake said. “There are times when we must risk our careers in favor of our principles. Now is such a time. “We must never allow ourselves to lapse into thinking that that is just the way things are now,” he added. “We must stop pretending that the degradation of our politics and the conduct of some in our executive branch are normal.” “Reckless, outrageous, and undignified behavior has become excused and countenanced as ‘telling it like it is’ when it is actually just reckless, outrageous, and undignified.” He said such behavior was “dangerous to our democracy” and projected not strength but a “corruption of the spirit”. He then asked his colleagues: “When the next generation asks us: ‘Why didn’t you do something? Why didn’t you speak up? What are we going to say?’” Flake joins a list of high-profile Republicans who have jumped ship in recent months amid the turmoil of Trump’s presidency. Bob Corker, the chairman of the Senate foreign relations committee, declared his retirement last month and has since been locked in a bitter feud with Trump that reached new heights on Tuesday . Hours before Flake’s announcement, Trump’s war of words with Corker escalated in unprecedented fashion ahead of a meeting between the president and Senate Republicans on Capitol Hill. Prior to the closed-door luncheon, Corker branded Trump as an “utterly untruthful president” on NBC’s Today Show. In a separate interview with CNN, Corker went even further, stating of the president: “I don’t know why he lowers himself to such a low, low standard and debases our country in that way but he does.” Coupled with Flake’s scathing remarks on the Senate floor, the growing list of Republicans sounding the alarm over Trump’s presidency marked a potential watershed moment within the party. Several prominent Republicans have spoken out, albeit in veiled terms, against so-called “Trumpism” in recent weeks. John McCain, who represents Arizona alongside Flake in the Senate, denounced “half-baked, spurious nationalism” in a speech last week that also decried the abdication of US leadership on the global stage. Days later, George W Bush condemned bigotry while declaring American politics “more vulnerable to conspiracy theories and outright fabrication”. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, the White House press secretary, played into the intra-party rift by dubbing Flake’s decision as “a good move” while telling reporters his remarks were not “befitting of the Senate floor”. National Recreation Trail designation promotes some of our country's highest-caliber trails with the intention of providing recreation access to rural and urban communities, economic development through tourism, and healthy recreation opportunities. National Recreation Trails are recognized by the federal government, with the consent of any Federal, State, Tribal, local, nonprofit, or private entity having jurisdiction over these lands. pages.text: Current and Recently Completed Work | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Current and Recently Completed Work ODEP and our grantees, contractors, and other partners undertake a variety of research, analysis and evaluation efforts to help us achieve our mission. This page contains information and links to work currently underway as well as work published in the past year. For tools and other resources related to research highlighted in this section, please visit project-specific pages. 2026 Research Support Services for Employment of Young Adults on the Autism Spectrum (REYAAS) Project REYAAS (August 2021 to September 2026) is seeking to identify promising practices and policies to support the employment of young people (ages 16 to 28) on the autism spectrum. Recent estimates suggest that annually about 100,000 children on the autism spectrum turn 18 in the United States. A majority of young adults on the autism spectrum have one or more co-occurring health or mental health conditions, and young adults on the autism spectrum are more likely than young adults without disabilities to be living in households with income below the federal poverty level. Young adults on the autism spectrum can face challenges to entering the labor force, including a sudden reduction of services when exiting high school (the “services cliff”). In addition autistic young adults are less likely to participate in vocational or technical education or have a job after leaving high school, compared with young adults with other disabilities. Capstone Webinar On September 16, 2026, Mathematica delivered a capstone webinar to the public, providing an overview of project findings, with remarks from ODEP Assistant Secretary Julie Hocker, Jeff Hemmeter, Scott Robertson, and Tiffany Jameson. The recorded presentation and PowerPoint slides are available. Recording of the capstone webinar Slides presented during the capstone webinar Employer Practices Brief This brief describes principles and practices that employers can apply to improve the hiring and retaining of autistic workers. Employer practices brief LifeMAP Case Study Brief This brief describes the Life Management Assistance Program (LifeMAP) one-on-one coaching program that helps people on the autism spectrum identify and work toward goals, including attaining and retaining employment. LifeMAP case study brief Evaluation Design Options Report This report builds on literature reviews and listening sessions conducted in the knowledge development phase of the REYAAS project. It presents evaluation design options for the following interventions, which are designed to improve employment outcomes for autistic young adults: enhancing access to Registered Apprenticeship and related support services; tailoring YouthBuild program to the needs of autistic young adults; enhancing access to supported employment in Vocational Rehabilitation; and incorporating virtual interview training for transition-age youth in Job Corps. Evaluation design options report Spotlight on evaluation design options report Data Analysis Report This report examines the way young adults on the autism spectrum (ages 16 to 28) engage with state Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) agencies, the characteristics of those who apply for VR services, the VR services they use, and their employment outcomes. This study examined Rehabilitation Services Administration—Case Service Reports (RSA-911) restricted-use files for program years 2017 to 2020. Data analysis report Spotlight on data analysis report Infographic on data analysis report Data Inventory Brief This issue brief presents an inventory of 11 data sets, including administrative and survey data sources, that contain employment-related information about young adults on the autism spectrum. Researchers can use these data sets to shed light on the topic, though the data are limited in their ability to provide a detailed, longitudinal assessment of this population or their employment outcomes.

The one-room schoolhouse of Colonial days was a simple design built from local materials. Kids sat on benches with the oldest in the back. While nostalgia has kept these in our minds, they were hardly conducive for much beyond basic rote learning. IRS 는 대부분의 환급금을 21일 이내에 지급합니다. 환급 현황 확인 가능 시점: 전자 신고서 : 본 기관이 접수한 후 24시간 이내 서면신고서: 발송 후 4주 뒤 다음의 경우에만 전화 연락을 취하십시오: 전자 신고서: 제출 후 3주 경과 서면신고: 발송 후 6주 경과 서식 8379, ‘피해 배우자 할당’: 전자 신고는 12주, 서면 신고서 제출은 14주 경과 환급: '내 환급금은 어디 있나요?' 도구가 본 기관에 연락하도록 안내한 경우 IRS 운영 및 서비스에 대한 최신 정보 얻기(영어) 세금 신고서 정정 또는 수정 수정 신고서를 제출해야 하는지 여부(영어) 내 수정 신고서가 어디에 있습니까? 수정 신고서 관련 자주 묻는 질문 수정 신고서 제출 후 현황을 확인하려면: 신고서를 제출하고 3주 후에 ‘내 수정 신고서가 어디에 있습니까?’ 도구를 사용하십시오. 다음 경우에만 전화 연락을 취하십시오: 수정 신고서를 우편 발송한 후 16주가 경과했거나, ‘내 수정 신고서가 어디에 있습니까?’ 도구가 본 기관에 전화하도록 안내한 경우 납부 및 가산세 납부 납부 옵션 납부 계획 또는 분할 납부 합의 잔액 및 납부 내역 조회 생활고를 겪고 있는 납세자에 대한 도움(영어) 세액 조정 제안 선취권 및 압류 연방세 선취권 이해하기 압류 이해하기(영어) 간행물 594, ‘ IRS 징수 절차’(영어) PDF 분쟁 해결 항소국 향후 세금 고지서 방지 세금 원천징수 추정기 세금 중간예납 가산세 가산세 감면/경감 IRS IRS 통지서 또는 서신 이해하기 EITC 세무조사 통지서 또는 서신 툴키트 IRS 문서 업로드 도구(영어) 신원 인증하기(5071 C )(영어) 신원 인증하기(4883 C )(영어) 본 기관이 귀하의 세금 신고서를 변경했습니다( CP 12)(영어) 압류 임박 고지( CP 504)(영어) 소득 신고 또는 지불 오류( CP 2000)(영어) 체납액 고지서( CP 71 A )(영어) 다른 신고서에 기재된 부양가족의 사회보장번호( CP 87 A )(영어) IRS 서면 통신의 선호 언어 설정 변경(영어) 신원 도용, 사기 및 신용 사기 신원 도용 신원 도용 방지 센터 신원 도용에 대한 납세자 가이드 정보 보안 IRS 통지 4883 C (영어) 또는 CP 01(영어) 신원 확인 신원 보호 PIN ( IP PIN ) 받기 사기수법 피싱, 전화 및 이메일 사기 신고 사기 세금 사기로 의심되는 활동을 신고하는 방법 세무 대리인에 대한 민원 제기(영어) 세금 신고하기 준비하기 W- 2에 오류가 있거나, 분실 또는 받지 못한 경우(영어) 개인 납세자 식별 번호( ITIN ) 신고 지원 세금 신고 방법: 단계별 안내 무료 세금 신고 준비 지원 세무 전문가 선택하기 신고 전자식 신고 및 계좌 입금 방식을 이용하여 지연을 방지하십시오. IRS Free File : 무료로 세금을 신고하십시오 세금을 신고하는 다른 방법들을 알아보십시오 군인을 위한 세금 정보 환급금 계좌 입금 세금 신고 기한 연장 사망자의 세금 신고(영어) 기한이 경과한 세금 신고하기 조정총소득( AGI )으로 e-file 신고서에 서명하기 비고: AGI 는 전화로 확인할 수 없습니다. 온라인 계정 또는 작년 세금 신고서에서 귀하의 AGI 를 확인할 수 있습니다 - 사본을 요청하십시오 . 우편으로 제출​​​​​ 신고서를 보낼 우편 주소 찾기 흔한 질문 사항 대화형 세무 지원을 이용하여 다음과 같은 세무 관련 질문에 대한 답을 얻으십시오: 귀하의 실업 수당은 과세대상입니까? 귀하가 세금 신고서를 제출해야 합니까?(영어) 귀하의 납세자 구분은 무엇입니까?(영어) 귀하의 사회보장혜택은 과세대상입니까?(영어) 귀하의 퇴직연금은 과세 대상입니까?(영어) 세금 증명서 얻기 세금 증명서 주문하기 증명서 유형 증명서를 받을 수 있는 다른 방법들 무신고 서신 받기 증명서 얻기 관련 자주묻는질문(영어) 사업 관련 주제 고용세 e-file E-file 서명 PIN 신청하기(영어) ​​​​​ 고용주식별번호( EIN ) 온라인에서 EIN 신청하기 온라인에서 서식 2290 제출하기(영어) 고객 서비스 의견 귀하의 의견을 소중히 생각합니다. 서비스 개선에 도움이 될 수 있도록 최근 IRS 고객 서비스 담당자와의 경험에 대한 의견을 공유해 주십시오(영어) . 귀하의 언어로 지원 IRS.gov 에서 세금 관련 질문에 대한 답변을 찾을 수 없는 경우, 본 기관은 전문 통역사의 지원을 받아 스페인어, 중국어(만다린어, 광둥어), 한국어, 베트남어, 러시아어, 아이티 크레올어로 도움을 제공합니다. 대체 매체 형식 요청 우편으로 받은 서식 또는 통지서의 접근 가능한 버전을 요청하는 가장 빠른 방법은 대체 매체 형식 요청(영어) 을 선택하는 것입니다. 서식 및 간행물 등 기타 접근 가능한 세금 자료에 대한 자세한 내용은 접근 가능한 IRS 세금 자료(영어) 페이지를 방문하십시오. 통역 서비스 스페인어는 800-829-1040 로 전화하십시오. 그 외 모든 언어는 833-553-9895 로 전화하십시오. 다음 서비스를 제공할 수 있는 IRS 직원과 연결됩니다: 전화 통역을 제공하거나 지역 납세자 지원 센터(영어) 중 한곳에 예약하여 대면으로 도움을 받으십시오. 지역 사무실은 특정 주제 에 대해서만 지원이 가능하다는 점을 고려하십시오. 전화 및 지역 사무소 지원 세금 신고서 또는 서신을 우편으로 제출한 후 본 기관의 응답을 받지 못한 경우, 전화하거나 신고서를 다시 제출하지 마십시오. 현재 IRS 운영 및 서비스(영어) 의 예상 대기 시간을 확인하십시오. IRS 전화번호 전화 상담원은 다양한 주제에 대해 도움을 줄 수 있습니다. 단, IRS 전화 상담원이 다룰 수 없는 주제(영어) 목록도 참고하십시오. 전화연락 시 본인 신원 인증하기 본 기관의 상담원은 귀하의 개인 정보를 논의하기 전에 귀하의 신원을 확인해야 합니다. 전화연락시 다음을 준비하십시오: 개인 사회보장 번호( SSN ) 및 생년월일 사회보장 번호가 없는 납세자의 경우, 개인 납세자 식별 번호( ITIN ) 납세자 구분 – 미혼, 세대주, 부부공동신고, 부부개별신고, 또는 적격생존배우자 전년도 세금 신고서 귀하가 문의하고자 하는 세금 신고서 본 기관에서 보낸 서신 다른 사람을 대신해 전화하는 제3자 납세자의 성명, SSN 또는 ITIN 귀하가 전화로 문의하고자 하는 세금 신고서 계정에 관하여 논의할 수 있는 구두 또는 서면 승인( 서식 8821, ‘세금 정보 승인’(영어) 또는 서식 2848, ‘위임장 및 대리인 신고서’(영어) 세무 대리인 세금 식별 번호( PTIN )(영어) 또는 개인 식별 번호( PIN ) 사망한 납세자를 대신해 전화하는 제3자 사망 증명서 법원 승인 서신 또는 IRS 서식 56, ‘신탁 관계에 관한 통지’(영어) (상속 재산 집행인 용) IRS 전화 번호 - 통화 대기 시간 세금 신고 기간 (1월 ~ 4월) 전화 상담 대기 시간은 평균 8분 입니다. 일부 전화 상담 라인은 대기 시간이 더 길 수 있습니다. 전화 상담 대기 시간은 월요일과 화요일, 대통령의 날( Presidents Day ) 주말과 4월 세금 신고 마감일 무렵 더 길어집니다. 세금 신고 기간 이후 (5월 ~ 12월) 전화 상담 대기 시간은 평균 15분입니다. 일부 전화 상담 라인은 대기

pages.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments - a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed".
pages.text: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says 1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Aleks Phillips and Sarah Rainsford , Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent, Kyiv Getty Images US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments. A US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed but any final deal will have to be agreed to by both parties". Zelensky's remarks came after US envoys met him and Russian President Vladimir Putin as part of US efforts to end the war between their two countries. Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others, while Russia has said another Nato member on its border was unacceptable. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and currently controls most of the industrial Donbas region. Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine was unwilling to give up sovereign territory. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday. He went on to say that if he received a specific proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow. Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted. It has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal. Ukraine has rejected these suggestions, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion. Other Nato members apart from the US are wary of membership for Ukraine - and it is understood that Ukraine itself sees it as unrealistic. The Kremlin has always been fiercely opposed, too. It is one reason why Russia started this war in the first place. It is possible the US envoys were exploring Ukraine's "red lines" when it comes to occupied land in the Donbas. Zelensky recently said that the two American mediators believed Kyiv only had to cede territory to achieve peace and were applying pressure, keen to do a deal as soon as possible. Ukraine is sure that Russia's ambitions are far greater and has long seen Nato as its only sure protection. So it is also possible that Zelensky made this suggestion public to re-open a discussion that had been considered all but closed. He said the idea was now "back on the agenda" as part of an "extremely difficult conversation" on European security in his latest remarks. It also looks like Ukrainian push-back against Russia's renewed hardline stance. Moscow now talks about a "new European security architecture", which is long-standing Russian code for a weaker Nato. The issue appears to have been the main focus at the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week. Hours after Zelensky's remarks, Jared Kushner appeared keen to dampen down any US offer of Nato membership for Ukraine, urging "confidentiality" in a sensitive process. He said that "maximalist" proposals had been reported from the negotiations, along with "strong political rhetoric". Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office October 30, 2026 Estimated Read Time min The U.S. Energy Association and the National Laboratory Gasification Consortium (NLGC) will host an update on research and development advancing gasification technologies and alternative feedstock utilization. The free webinar, A 2026 Update on the National Laboratory Gasification Consortium , will take place on November 2, 2026, from 1:00 pm – 3:00 pm ET. Led by the National Energy Technology Laboratory and supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office , the webinar will provide an overview of the NLGC, present accomplishments through its first year of operation, and highlight planned work to support the needs of the gasification community in its four key topic areas: Feedstock Supply-Chain Modeling & Analysis Upstream Feedstock Quality and Preprocessing Feedstock Variability Sensing for Gasifier Control Developing a Co-gasification Kinetic Database and Machine Learning Tool NLGC’s goal is to facilitate the use of a broader spectrum of alternative and blended feedstocks to produce chemicals, fuels or hydrogen and ensure fuel resiliency in gasification systems. For more information, contact NLGC Industry Engagement Lead Jim Parks at parksjeii@NLGC.gov . Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us America's National Trails System "A national trail is a gateway into nature’s secret beauties, a portal to the past, a way into solitude and community. It is also an inroad to our national character. Our trails are both irresistible and indispensable." —STEWART UDALL, US Secretary of the Interior (1961–69); 1920–2010 The National Trails System Act of 1968, as amended, calls for establishing trails in both urban and rural settings for people of all ages, interests, skills, and physical abilities. The National Trails System promotes the enjoyment and appreciation of trails while encouraging greater public access. The system includes national scenic trails, national historic trails, and national recreation trails. The National Park Service encourages all public and private agencies to develop, maintain, and protect trails. With the cooperation and support of a nationwide trails community, the vision of an interconnected, cross-country trail system will become a reality. NAAQS Table The Clean Air Act , which was last amended in 1990, requires EPA to set National Ambient Air Quality Standards (40 CFR part 50) for six principal pollutants ( "criteria" air pollutants ) which can be harmful to public health and the environment. The Clean Air Act identifies two types of national ambient air quality standards. Primary standards provide public health protection, including protecting the health of "sensitive" populations such as asthmatics, children, and the elderly. Secondary standards provide public welfare protection, including protection against decreased visibility and damage to animals, crops, vegetation, and buildings. Periodically, the standards are reviewed and sometimes may be revised, establishing new standards. The most recently established standards are listed below. In some areas of the U.S., certain regulatory requirements may also remain for implementation of previously established standards . Units of measure for the standards are parts per million (ppm) by volume, parts per billion (ppb) by volume, and micrograms per cubic meter of air (µg/m 3 ). Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. Acerca del asma Para todos 28 de ago. del 2026 English (US) Puntos clave El asma es una enfermedad que afecta los pulmones. Es una de las enfermedades de larga duración más comunes en los niños, pero los adultos también pueden presentarla. El asma causa sibilancias, dificultad para respirar, opresión en el pecho y tos durante la noche o temprano en la mañana. Lo que es El asma es una enfermedad que afecta los pulmones. El asma causa sibilancias, dificultad para respirar, opresión en el pecho y tos durante la noche o temprano en la mañana. El asma es algo que se tiene todo el tiempo, pero usted solo tendrá ataques de asma cuando algo afecte sus pulmones. Síntomas El asma causa sibilancias, dificultad para respirar, opresión en el pecho y tos durante la noche o temprano en la mañana. El asma es algo que se tiene todo el tiempo, pero usted solo tendrá ataques de asma cuando algo afecte sus pulmones. Un ataque de asma puede incluir tos, opresión en el pecho, sibilancias y dificultad para respirar. El ataque ocurre en las vías respiratorias, que son los conductos que llevan aire a los pulmones. A medida que el aire entra a los pulmones, pasa por vías respiratorias cada vez más pequeñas, como las ramas de un árbol que son más pequeñas que el tronco. Durante un ataque de asma, las paredes de las vías respiratorias en los pulmones se inflaman, y las vías respiratorias se vuelven más estrechas. Entra y sale menos aire de los pulmones, y la mucosidad que su cuerpo produce tapona las vías respiratorias. Usted puede manejar el asma si reconoce los signos de advertencia de un ataque, se mantiene alejado de las cosas que pueden provocar un ataque y sigue los consejos de su médico. Diagnóstico Puede ser difícil determinar si alguien tiene asma, especialmente si se trata de niños menores de 5 años. Un médico puede ayudarlo a averiguar si tiene asma. Durante el chequeo, el médico podría preguntarle si tose mucho, particularmente de noche. También podría preguntarle si la dificultad para respirar empeora después de la actividad física o durante ciertas épocas del año. También podría preguntarle si ha tenido opresión en el pecho, sibilancias y resfriados que duraran más de 10 días. Le preguntará si alguien en su familia tiene o ha tenido asma, alergias u otros problemas respiratorios. El médico también podría preguntarle acerca de su casa y si ha faltado a la escuela o el trabajo, o si tiene dificultad para hacer ciertas cosas. Y podría hacerle una prueba respiratoria, llamada espirometría, para averiguar qué tan bien están funcionando sus pulmones. Una espirometría mide cuánto aire exhala después de respirar hondo, antes y después de usar medicamentos para el asma. Manejo de síntomas Para controlar el asma, adminístrese los medicamentos según las indicaciones exactas de su médico y manténgase alejado de las cosas que puedan desencadenar un ataque. No todas las personas con asma usarán los mismos medicamentos. Algunos medicamentos se inhalan, otros se toman como pastillas. Los medicamentos para el asma se pueden usar de varias maneras, como terapia de alivio o como terapia de control. Si usted necesita usar su medicamento de alivio cada vez más, consulte a su médico para ver si necesita un medicamento distinto. Los medicamentos de control lo ayudan a tener menos ataques de asma y a que sean más leves. Los medicamentos para el asma pueden causar efectos secundarios. Notice of Intent: Leveraging Domestic Infrastructure and Resources to Unleash Alternative Chemicals, Fuels, and Feedstocks Funding Opportunity Banner Color Light Text on a Dark Overlay (Default) The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office (AFFO) announced its intent to award up to $60 million to expand domestic energy production and distribution through novel, high-impact chemicals, fertilizers, fuels, and feedstock technologies. The funding opportunity, Leveraging Domestic Infrastructure and Resources to Unleash Alternative Chemicals, Fuels, and Feedstocks, fulfills President Donald J. Trump’s Executive Order, Unleashing American Energy which calls for affordable and reliable domestic energy production and strong domestic supply chains to lower prices for hardworking Americans, including farmers, ranchers, and small businesses. DOE will seek research, development and scale-up projects that harness existing domestic biomass, hydrogen, and pipeline resources to expand U.S. domestic energy production, distribution, and fertilizer technologies. Topic Areas AFFO expects to issue a notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) in November 2026, addressing the following topic areas: Topic Area 1: Biointermediate Depots Enhance the production of liquid intermediate-products that are made from biomass and establish pilot sites to produce traditional intermediate products such as high impact chemicals, sugars, bio-crudes, or bio-oils, from biomass and wastes. Projects under this topic area will derisk technologies for solids-to-liquids conversion, while also validating the economics of distributed depots that would operate on a hub-and-spoke model, sending intermediate products to a central hub (a refinery or biorefinery) for further upgrading to finished products. Topic Area 2 : Refinery Integration Advance the production of commodity chemicals and fuels from alternative feedstocks using existing refinery assets and achieving production-costs that enable competitive market pricing. This topic area also supports research and development to advance technologies for processing intermediates in existing refinery or petrochemical infrastructure. For example, projects under this topic could conduct research into co-processing biocrudes or waste plastic oils with crude oil to determine impact on catalyst life, the mix and proportions of different end-products, and compatibility with the plant’s physical equipment. Topic Area 3: Pilot Site for Hydrogen/Natural Gas Blending Establish pilot sites for hydrogen and natural gas blending and the distribution/utilization of those blends to improve the reliability, scalability, suitability, performance and durability of distribution networks. Projects under this topic area will address stakeholder needs by evaluating the reliability and scalability potential associated with blending, including the suitability, performance, and durability of pipeline components. They may also provide valuable information that will help address the unique workforce needs related to hydrogen-natural gas blending. This site will represent an intermediate step prior to broader large-scale blending in commercial applications. Applicants should plan to leverage existing relevant assets and include a business and management plan for continued facility operation after the end of the DOE award. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us Community-Led Conservation and Development National Heritage Areas are places where historic, cultural, and natural resources combine to form cohesive, nationally important landscapes. Unlike national parks, National Heritage Areas are large lived-in landscapes. Consequently, National Heritage Area entities collaborate with communities to determine how to make heritage relevant to local interests and needs. In 1984, the first National Heritage Area, Illinois and Michigan Canal National Heritage Area, was signed into law by President Ronald Reagan. In his dedication speech, Reagan referred to National Heritage Areas as "a new kind of national park" that married heritage conservation, recreation, and economic development. On January 5, 2023, President Biden signed the National Heritage Areas Act (P.L. 117-339) into law. This law established the National Heritage Area System, a statutory framework for the National Park Service’s role in its administration. In 2023, seven National Heritage Areas were designated, bringing the total to 62 National Heritage Areas . Today, National Heritage Areas and the National Park Service are making an impact nationwide: Read our 2025 Annual Report ! The National Heritage Areas brochure (NPS unigrid) is a great way to learn more and easy to share. Heritage Areas 101: What is an NHA? pages.title: Employment Rights: Who has Them and Who Enforces Them | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: Employment Rights: Who has Them and Who Enforces Them | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Employment Rights: Who has Them and Who Enforces Them Individuals with disabilities are protected from discrimination in employment primarily by two federal laws. The Americans with Disabilities Act (Public Law 101-336), enacted into law on July 26, 1990, prohibits private sector employers who employ 15 or more individuals and all State and local government employers from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities in all aspects of employment. The Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Public Law 93-112), as amended, prohibits discrimination in employment in three areas. Section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act prohibits federal executive branch agencies, including the U.S. Postal Service and the Postal Rate Commission, from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities. It requires executive branch agencies to take affirmative action in the hiring, placing and advancing of individuals with disabilities. Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act requires contractors who have a contract with the federal government for $10,000 or more, and their subcontractors who have subcontracts satisfying the same criteria, to take affirmative action to employ and to advance in employment qualified individuals with disabilities. Section 504 prohibits recipients of federal financial assistance from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities in employment and in their programs and activities. Section 188 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) forbids disability-based discrimination, in employment or in provision of services, by any organization or other entity that receives Federal financial assistance under WIA, and by any program or activity that is provided as part of the nation's One-Stop job training system by a One-Stop partner. Veterans with disabilities are protected further by 38 U.S. Code 4212 of the Vietnam Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 (VEVRAA). VEVRAA requires that contractors or subcontractors who have a contract with the federal government for $25,000 or more take affirmative action to employ, advance in employment, and otherwise treat covered veterans without discrimination. Individuals with disabilities also may be protected by their state anti-discrimination laws, some of which are more stringent than the federal laws. To learn more about rights under state laws, contact the State Human Rights Commission or its equivalent, or contact the State Governor's Committee on People with Disabilities. Applicants or Employees with Disabilities in the Private Sector If a private sector employer employs 15 or more people, an individual with a disability who is employed by or applies for employment with that employer is protected by Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), enforced primarily by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). To file a complaint under ADA Title I, contact the nearest EEOC office or call 1-800-669-4000 (voice) or 1-800-669-6820 (TTY). If EEOC dismisses the complaint or fails to take action within 180 days, EEOC will issue the individual a right to sue letter, upon the person's request. The individual must sue within 90 days of the date of the notice. If a private sector employer has a contract with the federal government for $10,000 or more, or a subcontract for that amount with a Federal contractor, an individual with a disability who is employed by or applies for employment with that employer is protected by Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended, enforced by the U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP). To file a complaint under Section 503, send it to OFCCP at the nearest U.S. Department of Labor district or regional office. pages.title: Self-Employment & Entrepreneurship | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: Self-Employment & Entrepreneurship | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Self-Employment & Entrepreneurship More in This Section Close Federal Employers Recruitment and Retention Research & Publications Self-Employment & Entrepreneurship Small Business Tax Incentives for Employers Self-employment has long been an option for individuals seeking a new or better career. And today, many individuals with disabilities are turning to the flexibility self-employment offers in assisting them to meet both professional and financial goals. Starting one's own business can offer similar flexibility, allowing people to make a living while maintaining a lot of latitude in choices such as work hours, nature of tasks, and income. As a result, ODEP encourages and supports self-employment and entrepreneurship among individuals with disabilities and has helped foster an array of partnerships at the federal, state, and local levels to encourage access to funding and resources to assist individuals with disabilities interested in these alternatives to traditional employment. The following resources provide more information about self-employment and entrepreneurship: JAN Entrepreneurship Resources — The ODEP-funded Job Accommodation Network (JAN) provides entrepreneurs with individualized technical assistance expertise and referrals. JAN’s self-employment consultants can help with business development planning, financing strategies, marketing research, disability-specific programs, income supports, benefits planning, e-commerce, independent contracting, home-based business options and small business initiatives for disabled veterans. Find a consultant via the JAN on Demand for Self-Employment on this page. Here you will also find resources to help develop a small business. Small Business Administration (SBA) — Federal agency that provides assistance to current and prospective small business owners. SCORE Small Business Mentors — Seasoned business professionals help entrepreneurs start businesses, grow companies, and create jobs in local communities. Find a SCORE location near you. Self-Employment: What to Know to Be Your Own Boss — Information from the Bureau of Labor Statistics on self-employment. START-UP — ODEP initiated START-UP, a three-year grant project, in 2007 to identify policies and practices then in place that either made it difficult for individuals with disabilities to become self-employed or supported them in becoming self-employed. As part of the initiative, three states (Alaska, Florida, and New York) were awarded grants to pilot new innovative models for assisting individuals with disabilities to start businesses. A fourth grant established a national technical assistance center, Self-Employment Technical Assistance, Resources, & Training (START-UP/USA), to provide information and guidance about promoting self-employment for disabilities to the state grantees, as well as serving as a national resource for individuals and agencies wanting to pursue self-employment goals for people with disabilities. Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs) — SBDC advisors provide aspiring and current small business owners a variety of free business consulting and low-cost training services. How to Write a Business Plan — Online training course from the Small Business Administration explains the importance of business planning, defines and describes the components of a business plan, and provides access to sample plans and resources that can help you develop a plan for your business. USA.gov Start Your Own Business — Resources to help you start your own business, including information on programs to help military veterans and minorities become entrepreneurs.

pages.title: CVM Offices | FDA
pages.description: CVM is responsible for assuring that animal drugs and medicated feeds are safe and effective and that food from treated animals is safe to eat.
pages.text: CVM Offices | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home About FDA FDA Organization Center for Veterinary Medicine CVM Offices Center for Veterinary Medicine In this section Español The mission of FDA’s Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM) is to protect human and animal health throughout the United States. Accomplishing such a broad and varied mission takes many people working in many roles across the seven offices that make up CVM. Each office has specific responsibilities, including: Office of the Director Overseeing and directing our general activities. Coordinating and establishing policies to support our mission. Educating pet owners, animal producers, veterinarians, and the animal health industry about the products we regulate. Office of New Animal Product Evaluation Managing the approval process for new animal products, including intentional genomic alterations in animals and cell- and tissue-based products for animals. Ensuring new animal products are safe and effective, properly made, and adequately labeled and packaged. Ensuring that when food-producing animals, such as cattle and chickens, are treated with animal products, food made from those animals, such as meat, milk, and eggs, are safe for people to eat. Office of Generic Animal Drugs Managing the approval process for generic animal drugs. Ensuring generic animal drugs are bioequivalent to the reference-listed new animal drug product (RLNAD), properly made, and adequately labeled and packaged. Ensuring that when food-producing animals are treated with generic animal drugs, food made from those animals are safe for people to eat. Office of Minor Use and Minor Species Working to make more animal drugs legally available for minor species, such as ferrets and fish, and for minor uses (uses that are infrequent and limited) in a major species, such as horses and dogs. Office of Management Providing direction of our administrative programs, including budget planning and execution, human resources, information technology, and training and talent development. Overseeing our safety, security, and facility services. Office of Surveillance and Compliance Monitoring animal products to make sure that the companies marketing them are following the law. When companies that market animal products violate the law, taking necessary action to make them comply, such as issuing warning letters and withdrawing unsafe products from the market. Office of Applied Science Using science to develop and support our policies and regulatory decisions about animal food and drugs. Developing and applying alternative methods to ensure animal drugs are safe and effective. We embrace the important concept of One Health in every aspect of our work—we recognize that the health of people, animals, and the environment is intertwined. A One Health approach involves experts in human health, animal health, and the environmental sciences working together to address health and environmental problems in the U.S and around the world. For example, medical advances in understanding and treating a disease in one species, such as heart disease in people, may be applied to other species, while a change in the environment can affect all living things, from people to animals to plants. We are a small center within FDA, yet our work touches the lives of people and animals in the U.S. every day. Content current as of: 11/25/2024 Feedback Back to Top

Please check with your State for the specific permitting rules that apply in that State. Appendix A of Part 70 – This appendix provides information on the approval status of State and Local operating Permit Programs. 40 CFR Part 71 – This is the rule we (EPA) use when we are the Title V permitting authority; this occurs where a State or local Title V permitting program does not exist, such as in Indian County. Recent Regulatory Actions Related to Title V Clarifying the Scope of “Applicable Requirements” Under State Operating Permit Programs and the Federal Operating Permit Program: Final Rule September 22, 2026 - EPA issued a final rule to clarify the agency’s existing policies concerning when and whether Clean Air Act (CAA) program “applicable requirements” should be reviewed, modified, and/or implemented through the CAA’s title V operating permits program. The final action clarifies: That in most situations, requirements under the New Source Review (NSR) preconstruction permitting program cannot be reviewed using the agency’s unique title V oversight authorities. That most preconstruction permitting decisions in NSR permits will not be subject to later second-guessing through the CAA title V permitting process. This provides much needed certainty for permitting authorities and regulated entities. That CAA requirements related to the operator’s general duty to prevent accidental releases of hazardous substances are not “applicable requirements” for title V purposes. EPA’s final rule will improve permitting efficiency, reduce uncertainty regarding permit review processes, and provide greater consistency for title V permits nationwide, while maintaining statutory requirements on NSR permitting decisions. Given that the title V program has generally not been used to impose substantive emissions controls, EPA does not expect this rulemaking to affect emissions. Final Rule: Clarifying the Scope of “Applicable Requirements” Under State Operating Permit Programs and the Federal Operating Permit Program Rescission of Title V Emergency Affirmative Defense Rule September 24, 2026 - Final Rule: Rescission of Title V Emergency Affirmative Defense Rule; Corrections May 28, 2026 - In accordance with a court ordered mandate, EPA has rescinded a Biden EPA 2023 final rule that removed emergency-related affirmative defense provisions from federal regulations governing title V operating permit programs (the “Affirmative Defense Rule”). EPA is taking this final action in response to the September 5, 2025, decision of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit in SSM Litigation Group v. EPA , which reversed the 2023 Affirmative Defense Rule. This rescission is necessary to carry out the court’s mandate and restore EPA regulations to how they existed before the 2023 Affirmative Defense Rule. This action provides regulated industry a clear pathway to demonstrate that excess emissions were unavoidable and properly managed, while encouraging them to invest in prevention, maintenance, and rapid response systems. EPA is reinforcing the principle that penalties should distinguish between liability for noncompliance, and situations where noncompliance occurs as a result of circumstances beyond a facility’s control. pages.text: 世界厕所日 - 背景信息 | 联合国 Skip to main content 联合国儿童基金会 / Karel Prinsloo 厕所为何如此重要？ 卫生设施是一项人权。 每个人都应该能够使用安全、卫生、私密的厕所，并连接到安全管理的卫生系统以妥善处理废物。 当厕所数量不够、损坏或破损时，污染就会蔓延，并引发致命疾病。 特别是对于妇女和女童而言，缺乏安全管理的卫生设施、供水和个人卫生服务使她们更容易受到虐待和攻击并且健康不佳，影响她们有尊严地学习、工作和生活的能力。 厕所不仅是方便之所，它还是一项人权，是公共卫生、性别平等和气候韧性的基石。 进加快和加大行动力度，让更多的人用上安全的厕所，这将推进可持续发展、人权与和平方面取得成果。 什么是世界厕所日？ 世界厕所日由世界厕所组织于2001年首次发起。自2013年起，世界厕所日成为联合国的年度纪念日。 每年11月19日是世界厕所日，旨在强调厕所的重要性，并提高对无法获得安全卫生设施人群的认识。 世界厕所日的核心是倡导采取行动应对全球卫生危机，并实现 可持续发展目标6：到2030年为所有人提供水和卫生设施。 世界厕所日会举行哪些活动？ 世界厕所日是一次全球行动号召。在 联合国水机制 的协调下，本次活动通过 #世界厕所日# 标签的推广，涵盖世界各地的线上参与和现场活动。 个人、学校、政府、企业和组织通过提高认识、分享经历以及举办各种活动参与其中，这些活动包括社区清洁、学校课程、公众讲座和政策对话等。 活动目的是强调迫切需要在任何地方让每个人都可以用上安全、方便的厕所，并激励人们采取具体行动，缩小卫生设施差距。 谁在推动2026年世界厕所日？ 世界厕所日由联合国水机制、联合国机构间水和卫生设施协调机制负责协调。每年，在一个专门专家组的支持下，一个或多个联合国水机制成员及合作伙伴牵头这项活动。 所有参与世界厕所日的实体 国际私人水域运营商联合会 经济实惠水资源和卫生技术中心 联合国粮食及农业组织（粮农组织） 全球水伙伴关系 享有水的人权组织 国际水利与环境工程学院代尔夫特水教育研究所 国际水文科学协会 国际劳工组织（劳工组织） 国际移民组织（移民组织） 国际水和卫生中心 国际水务管理研究所 联合国人权事务高级专员办事处（人权高专办） 环境卫生和个人卫生基金 全民环境卫生和供水 厕所委员会联盟 联合国全球契约首席执行官节水任务（联合国全球契约） 欧洲经济委员会（欧洲经委会） 联合国开发计划署（开发署） 妇女署 水援助组织 Water.org 世界厕所组织 世界自然基金会

pages.text: Arizona Strip District Office | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Arizona Strip District Office and Public Lands Information Center The Arizona Strip District is the Bureau of Land Management’s northernmost district in Arizona, encompassing more than 2.7 million acres of remote public lands located north of the Grand Canyon and south of the Utah state line. The closest town to the east of the district is Page, Arizona, and the closest town to the west is Mesquite, Nevada. The public lands information center and district office are located in St. George, Utah, the largest nearby city. As one of the most rugged and least developed regions in the lower 48 states, the Arizona Strip region requires careful planning and preparation. Visitors should be ready for remote backcountry travel on unimproved roads, limited services, and potentially extreme weather conditions. The Arizona Strip District is managed for conservation, recreation, grazing, cultural resource protection, and a variety of multiple‑use activities. The district includes four management units: the Arizona Strip Field Office , Vermilion Cliffs National Monument, Grand Canyon–Parashant National Monument jointly managed under a service first agreement with the National Park Service, and the Baaj Nwaavjo I'tah Kukveni – Ancestral Footprints of the Grand Canyon National Monument jointly managed with the U.S. Forest Service. Thank you for your patience! Please visit us at our BLM/NPS centralized location at 4001 East Aviator Drive (just east of the St. George Municipal Airport) to obtain maps, resource permits, and recreation information for the BLM Arizona Strip District, BLM St. George Field Office, Vermilion Cliffs National Monument, BLM/NPS Grand Canyon-Parashant National Monument and Baaj Nwaavjo I’tah Kukveni National Monument. Public Room Visit our public room to find maps, brochures, and information about BLM Arizona programs. Fire Restrictions Find the latest fire restrictions for the Arizona Strip District. Lotteries and Permits We limit the number of visitors to certain areas to protect the landscape and wildlife and to ensure a quality experience. Arizona Strip Field Office The BLM Arizona Strip Field Office is more than 1,145, 000 acres and is managed for recreation, grazing, and a variety of multiple‑use activities. Visitors can enjoy historic sites like the Old Spanish National Historic Trail and the Mt.Trumbull Schoolhouse . Visit the Arizona Strip Field Office Grand Canyon-Parashant National Monument The Grand Canyon-Parashant National Monument is under joint management by the BLM and National Park Service through a service first agreement. Covering approximately one million acres of remote public lands, this monument is a scientific treasure, containing many of the same values that have long been protected in Grand Canyon National Park. Visit the Grand Canyon-Parashant National Monument Vermilion Cliffs National Monument This remote, rugged monument is approximately 279,000 acres and is a geologic treasure with some of the most spectacular trails and views in the world. The monument contains many diverse landscapes, including the Paria Plateau, Vermilion Cliffs, Coyote Buttes, and Paria Canyon. The monument borders Kaibab National Forest to the west and Glen Canyon National Recreation Area to the east. pages.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.
pages.text: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says 4 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Dearbail Jordan , Business reporter and Lily Jamali , North America Technology correspondent, Palo Alto, CA Reuters The Nvidia scandal has sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley as well as the political establishment Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says. Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees. Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business. Megaspeed said it was aware of reports "containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence". It added that it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation". But while Alice Huang is said to have stepped down from her role as Megaspeed director near the end of 2023, there were suspicions that she was still heavily involved in the firm's operations, according to Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS C4ADS said that Huang was still "practically in control" of Megaspeed even after she had handed over the reins of the firm. Huang - who is of no relation to Nvidia's former boss - had been investigated by Singapore authorities in February 2025 as part of the country's probe into Megaspeed and other companies. Also on Sunday, US Congressman John Moolenaar said that Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the Select Committee on China, which he chairs, as well as the House Foreign Affairs and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. The committee heads had threatened to issue subpoenas to Huang if he did not comply with their requests to testify. Moolenaar told CBS, BBC's US partner, that none were ultimately issued. Huang's testimony is expected to take place behind close doors, with the dates still being finalised. "That's going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed, and to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy and may have had an influence on some of our policies with respect to AI and export controls," the congressman told the Face The Nation programme. Separately, a group of tech leaders, including Space X's Elon Musk, have been trying to rally support to have Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. A representative for Huang declined to comment on a report in the Financial Times Sunday suggesting that he was discussing a comeback to the firm he co-founded. The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated to lead Nvidia is very low while the company's internal investigations are ongoing. The move would also face scrutiny from Washington, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling for Nvidia to hire its next CEO from outside the company. On Friday, Bessent had blamed fellow Trump cabinet colleague Howard Lutnick's commerce department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-end chips. Bessent told CNBC that several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months... but Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process".
