pages.title: AFFO Consortia | Department of Energy Lock
pages.description: The Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office (AFFO), which brings together legacy efforts under the former Bioenergy Technologies Office and Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Technologies Office, provides funding for bioenergy industry and hydrogen and full cell technologies lab-led consortia.
pages.text: AFFO Consortia | Department of Energy Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. AFFO Consortia The Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office (AFFO), which brings together legacy efforts under the former Bioenergy Technologies Office and Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Technologies Office, provides funding for bioenergy industry and hydrogen and full cell technologies lab-led consortia. Each consortium utilizes the capabilities of the DOE National Laboratory system to overcome the challenges of researching and developing competitive, cost-effective, and scalable fuels and products made from biomass. The office may add innovative projects to the consortia through future lab calls and funding opportunities, subject to appropriations. Below are brief descriptions and links to each AFFO-funded consortium: AGILE BIOFOUNDRY Agile Biofoundry works to accelerate and streamline the biomanufacturing pipeline through the use of synthetic biology tools, processes for predictable scale-up, machine learning, and the use of non-model host organisms by establishing a robust set of biomanufacturing principles. Learn more at Agile Biofoundry . Download the Agile BioFoundry flyer . ALGAE TECHNOLOGY EDUCATIONAL CONSORTIUM The Algae Foundation launched the Algae Technology Educational Consortium (ATEC) project, recognizing algal production will provide a source of biomass for bio-based products, feed, fuel and foods creating high-quality jobs for an educated workforce. A partnership between academic institutions, national research laboratories, and industry leaders, the consortium’s goal is to develop novel educational programs to strengthen industry workforce capabilities, by focusing on the skills needed to support the commercialization of algal products. Through algal education, students learn practical applications of farming and biotechnology developing the skills for the next generation of algal-based jobs. Learn more at Algae Technology Educational Consortium . BIOPROCESSING SEPARATIONS CONSORTIUM The Bioprocessing Separations Consortium develops cost-effective, high-performing separations technologies that are coordinated with challenges relevant to industry in order to facilitate adoption. This consortium addresses separations challenges such as impurities in intermediates impeding downstream biological and chemical catalysts, the need for low-cost purification technologies, and recovery and conversion of dilute carbon. Learn more at Bioprocessing Separations Consortium . BIO-OPTIMIZED TECHNOLOGIES TO KEEP THERMOPLASTICS OUT OF LANDFILLS AND THE ENVIRONMENT Supported by both AFFO and the Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Office, Bio-Optimized Technologies to keep Thermoplastics out of Landfills and the Environment (BOTTLE™) is a multi-organization consortium focused on developing new chemical upcycling strategies for today's plastics and creating tomorrow's plastics to be recyclable by design. BOTTLE’s vision is to deliver selective, scalable technologies to enable cost-effective recycling, upcycling, and increased energy efficiency. Learn more at BOTTLE . CO2 REDUCTION AND UPGRADING FOR E-FUELS CONSORTIUM (CO2RUe) The CO2RUe Consortium develops and derisks advanced technologies that use electricity to convert carbon dioxide (CO2) into e-fuels and commodity chemicals. Millions of tons of CO2 are emitted annually from biorefineries and industrial sites across the United States. CO2RUe is working toward using electricity to convert waste CO2 into "e-fuels"—a shorthand for electrofuels, which have dramatically lower land, water, and emissions footprints. Learn more at CO2 Reduction and Upgrading for E-Fuels Consortium . CHEMICAL CATALYSIS FOR BIOENERGY (ChemCatBio) ChemCatBio addresses challenges

pages.title: Ofrecimiento de transacción | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Un ofrecimiento de transacción le permite saldar su deuda tributaria por menos de la cantidad total que debe.
pages.text: Ofrecimiento de transacción | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Ofrecimiento de transacción English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Pagar Cuenta bancaria (Pago directo) Tarjeta de crédito o débito Su Cuenta en línea Pago de impuestos de negocio (EFTPS) Plan de pagos Ayuda para la deuda tributaria Multas Intereses Retención de impuestos Pagos electrónicos extranjeros Cargos administrativos Un ofrecimiento de transacción ( OIC , por sus siglas en inglés) puede permitirle saldar su deuda tributaria por menos de la cantidad total que debe si no puede pagar en su totalidad o hacerlo le causaría dificultades financieras. Consideramos sus ingresos, gastos y valor neto de los bienes. Por lo general, no aceptaremos un ofrecimiento si puede pagar su deuda tributaria en su totalidad a través de un plan de pago y/o valor neto de los bienes. Antes de aplicar, explore otras opciones de pago para determinar qué opción es la adecuada para usted. Cómo solicitar una OIC Compruebe su elegibilidad Use la Herramienta pre-calificadora del ofrecimiento de transacción (en inglés) para verificar su elegibilidad y preparar un ofrecimiento preliminar. Para ser elegible, tiene que: Presentar todas las declaraciones de impuestos requeridas Realizar los pagos de impuestos estimados requeridos No estar en un proceso abierto de quiebra Si es empleador, realizar depósitos de impuestos federales requeridos para el trimestre actual y los dos últimos trimestres Envíe su solicitud Puede enviar su solicitud para un OIC en su cuenta para personas físicas. Inicie sesión o cree una cuenta para comenzar. Los negocios y las personas físicas sin una cuenta pueden descargar los formularios y las instrucciones paso a paso en el Formulario 656-B (sp), Folleto de Información sobre el Formulario 656 Ofrecimiento de transacción PDF . Los contribuyentes de negocios pueden realizar pagos de un OIC a través de su cuenta de impuestos de negocios o pagos por correo con sus formularios de un OIC . Cada solicitud de OIC requiere una cuota de solicitud de $205 y un primer pago a menos que cumpla con las calificaciones de bajos ingresos. Realice el primer pago Su pago inicial depende de su ofrecimiento y la opción de pago que escoja. Puede elegir un pago de suma global o pagos periódicos. Si cumple con los requisitos de bajos ingresos, no tiene que pagar la cuota de solicitud, el pago inicial o los pagos periódicos mientras revisamos su ofrecimiento. Solo las personas físicas califican para la consideración de la calificación de bajos ingresos. Suma global Pague el 20% del monto de su ofrecimiento al presentar la solicitud. Si se acepta, pague el saldo restante en cinco o menos pagos. Pago periódico Realice el pago inicial cuando presente la solicitud y continúe realizando pagos periódicos mientras consideramos su ofrecimiento. Si se acepta, continúe realizando pagos hasta que el monto del ofrecimiento se pague en su totalidad. Si presenta una solicitud y no es elegible, le devolveremos su solicitud y la cuota de solicitud. Su suma global o pago(s) periódico(es) se aplicarán a su deuda tributaria. Después de presentar su solicitud Si confirmamos su elegibilidad y procesamos su solicitud: Recibirá una notificación Es posible que le solicitemos información adicional para completar nuestra investigación Suspendemos la mayoría de las actividades de cobro Extendemos el periodo de cobro Es posible que presentemos un aviso de gravamen tributario federal Usted tiene que continuar realizando todos los pagos requeridos del OIC durante el proceso de solicitud. No es necesario realizar pagos de un plan de pagos existente para el mismo saldo adeudado. Su solicitud será aprobada automáticamente si no la aceptamos o rechazamos dentro de dos años. Este periodo de dos años comienza cuando recibimos su solicitud y no incluye el tiempo transcurrido durante una apelación. pages.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself.
pages.text: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Michelle Fleury New York business correspondent How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security? How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang? The answer is very. The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits. But that relationship now looks rather more complicated. Getty Images The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president. US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it? That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections. A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny. Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist. On Friday, Bessent pointed the finger at Commerce for not blacklisting the company, telling CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months". "But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added. There have also been questions about why an investi

pages.text: Sajeevini sivajothy's Diary | Geospatial Action Against Dengue: Empowering Communities Through Open Mapping and Waste Hotspot Identification in Eravur Pattu, Sri Lanka | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close Sajeevini sivajothy's Diary Geospatial Action Against Dengue: Empowering Communities Through Open Mapping and Waste Hotspot Identification in Eravur Pattu, Sri Lanka Posted by Sajeevini sivajothy on 11 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 13 November 2026. Turning Geospatial Knowledge into Community Action Maps are more than representations of places. They help us understand our surroundings, identify challenges and make informed decisions that can improve people’s lives. With this belief, I had the opportunity to organise and facilitate the Open Mapping Guru Workshop and Field Mapping Programme 2026, held on 5th–6th October 2026 at the Faculty of Arts and Culture, Eastern University of Sri Lanka. Under the theme “Geospatial Action Against Dengue: Mapping Waste Hotspots and Stagnant Water in Eravur Pattu,” this initiative brought together university students, academic staff and the Open Mapping community to explore how geospatial technologies can contribute to environmental monitoring and public health awareness. Supported and sponsored by Open Mapping Hub - Asia-Pacific and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT), the programme was designed to go beyond traditional classroom learning. It provided students with an opportunity to learn, explore, collect real-world geographical information and understand how their mapping contributions could support their surrounding communities. As the Resource Person and Organiser, my main objective was to connect geospatial knowledge with practical community needs and encourage students to become active contributors to the global Open Mapping community. Day 01: Taking Open Mapping Beyond the Classroom. The first day focused on practical field mapping and community-based data collection, with about 21 university students participating. The programme commenced at the Department of Geography, where students were divided into five groups and assigned different mapping areas surrounding the university and nearby communities. Before heading into the field, I introduced the participants to several mobile mapping applications and explained how these tools could be used to collect accurate, location-based information. The applications included ChatMap for capturing geotagged photographs and location-based field information, EveryDoor for contributing to OpenStreetMap through field-based data collection, and Organic Maps for navigation and exploring geographical locations, Mapillary for collecting and exploring street-level imagery, and Field Papers for preparing field maps and supporting systematic data collection. Following the technical introduction, the student groups began their field activities, focusing on identifying and documenting waste accumulation sites that could create potential mosquito breeding environments. Although the original theme included identifying both waste hotspots and stagnant water locations, the severe drought conditions experienced in Batticaloa District during this period limited the availability of stagnant water observations. Therefore, the students concentrated mainly on identifying waste accumulation locations and their surrounding environmental conditions. One of the most valuable tools during this activity was ChatMap. It enabled students to capture actual field photographs together with geographical coordinates, allowing us to build a location-based dataset supported by visual evidence. Throughout the fieldwork, I coordinated the groups, monitored their progress and provided technical guidance through a dedicated WhatsApp group. Students returned to the university in the afternoon, where we discussed their field experiences, observations, challenges and feedback. Secondary National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2) and Sulfur Dioxide (SO2) and Particulate Matter (PM) Secondary National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2) and Sulfur Dioxide (SO2) and Particulate Matter (PM) Basic Information Federal Register Citations 89 FR 105692 89 FR 26620 77 FR 20218 76 FR 46084 Docket Numbers EPA-HQ-OAR-2014-0128 On this page: Rule Summary Rule History Additional Resources Rule Summary On December 10, 2024, the Environmental Protection Agency revised an air quality standard to better protect public welfare against adverse effects caused by criteria air pollutants – including ecological effects such as damage to aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. This action revises the secondary National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) for oxides of sulfur ( SO X ) and retains the existing secondary standards for oxides of nitrogen (N oxides) and particulate matter (PM), aligning standards with the best-available science and ensuring air pollution concentrations remain at historically low levels. The revised standard will take effect 30 days after EPA’s decision is published in the Federal Register. pages.text: Cómo entender un gravamen por impuestos federales | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Cómo entender un gravamen por impuestos federales English Español 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Presentar Individuos Negocios y trabajadores por cuenta propia Cuenta tributaria de negocios Números de identificación del empleador Impuestos del negocio Estructuras de negocio Cómo operar un negocio Trabajo por cuenta propia Pequeños negocios Industrias/Profesiones (en inglés) Eventos de los pequeños negocios (en inglés) Aprendizaje en línea (en inglés) Negocios grandes Organizaciones caritativas y sin fines de lucro Contribuyentes internacionales Enlaces gubernamentales (en inglés) Gobiernos federales, estatales y locales (en inglés) Gobiernos tribales indígenas (en inglés) Bonos exentos de impuestos (en inglés) Números de identificación del contribuyente (TIN) Un gravamen por impuestos federales es el dominio legal que tiene el gobierno sobre sus bienes cuando usted es negligente o no paga su deuda tributaria. Este gravamen protege el interés del gobierno federal contra sus bienes, incluyendo bienes raíces, propiedad personal y bienes financieros. Un gravamen por impuestos federales podrá imponerse cuando: El IRS: Registre su saldo adeudado (determine su obligación tributaria); Le envíe una factura, explicándole cuánto adeuda (Aviso y Demanda de Pago); y Usted: No pague o rehúse pagar la deuda completa a tiempo. El IRS presenta un documento público, el Aviso de Gravamen por Impuestos Federales para informar a los acreedores que el gobierno tiene derecho legal sobre su propiedad. Si desea más información, consulte la Publicación 594 (SP), El Proceso de Cobro del IRS PDF . Cómo se elimina un gravamen Cómo un gravamen le afecta Evite un gravamen Gravamen vs. embargo Recursos de ayuda Cómo se elimina un gravamen Pagar su deuda tributaria - en su totalidad - es la mejor manera de eliminar un gravamen por impuestos federales. El IRS emite una liberación del gravamen por impuestos federales dentro de 30 días de usted satisfacer la deuda tributaria. Al cumplir ciertos requisitos a favor tanto del contribuyente como del gobierno, se hacen disponibles otras opciones para reducir el impacto de un gravamen. Exoneración de propiedad Una “exoneración” libera un gravamen de una propiedad específica. Hay varias disposiciones del Código de Impuestos Internos que determinan la elegibilidad. Si desea más información vea la Publicación 783, Instrucciones para solicitar un certificado de exoneración de gravamen por impuestos federales (en inglés) PDF . Subordinación de gravamen La “subordinación” no elimina el gravamen, pero permite a otros acreedores anteponerse al IRS, lo cual puede facilitar el obtener un préstamo o hipoteca. Para determinar si es elegible para esta opción, consulte la Publicación 784, Cómo solicitar un certificado de subordinación de gravamen por impuestos federales (en inglés) PDF . Retiro de gravamen Un “retiro” elimina el aviso público por gravamen de impuestos federales y asegura que el IRS no está en contienda con otros acreedores sobre su propiedad. Sin embargo, usted todavía es responsable de pagar el saldo adeudado. Si desea averiguar su elegibilidad, consulte el Formulario 12277, Solicitud del retiro del Formulario 668(Y), Aviso de un gravamen de impuestos federales (sección 6323(j) del Código de Impuestos Internos) (en inglés) PDF . Hay dos opciones adicionales para el retiro, disponibles como resultado de la iniciativa del Comisionado del 2011, nombrada Fresh Start (Nuevo comienzo). Una opción puede permitir el retiro del aviso de gravamen por impuestos federales, después de la liberación del mismo. Los requisitos generales incluyen: Haber liquidado su responsabilidad tributaria, y haberse liberado el gravamen; y además: Tener tres años corridos de cumplir en presentar toda declaración del impuesto personal, toda declaración del impuesto del negocio, y toda declaración informativa; Estar al día con

pages.description: Earlier this month, volunteers and soldiers from Fort Huachuca served on public lands at a National Public Lands Day project hosted by the Friends of the San Pedro River.

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM Partners and Volunteers Enhance Desert Garden at San Pedro Riparian National Conservation Area Oct 30, 2026 Volunteers pose after completing National Public Lands Day improvements at the San Pedro House xeriscape garden. (Photo courtesy Friends of the San Pedro River) Volunteers, community organizations and servicemembers play an important role in helping care for America's public lands. Supporting those connections is a key goal of the Bureau of Land Management (BLM)'s All Americans Outside initiative , which promotes opportunities for people to explore, learn, serve and work on public lands. Earlier this month, those goals came together at the San Pedro Riparian National Conservation Area during a National Public Lands Day project hosted by the Friends of the San Pedro River . During this event, volunteers and soldiers from Fort Huachuca’s 111th Military Intelligence Brigade, Company B took advantage of mild temperatures and cloud cover to support a work project at the San Pedro House . The workers improved the xeriscape garden outside the San Pedro House. They removed several stumps, placed landscape gravel, removed Bermuda grass and other weedy species, raked leaves, and planted new desert plants. San Pedro House is the primary visitor contact station at the San Pedro Riparian National Conservation Area. In addition to the xeriscape garden, the area includes a volunteer-run bookstore and gift shop, restrooms, informational signage, and a picnic area. Volunteers transplant a yucca outside the San Pedro House. (Photo courtesy Friends of the San Pedro River) “Service projects like this are a perfect way to take ownership as a steward of public lands,” said Tucson Assistant Field Manager Michael Dixon. “Our volunteers provide real benefits to the scenery, natural resources, and visitor enjoyment of these special places.” After the work was completed, everyone gathered for a picnic of burgers, homemade dishes, fruit, and dessert. “In the tradition of military coin exchange, we handed out Friends of the San Pedro River hat pins to the soldiers and National Public Lands Day t-shirts for the volunteers,” said Joanne Roberts, president of the Friends of the San Pedro River. Volunteers enjoy a picnic after finishing the site improvement work. (Photo courtesy Friends of the San Pedro River) Since 2013, the BLM has been a partner in the Sentinel Landscapes program with Fort Huachuca. The BLM works with the military and other federal, state, and local partners to promote compatible land uses that support the operations and mission of the fort. Soldiers at the fort have partnered with the Friends of the San Pedro River for more than 20 years supporting the xeriscape garden and other large projects within the national conservation area. Company B has adopted two xeriscape “pods” in the garden. They schedule a work morning each month and participate in two major work days each year. Volunteers remove a stump near the San Pedro House. (Photo courtesy Friends of the San Pedro River) In addition to volunteer work days, the Friends of the San Pedro River manages two visitor contact stations—San Pedro House and Fairbank School House —and hosts guided walks and other educational programs at the San Pedro Riparian National Conservation Area. Groups like the Friends of the San Pedro River support the BLM’s mission to manage these special areas for the benefit of current and future generations. pages.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
pages.text: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kali Hays , Technology reporter and Lily Jamali , North America Technology correspondent How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security? Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. EPA/Shutterstock Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? pages.title: A new species offers a clue to the boom of giant dinosaurs | National Geographic
pages.description: Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis may be the largest dinosaur ever found in Southeast Asia. Paleontologists estimate this behemoth weighed 30 tons and measured over 88 feet long.
pages.text: A new species offers a clue to the boom of giant dinosaurs | National Geographic SCIENCE A new species offers a clue to the boom of giant dinosaurs Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis may be the largest dinosaur ever found in Southeast Asia. Paleontologists estimate this behemoth weighed 30 tons and measured over 88 feet long. The recent discovery of Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis , shown in this illustration, in Thailand adds support to the idea that warm, open, and relatively dry habitats created ideal conditions for the evolution of giant sauropods. DinoThaiThai By Riley Black Published May 14, 2026 Titans once towered over Thailand. A research team led by National Geographic Explorer Sita Manitkoon has discovered a new long-necked dinosaur they estimate was over 88 feet long and weighed nearly 30 tons. “Initial measurements of the bones excavated suggested that this could be the largest dinosaur ever found in Southeast Asia,” says Manitkoon, a paleontologist at Mahasarakham University in Thailand. The telltale bones were uncovered in 2016 by a local man named Thanom Luangnan in Chaiyaphum Province, northeastern Thailand. “He observed what he described as strange-looking rocks on the banks of a public pond,” says Manitkoon. Luangnan reported the findings to the country’s Department of Mineral Resources. The strange rocks, it turned out, were dinosaur bones, and when Manitkoon came upon them, he knew the creature must have been enormous. ( How to bring a 75-foot-long dinosaur back to life ) The researchers named the new species Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis after where it was found, and the giant serpent-like Naga of Southeast Asian folklore. The discovery, which was announced Thursday in the journal Scientific Reports , provides insight into how changes in ancient climate and vegetation opened the doors for gigantic dinosaurs to develop. “This is the most complete sauropod specimen discovered from the Khok Kruat Formation,” says Pedro Mocho , a paleontologist at the Universidade de Lisboa in Portugal, who was not involved in the study. Until now, Mocho says, the big dinosaurs in Thailand were known only from bits and pieces of skeletons. The new find is substantially more complete, revealing a titanic dinosaur never seen in the country before. Sita Manitkoon oversaw the recovery of Nagatitan , the largest dinosaur ever discovered in Thailand. Tanintorn Ketburana Colossal Cretaceous sauropods Nagatitan left behind a smattering of vertebrae, ribs, hip bones, and limb bones entombed in 113-million-year-old rock. Its right forelimb is longer than that of other, recently uncovered giant sauropods such as Patagotitan and Dreadnoughtus , though the dinosaur itself likely was not as big as those heavy hitters, which weighed an estimated 60 and 50 tons respectively. The largest dinosaurs of all time were not each other’s closest relatives. Sauropod dinosaurs evolved their giant body sizes more than 30 times over the course of more than a hundred million years on at least six landmasses. Nagatitan became a giant independently of other huge dinosaurs from other periods and places, but its relationships and habitat suggest it lived at the beginning of a time conducive to enormous dinosaurs. Nagatitan belonged to a group called the somphospondyli . These dinosaurs tend to have long forelimbs compared to other sauropods, as well as a wide stance, says Paul Upchurch, a paleontologist at the University College London and a coauthor of the study. The other differences would have been difficult to spot on the living animal, but these subtle cues identify the Nagatitans as a group of immense dinosaurs that spread far and wide some 110 to 120 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous. Sita Manitkoon and the Thai Paleontology Youth Network recovered a dorsal rib (about six feet long) from the site and moved it to the Sirindhorn Dinosaur Museum. Final Reconsideration of the National Ambient Air Quality Standards for Particulate Matter (PM) On February 7, 2024, EPA strengthened the National Ambient Air Quality Standards for Particulate Matter (PM NAAQS) to protect millions of Americans from harmful and costly health impacts, such as heart attacks and premature death. ​Particle or soot pollution is one of the most dangerous forms of air pollution, and an extensive body of science links it to a range of serious and sometimes deadly illnesses. ​ EPA is setting the level of the primary (health-based) annual PM 2.5 standard at 9.0 micrograms per cubic meter to provide increased public health protection, consistent with the available health science. EPA is not changing the current: primary and secondary (welfare-based) 24-hour PM 2.5 standards, secondary annual PM 2.5 standard, and primary and secondary PM 10 standards. EPA is also revising the Air Quality Index to improve public communications about the risks from PM 2.5 exposures and making changes to the monitoring network to enhance protection of air quality in communities overburdened by air pollution. Let's Plan Your Adventure! This guide will give you some key tips, links, and tools to help you "Plan like a Ranger" for your national park adventure! Having a plan will help you avoid common mistakes that can affect your visit and even lead to injury. The Trip Planning Guide is meant for day or overnight trips to a park.If you are planning a multi-day trip, especially to backcountry areas, additional planning steps will be required and are beyond the scope of this guide. Continue reading to learn how you can get the most out of your visit to a park. On this page, you'll also be able to: Download the NPS Trip Planning Guide Fill out a Trip Plan Template Practice the Outdoor Emergency Plan View a list of the 10 Essentials . Know Before You Go “If you don’t know where you are going, you’ll end up someplace else.” -Yogi Berra Researching ahead of time gives you the opportunity to learn about the park and the environment(s) you’ll encounter during your adventure. You’ll have time to prepare and get the right gear/equipment needed for you and anyone that may be traveling with you. Keep reading to learn about what you should "Know Before You Go": Learn about the park Every park environment is unique and continuously changing with the seasons. Visit the park's website on NPS.gov or the NPS mobile app to become familiar with the places you will visit. Consider the following: Amenities - Does the park have drinking water, park shuttles, or stores where you can buy food and gear? Weather - What is the weather forecast for the duration of your trip? How will you prepare for it? Wildlife - What animals live in the park and how can you prepare for a chance encounter? Terrain - Are there uneven surfaces like unpaved trails or stairs you need to be aware of? Water - Are there currents or underwater hazards? Is the temperature of the water cold? Park Alerts - Are there closures, hazards, or other active alerts that may affect your visit? Find out what activities you can do at the park There is more than one way to experience the park. Find a complete list of activities on the park's website under the "Things to do" page under the Plan Your Visit page. Explore the pages of the activities that interest you. Find out if the park has Ranger-guided and Junior Ranger programs and consider participating in them. Know your limits Your experience in the park is yours to decide. Only you know your abilities and your comfort level. Assess the following about yourself: Skills - What outdoor skills do you have? Have you used them in a park like the one you're visiting? Experience - How often do you recreate outdoors? Have you recreated in a park like the one you're visiting? *Physical Fitness - Are you physically fit for your trip? Are there any activities that are beyond your abilities? *Medical Condition - Do you have a medical condition that could be worsened by the weather, altitude, or physical exertion? *Consult a physician if you have any questions on fitness levels, health conditions, or medications required. Pick the right activity for YOU There is more than one trail to hike, river to paddle, or mountain to climb. Pick an activity that you can safely enjoy during your visit. pages.text: Embargo | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Embargo English Español Más en Presentar Individuos Negocios y trabajadores por cuenta propia Cuenta tributaria de negocios Números de identificación del empleador Impuestos del negocio Estructuras de negocio Cómo operar un negocio Trabajo por cuenta propia Pequeños negocios Industrias/Profesiones (en inglés) Eventos de los pequeños negocios (en inglés) Aprendizaje en línea (en inglés) Negocios grandes Organizaciones caritativas y sin fines de lucro Contribuyentes internacionales Enlaces gubernamentales (en inglés) Gobiernos federales, estatales y locales (en inglés) Gobiernos tribales indígenas (en inglés) Bonos exentos de impuestos (en inglés) Números de identificación del contribuyente (TIN) Un embargo del IRS es la incautación legal de sus bienes para satisfacer una deuda tributaria. Pueden quitársele sueldos, dinero de su banco u otra cuenta financiera; o quitarle y vender su(s) vehículo(s), bienes inmuebles, y otra propiedad personal. Si recibe una factura del IRS con el título, Aviso Final de la Intención de Embargo y su Derecho a una Audiencia, ( Final Notice of Intent to Levy and Notice of Your Right to A Hearing en inglés), comuníquese con nosotros de inmediato. Si recibe un aviso del IRS avisándole de un embargo contra un empleado, un vendedor del que es cliente, un cliente suyo o un tercero , es importante que usted cumpla con los requisitos del embargo. Los enlaces a continuación le ayudarán a entender más de los embargos del IRS, y contestarán muchas de sus preguntas referentes a los embargos. ¿Qué es un embargo? Información básica acerca de los embargos del IRS. ¿Cómo evito un embargo? Explicamos lo que debe hacer para evitar un embargo del IRS. ¿Cómo consigo que me liberen el embargo? Si un embargo del IRS fue emitido a su empleador, banco o un tercero, aprenda las acciones que debe tomar para que liberen el embargo. ¿Qué pasa si el embargo me causa daño económico? Se puede liberar un embargo del IRS si le causa un daño económico inmediato, o si fue emitido por error. ¿Qué pasa si recibo un embargo contra uno de mis empleados, vendedor del quien soy cliente, un cliente mío o un tercero? Los empleadores, instituciones financieras y otros pueden recibir un embargo del IRS. Esta página le brinda información para ayudarle a cumplir con el embargo. Información sobre los embargos de sueldos Embargos contra los sueldos son continuos, y una parte de sus sueldos está exenta del embargo. Aquí puede aprender más acerca de los embargos de sueldos. Información sobre los embargos bancarios Si el IRS emite un embargo a su banco, los fondos en su cuenta están retenidos, y enviados al IRS al cabo de 21 días. Aquí puede aprender más acerca de los embargos bancarios y otros embargos parecidos. ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre un embargo y un gravamen? Un embargo es diferente a un gravamen. Aquí puede aprender acerca de las diferencias. ¿Qué pasa cuando me quitan mi propiedad, y cómo consigo que me la devuelvan? Aquí explicamos las acciones que el IRS toma después de quitarle su propiedad, y explicamos los pasos que debe tomar para que se libere la propiedad quitada. Venta de sus bienes Vea los requisitos del IRS para difundir avisos públicos de ventas pendientes. Redención de sus bienes inmuebles Obtenga información sobre las redenciones del IRS. Programas de embargos federales y estatales (en inglés) Si le han impuesto un embargo de sus pagos federales, el reembolso estatal de impuestos sobre los ingresos o el dividendo del Fondo Permanente de Alaska, esta sección le proveerá información sobre a quién llamar y qué hacer para solucionar el problema. Se les pide a los depositarios respetar las reglas de cumplimiento con los embargos (en inglés) El IRS pide a los depositarios (bancos, cooperativas de crédito, cooperativas de ahorros y préstamos y otras instituciones parecidas) revisar y entender sus responsabilidades relativas al trámite de los embargos. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Beyond the Badge: Protecting People and Public Lands Oct 26, 2026 Cole poses next to the Yuma Field Office entrance sign. (Photo by the Bureau of Land Management) A routine patrol across public lands near Yuma, Arizona, can change in an instant. Eric Cole knows that better than most. Cole, a supervisory law enforcement ranger with the Bureau of Land Management’s Yuma Field Office , was once called into the desert after another hiker found an unconscious woman and called 911. She had apparently suffered an allergic reaction to an insect bite and, by the time Cole reached her, also appeared to be suffering from heat-related illness. The terrain made getting a conventional ambulance directly to her impractical. Cole loaded her into his patrol vehicle, transported her across the backcountry and transferred her to an awaiting ambulance. “What stays with me is how quickly a situation in the desert can become life-threatening,” Cole said. “If the hiker hadn’t found her, or if she had remained out there much longer, I don’t know whether she would have survived.” For Cole, moments like that are part of a career spent being ready for whatever comes next. For BLM law enforcement rangers like him, being a first responder can mean bringing emergency response capabilities to places where traditional emergency vehicles may have difficulty reaching and where help can be many miles away. As the nation recognizes National First Responders Day on October 28, Cole’s career provides a look at the people behind one part of the BLM mission that visitors may rarely see: law enforcement rangers who patrol vast stretches of public land and may suddenly find themselves among the closest trained responders when someone needs help. Cole and his wife, Emily. (Photo courtesy of Eric Cole) Cole supervises BLM law enforcement rangers and Bureau of Reclamation rangers, but his supervisory responsibilities have not taken him out of the field. He still patrols public lands, makes visitor contacts, enforces federal laws and regulations, responds to emergencies and assists state, local and federal partners. Staying involved in day-to-day field operations matters to him. It keeps him connected to the work his rangers are doing and to the people who depend on them. “In an emergency, sometimes it simply comes down to which trained first responder is closest,” Cole said. “On millions of acres of public land, that person can very easily be a BLM ranger.” For Cole, responding to an emergency often begins with the challenge of simply reaching the person who needs help. The Yuma Field Office manages approximately 1.2 million acres of public land. Cell service can be limited or nonexistent. A call may begin with a distress beacon, an SOS activation from a satellite-capable GPS device or an incomplete 911 call that provides only limited information about where someone is located or how to reach them. Locating the person can become part of the emergency response itself. Years spent patrolling the backcountry have taught him the access routes, terrain and travel patterns across the area. Rangers may use vehicle tracks, footprints and other signs to help determine where someone has gone. “Sometimes getting to the emergency is as challenging as dealing with the emergency once you arrive,” Cole said. That reality shapes the way Cole prepares before he ever leaves for patrol. pages.title: In this Canadian province grown-ups can dig up dinosaur fossils | National Geographic
pages.description: Dinosaur stories are often written for children, with a cast of neon cartoon characters or animatronic models. But for adults who never outgrew their fossil fascination, the Canadian province of Alberta offers a chance to explore the truth behind the fiction, witness new discoveries and touch real dinosaur bones with your bare hands.
pages.text: In this Canadian province grown-ups can dig up dinosaur fossils | National Geographic TRAVEL In this Canadian province grown-ups can dig up dinosaur fossils Dinosaur stories are often written for children, with a cast of neon cartoon characters or animatronic models. But for adults who never outgrew their fossil fascination, the Canadian province of Alberta offers a chance to explore the truth behind the fiction, witness new discoveries and touch real dinosaur bones with your bare hands. Close to 50 dinosaur species have been found in Alberta, including Albertosaurus, a formidable predator related to Tyrannosaurus rex . Photograph by Bella Falk By Bella Falk Published October 10, 2025 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). This journey back in time starts in southern Alberta, two hours east of Calgary, where the ground cracks open to reveal a prehistoric archive dating back some 76 million years. Here, the rolling prairie collapses into wrinkled valleys carved out by ancient glaciers, banded in orange and grey layers like the pages of a medieval book and punctuated by bizarre ‘hoodoos’ — pillars of rock wearing jaunty sandstone hats. These are Canada’s Badlands — so-called because early French fur traders found them inhospitable and difficult to cross. In this treeless desert, only the hardiest vegetation survives: yellow buffalo bean flowers and tiny pincushion cacti sprout between gullies, and the aroma of sagebrush hangs on the breeze. This area may have been bad for the settlers, but it’s a goldmine for palaeontologists. The scientific motherlode lies in Dinosaur Provincial Park, a 29-square-mile UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the richest fossil locations on Earth. Visitors can explore a wealth of fossils while walking along the public trails of Dinosaur Provincial Park. Photograph by Bella Falk “These layers date to between 76 and 74 million years ago, during the late Cretaceous period,” reveals geologist Jessica Glombick, the park’s visitor experience team leader. “People have been searching for fossils here since the early 1900s, though of course the local Indigenous people knew about them long before that.” Close to 50 dinosaur species have been found here, including Albertosaurus, a formidable predator related to Tyrannosaurus rex , and Corythosaurus, a crested herbivore whose near-complete skeleton was unearthed after a park ranger spotted a bone poking out of a cliff. These were found alongside fossils of prehistoric turtle shells and crocodile teeth, revealing a thriving, complex ecosystem. Visitors can explore public trails and museum displays, but to see these ancient monsters up close, it’s best to join a guided hike into the park’s protected zone, where fossils lie strewn like shattered pottery, and you may come across a hadrosaur leg bone or ankylosaur rib lying on the ground like driftwood washed up on a beach. Walking around requires concentration: there are so many fragments, it’s almost impossible not to step on something. The best discoveries end up at the Royal Tyrrell Museum, two hours north in Drumheller. This small town of about 8,000 inhabitants is known as the ‘Dinosaur Capital of the World’, a tag worn with pride. A gold dinosaur roars on the sign, there are dinosaur models on every street and the world’s largest model dinosaur, an 86ft T-rex named Tyra, towers over the town centre. But these are mere warm-ups for the headline act. As one of the world’s top dinosaur museums, the Royal Tyrrell houses more than 170,000 specimens covering almost the entire history of evolution, from weird, 500-million-year-old worms found in the Canadian Rockies to a woolly mammoth and sabre-toothed cat from the last Ice Age. Equidad en la salud relacionada con el cáncer Para todos 19 de ago. del 2026 English (US) Qué necesita saber La División de Prevención y Control del Cáncer de los CDC ayuda a todos los estadounidenses a prevenir el cáncer, encontrarlo en las etapas iniciales y recibir tratamiento, de modo que todos tengan igualdad de oportunidades de estar lo más sanos posible. Grupos de población impactados Distintos grupos de personas tienen distintas tasas de ciertos tipos de cáncer y de muerte por su causa. Algunos grupos encuentran más difícil tomar decisiones saludables que ayudan a prevenir el cáncer, u obtener atención médica. El cancer y las personas afroamericanas El cancer y las personas indoamericanas El cancer y las personas hispanas o latinas Mejorando la equidad en la salud Equidad es cuando todos tienen igualdad de oportunidades de estar lo más sanos posible. El racismo es una grave amenaza a la salud pública. Algunas mediciones comunes describen qué tanto un grupo de personas está afectado por el cáncer. Lo que los CDC están haciendo Los CDC están fomentando la equidad en la salud a través de investigaciones, programas y colaboraciones. Sepa qué están haciendo los CDC. Los CDC otorgaron fondos a tres organizaciones para aprender cómo avanzar la equidad en la salud relacionada con el cáncer. pages.title: Celebrating 30 Years of California Condor Recovery at Vermilion Cliffs National Monument | Bureau of Land Management Lock
pages.description: BLM Arizona marked a milestone on National Public Lands Day with the 30th anniversary California Condor Release at the Condor Viewing Site in Vermilion Cliffs National Monument in northern Arizona.
pages.text: Celebrating 30 Years of California Condor Recovery at Vermilion Cliffs National Monument | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Celebrating 30 Years of California Condor Recovery at Vermilion Cliffs National Monument Oct 15, 2026 BLM and NPS staff and volunteers pose with Seymour Antelope at the Condor Viewing Site at Vermilion Cliffs National Monument. (BLM Photo) The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Arizona marked a milestone on National Public Lands Day with the 30th anniversary California Condor Release at the Condor Viewing Site in Vermilion Cliffs National Monument in northern Arizona. As part of the Department of the Interior (DOI)’s Freedom 250 initiative, hundreds of visitors, partners, volunteers, and agency staff gathered to witness four juvenile condors take flight into the wild. The event not only commemorates a yearly tradition but also highlights the enduring success of one of the nation’s largest and most collaborative wildlife recovery efforts. 30-year Recovery Partnership With only 22 individuals remaining in the late 1980s, the California condor was on the brink of extinction. The California Condor Recovery Program emerged as an intensive multi-agency and partner effort to save the species, including BLM Arizona and Utah, The Peregrine Fund, Arizona Game and Fish Department, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Park Service, Utah Division of Wildlife Resources, and tribal nations. Through captive breeding, habitat management, monitoring, and public outreach, condor numbers have steadily increased. Today, the population has grown to over 600 with 392 flying free across four release sites. But challenges remain. Outreach, education, and partnerships remain essential to reducing threats and ensuring long-term success. “Collaboration is key,” said Bob Bate, BLM Arizona Vermilion Cliffs Monument Manager. “As land managers, we work closely with The Peregrine Fund to ensure conditions support condor recovery operations. Outreach continues to grow every year and that growth shows just how interested people are in these birds and in their public lands.” Federal and partner organizations set up educational stations at the Condor Viewing Site. (BLM Photo) A Day of Celebration In the early hours of Saturday, Sept. 26, the BLM, The Peregrine Fund, and several federal and non-federal partners arrived on-site to set up educational tents, spotting scopes, activity and education stations, and technology for the livestream broadcast. By midmorning, hundreds of visitors — many of whom have come year after year — gathered to celebrate this year’s cohort of condors, bringing their binoculars, folding chairs, curiosity, and a passion for birding. As they waited for the pens to open, attendees were able to explore information booths, speak with condor biologists, and learn more about the complex breeding, monitoring, and tracking that support condor recovery. “When you become embroiled in condor recovery, it never leaves your blood,” said Tim Hauck, Peregrine Fund Program Director. “You are family for life, and you appreciate the birds and the people that make this happen.” Seymour Antelope poses with the Great American Expedition flag in celebration of Freedom 250. (BLM Photo) As an official BLM Freedom 250 event and in honor of the 30th anniversary of the Condor Release, this year’s festivities included a few extra features, such as the Great American Expedition , a traveling flag that visits public land sites across the nation to record stories of stewardship, heritage, and pride. Visitors were invited to take photos with the flag and share their own experience

pages.title: Inside Richard Leakey's discovery of an ancient human ancestor skull—the same his parents chased | National Geographic
pages.description: In a 1970 National Geographic feature, paleoanthropologist Richard Leakey—son of Louis and Mary Leakey—recounted his discovery of a nearly complete Australopithecus boisei skull (now Paranthropus boisei), the same species his parents had found a decade earlier.
pages.text: Inside Richard Leakey's discovery of an ancient human ancestor skull—the same his parents chased | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE FROM THE VAULT Inside Richard Leakey's discovery of an ancient human ancestor skull—the same his parents chased In a 1970 National Geographic feature, paleoanthropologist Richard Leakey—son of Louis and Mary Leakey—recounted his discovery of a nearly complete Australopithecus boisei skull (now Paranthropus boisei ), the same species his parents had found a decade earlier. Anthropologists inspect fossils discovered during an excavation. By Richard E. Leakey Photographs by Gordon Gahan Published October 13, 2025 This story originally published in the May 1970 issue of National Geographic magazine. See more digitized stories from our archives here. In fairness, I must give credit for the dramatic find to a camel—a large ungainly beast who had already won my affection with his deep brown eyes. I called him George. We had hoped to reach Kenya 's frontier with Ethiopia by dusk, Dr. Meave Epps and I, in our exploration last August of this vast, virtually trackless region east of Lake Rudolf. It was the second season of our survey to learn the nature and extent of the area's fossil deposits. Had we been traveling in the relative comfort of a Land-Rover, no doubt we would have dismissed a small rocky outcrop some two miles east of our course as not worth investigating. But we were already three days' tiring march inland by camel from our base camp at Koobi Fora, on Lake Rudolf's eastern shore, where we had left the rest of the expedition. George was complaining noisily; he had carried me far enough that day. And frankly, I welcomed relief from his jolting gait. "Let's have a look at that exposure and make camp," I said. "Another day to the border won't matter." Meave, a zoologist on our expedition's staff, offered no objection, nor did the other two members of our camel party, Nzube Mutwiwa and Kamoya Kimeu. The grayish-brown ledge of sediments, sliced open by centuries of erosion, proved far more extensive than it had first appeared. As we approached it, Nzube and Kamoya circled out in one direction, Meave and I explored the other. Almost immediately we found fossils—heavy, bleached bones of ancient elephants , pigs, and other animals of the late Pliocene or early Pleistocene epochs , two to three million years old. Camels carry the 25-year-old author, left, and his party along Lake Rudolf in northern Kenya. With Richard Leakey ride Dr. Meave Epps, a zoologist with the National Museum at Nairobi, and assistants Kamoya Kimeu and Nzube Mutwiwa. Exploring a vast desert often too broken for motor vehicles, the expedition mapped areas for later study. We hobbled the camels and made camp. In the morning, after tea, we split up to explore the rest of the exposure. I was walking along the dry bed of a small stream that had carved open the fossil-bearing strata, when my heart suddenly leaped. "Meave!" I shouted, so sharply that she ran a few steps in alarm. "What is it—a snake?" I pointed. There on the sand 20 feet ahead, in full view beside a thorny bush, lay a domed grayish-white object. Halfway to it I sat down stunned, incredulous, staring. For years I had dreamed of such a prize, and now I had found it—the nearly complete skull of an early hominid. The bony sagittal crest atop the skull, together with enormous brow ridges, flat face, and small brain case, marked it clearly as an Australopithecus , a primitive manlike creature whose fragmented 1.75-million-year old remains had also been found at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania by my parents. The one I had found, intact except for teeth and lower jaw, closely resembled the Olduvai specimen of Australopithecus boisei , formerly called Zinjanthropus boisei . Mine was the first to be discovered in Kenya. And later study would indicate that it is perhaps 850,000 years older than the Olduvai skull! ( Remembering Richard Leakey , a trailblazing conservationist

Vistazo Las estadísticas del cáncer en los Estados Unidos son las estadísticas federales oficiales. Estas combinan los datos de registros recolectados por el Programa Nacional de Registros del Cáncer de los CDC y los del Programa de Vigilancia, Epidemiología y Resultados Finales del Instituto Nacional del Cáncer. Estos datos se usan para entender la carga y las tendencias del cáncer, apoyar las investigaciones sobre el cáncer, medir el progreso de los esfuerzos del control y la prevención del cáncer, dirigir acción para eliminar las disparidades, y mejorar los resultados relacionados al cáncer para todos. Hecho En los Estados Unidos en el 2023, se notificaron 1 941 540 casos nuevos de cáncer. En los Estados Unidos en el 2024, 619 871 personas murieron de cáncer. El 2023 es el año más reciente sobre el cual hay datos de incidencia del cáncer disponibles; el 2024 es el año más reciente sobre el cual hay datos de mortalidad del cáncer disponibles. pages.text: American holidays | USAGov Skip to main content American holidays The United States recognizes 12 federal holidays. Learn about federal, state, and cultural holidays celebrated in the U.S. Federal holidays Many government offices and some private businesses close on annual federal holidays. If the holiday falls during the weekend, the government may observe it on a different day. Holiday When it is observed New Year's Day January 1 Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr. Third Monday in January Inauguration Day January 20, every 4 years following a presidential election Washington's Birthday Also known as Presidents Day Third Monday in February Memorial Day Last Monday in May Juneteenth National Independence Day June 19 Independence Day July 4 Labor Day First Monday in September Columbus Day Second Monday in October Veterans Day November 11 Thanksgiving Day Fourth Thursday in November Christmas Day December 25 Find out the history and how holidays are celebrated in the U.S. Learn the difference between Memorial Day and Veterans Day On Memorial Day, America honors those who died while serving in the military. On Veterans Day, the country celebrates everyone who has served in the military. State holidays States and the District of Columbia may recognize their own holidays, such as Emancipation Day or Indigenous Peoples Day. These holidays recognize events and people important to a state’s history and culture. Commonly celebrated holidays and observances Some holidays honor specific groups and events, such as Flag Day and Halloween. These are not federal holidays. Some holidays and observances receive presidential proclamations. Ethnic and religious holidays Various ethnic and religious groups in the United States celebrate days with special meaning to them. These holidays include Easter and Christmas for Christians, the High Holy Days for Jews, Ramadan for Muslims, Day of Vesak for Buddhists, and Diwali for Hindus. Particulate Matter (PM) Basics On This Page: What is PM, and how does it get into the air? What are the harmful effects of PM? What is being done to reduce particle pollution? How can I reduce my exposure to PM? What is PM, and how does it get into the air? Size comparisons for PM particles PM stands for particulate matter (also called particle pollution): the term for a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets found in the air. Some particles, such as dust, dirt, soot, or smoke, are large or dark enough to be seen with the naked eye. Others are so small they can only be detected using an electron microscope. Particle pollution includes: PM 10 : inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 10 micrometers and smaller; and PM 2.5 : fine inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 2.5 micrometers and smaller. How small is 2.5 micrometers? Think about a single hair from your head. The average human hair is about 70 micrometers in diameter – making it 30 times larger than the largest fine particle. Sources of PM These particles come in many sizes and shapes and can be made up of hundreds of different chemicals. Some are emitted directly from a source, such as construction sites, unpaved roads, fields, smokestacks or fires. Most particles form in the atmosphere as a result of complex reactions of chemicals such as sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, which are pollutants emitted from power plants, industries and automobiles. What are the Harmful Effects of PM? Particulate matter contains microscopic solids or liquid droplets that are so small that they can be inhaled and cause serious health problems. Some particles less than 10 micrometers in diameter can get deep into your lungs and some may even get into your bloodstream. Of these, particles less than 2.5 micrometers in diameter, also known as fine particles or PM 2.5 , pose the greatest risk to health. Fine particles are also the main cause of reduced visibility (haze) in parts of the United States, including many of our treasured national parks and wilderness areas. Learn more about health and environmental effects What is Being Done to Reduce Particle Pollution? EPA regulates inhalable particles. Particles of sand and large dust, which are larger than 10 micrometers, are not regulated by EPA. EPA’s national and regional rules to reduce emissions of pollutants that form PM will help state and local governments meet the Agency’s national air quality standards. Learn about how air quality standards help reduce PM. How Can I Reduce My Exposure to PM? You can use air quality alerts to protect yourself and others when PM reaches harmful levels: AirNow : Every day the Air Quality Index (AQI) tells you how clean or polluted your outdoor air is, along with associated health effects that may be of concern. The AQI translates air quality data into numbers and colors that help people understand when to take action to protect their health. Go to About AirNow to learn how you can get AQI notifications. Also learn how the Air Quality Flag Program can help air agencies, schools, and other community organizations to notify their citizens of harmful conditions and adjust outdoor physical activities as needed. pages.text: Alivio de la imposición de multas | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Alivio de la imposición de multas English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Pagar Cuenta bancaria (Pago directo) Tarjeta de crédito o débito Su Cuenta en línea Pago de impuestos de negocio (EFTPS) Plan de pagos Ayuda para la deuda tributaria Multas Intereses Retención de impuestos Pagos electrónicos extranjeros Cargos administrativos Puede que tenga derecho al alivio de una multa si intentó cumplir con las leyes tributarias pero no pudo por circunstancias fuera de su control. Si recibió un aviso o carta, verifique que la información sea correcta. Si la información no es correcta, siga las instrucciones en su aviso o carta. Si pudo resolver el problema, puede que no deba aplicarse una multa. Para obtener más información, visite Cómo entender su carta o aviso del IRS . Tipos de alivios de imposición de multas Puede que le otorguen uno de los siguientes tipos de alivios de multas según la multa: Reducción de multa impuesta por primera vez u otra dispensa administrativa Causa razonable Excepción estatutaria Cómo solicitar el alivio de imposición de multa Siga las instrucciones en el aviso del IRS que recibió. Algunas solicitudes de alivio de multas pueden ser aceptadas por teléfono. Llámenos al número de teléfono gratuito que se encuentra en su aviso o carta. Tenga la siguiente información cuando llame: El aviso o carta que le enviamos La multa que desea aliviar Las razones por las que cree que deberíamos eliminarla Durante la llamada, le diremos si el alivio de la multa es aprobado. Si no podemos aprobar su alivio por teléfono, puede solicitar el alivio por escrito con el Formulario 843, Reclamación de reembolso y solicitud de reducción (en inglés) . Para reducir o eliminar una multa del impuesto estimado, consulte: Multa a individuos por pago insuficiente del impuesto estimado Multa a corporaciones por pago insuficiente del impuesto estimado Cómo apelar una decisión de alivio de multa Si recibió un aviso o carta que dice que le rechazamos su solicitud de alivio de la multa, consulte la Elegibilidad para apelar multas (en inglés) para conocer los próximos pasos. Alivio de intereses Cobramos intereses sobre las multas. Los intereses incrementan el monto que usted debe hasta que pague el saldo en su totalidad. Le reduciremos o eliminaremos automáticamente los intereses relacionados si se reduce o elimina cualquiera de sus multas. Para obtener más información sobre los intereses que cobramos sobre las multas, vea Intereses . pages.text: UNESCO: Construyendo la Paz a través de la Educación, la Ciencia y la Cultura, la comunicación y la información Pasar al contenido principal Búsqueda Búsqueda Quicks links : Inteligencia Artificial Respuestas a emergencias Desafíos clave ©Ramon R/Shutterstock.com COP31: Proteger nuestras reservas de agua Mientras se celebra la COP31 en Antalya (Türkiye), del 9 al 20 de noviembre de 2026, bajo el tema de la resiliencia hídrica y oceánica, la UNESCO llama la atención sobre la criosfera, es decir, las regiones heladas de la Tierra: glaciares, mantos de hielo, nieve, hielo marino y permafrost. Estas reservas heladas contienen casi el 70% del agua dulce del planeta, pero se están derritiendo a un ritmo acelerado. Para protegerlas, la UNESCO promueve soluciones integradas que combinan la ciencia, la educación y los conocimientos de los pueblos indígenas y las comunidades locales. Ver más La UNESCO actúa en apoyo de las personas afectadas por crisis La cultura, la educación, la ciencia y la información son necesidades esenciales en tiempos de turbulencia y crisis. Son motores poderosos de cohesión social, resiliencia y esperanza en un futuro mejor. La UNESCO desempeña un papel vital en la protección de los fundamentos sociales y culturales que sustentan la estabilidad, la dignidad y la recuperación de las comunidades afectadas por crisis. Al proteger estos pilares, ayudamos a garantizar que las sociedades puedan reconstruir no solo la infraestructura, sino también la confianza, la identidad y la capacidad colectiva para avanzar. Leer más ©UNESCO Nuestro impacto en las comunidades Descubra cómo la UNESCO impulsa el cambio en todo el mundo. ¿Cuál es la magnitud de la brecha de género en el liderazgo educativo? Cuatro preguntas que plantearse antes de elegir tecnología para la educación Adaptación al cambio climático en las escuelas de Madagascar De la promesa a la acción: cómo los docentes de Kenya toman medidas para lograr colegios más seguros y estudiantes más sanos Ver más UNESCO en breve La UNESCO es la organización de las Naciones Unidas que promueve la cooperación en educación, ciencia, cultura y comunicación para fomentar la paz en todo el mundo. La Organización ofrece servicios clave a sus Estados miembros, estableciendo normas y estándares globales, desarrollando herramientas para la cooperación internacional, generando conocimiento para las políticas públicas y construyendo redes globales de sitios e instituciones inscritas en sus listas. Descubrir Thumbnail play_arrow © UNESCO Nuestras áreas de competencia La UNESCO utiliza la educación, la ciencia, la cultura, la comunicación y la información para fomentar el entendimiento mutuo y el respeto por nuestro planeta. Nuestros objetivos estratégicos La estrategia de la UNESCO aborda los desafíos globales con objetivos en educación, medio ambiente, cohesión social y tecnología. Actuar en tiempos de emergencias La UNESCO apoya a las comunidades afectadas por los conflictos y catástrofes causadas por riesgos naturales, garantizando el acceso a una educación de calidad y la protección del patrimonio cultural. Construir un multilateralismo más fuerte La UNESCO se sitúa en primera línea de la cooperación internacional, en estrecha coordinación con los otros organismos del Sistema de Naciones Unidas. pages.description: OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
pages.text: infraboiii's Diary | Vending machines in France: what 7,800 OSM objects say about tagging | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close infraboiii's Diary Vending machines in France: what 7,800 OSM objects say about tagging Posted by infraboiii on 10 November 2026 in English . I maintain a map of vending machines built from OpenStreetMap data, part of a site that connects vending operators with venues (link at the end). It covers France, Belgium, Germany, Austria and Italy and is refreshed every month from Geofabrik extracts. While importing the 8 November 2026 extract, a few things about how vending machines are tagged stood out. I’m sharing them in case they are useful to mappers and data consumers. The numbers. The French extracts (mainland and overseas) contain 37,259 objects tagged amenity=vending_machine . The map shows 7,779 of them: those whose vending=* value (or, failing that, name ) is a product people seek out, such as food, drinks, bread, pizza, farm products, hygiene products and food lockers. Left out are, among others, machines with no identifiable product, cigarette machines and parcel lockers. The figures below refer to these 7,779 machines, compared with 17,924 selected the same way in Germany. Product mix. The most common values are condoms (1,456), pizza (1,425) and bread (934). Germany, with more than twice as many machines on the map, has 132 pizza and 42 bread machines. One machine, several products. In France, 1,530 machines (20%) list several products in a single semicolon-separated value, in no fixed order: drinks;sweets 418 times, sweets;drinks 30 times; drinks;food 257 times, food;drinks 60 times. That is valid tagging, but data consumers have to split the values before counting. Opening hours are rare. Only 9% of French machines have opening_hours (11% in Germany). Many are accessible around the clock, and for those opening_hours=24/7 is a one-tag fix. Payment. In France, 18% of machines have a payment:* tag, compared with 39% in Germany. Freshness. In France, 22% of machines have check_date or survey:date (38% in Germany), and 31% were last edited before November 2023. Machines are sometimes removed without the data being updated. Adding check_date when you see one tells the next person that it was still there on that date. Products hidden in the name. For 45 French machines, the product shown on the map came from name rather than vending=* . A vending=* value is far easier for software to use than free text in a name. If you walk past a vending machine, four tags help most: vending=* , opening_hours , payment:* and check_date . Corrections and comments are welcome. The map: https://globalvendingspot.com/fr/carte-distributeurs (also https://globalvendingspot.com/de/automatenkarte and https://globalvendingspot.com/at/automatenkarte ). The filtered data, as CSV and GeoJSON under the ODbL: https://globalvendingspot.com/fr/carte-distributeurs/donnees Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Setting and Reviewing Standards to Control Particulate Matter (PM) Pollution On This Page: What are PM air quality standards? How are they developed and reviewed? What scientific and technical information supports reviews? What Are Particulate Matter (PM) Air Quality Standards? National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM pollution specify a maximum amount of PM to be present in outdoor air. There are different standards for PM 10 and PM 2.5 (see Particulate Matter (PM) Basics to learn about particle types). Limiting PM pollution in the air protects human health and the environment. See NAAQS for PM for an in-depth explanation of the current PM standards, including Federal Register citations and fact sheets. How Are PM Standards Developed and Reviewed? The Clean Air Act requires EPA to set national air quality standards for particulate matter, as one of the six criteria pollutants considered harmful to public health and the environment. The law also requires EPA to periodically review the standards to ensure that they provide adequate health and environmental protection, and to update those standards as necessary. Learn more about the standards review process View a timeline of the particulate matter (PM) NAAQS : get an overview of how the standards have changed over time. What Scientific and Technical Information Supports Review of the Standards? The various documents published during the review process include multiple drafts of plans and assessments, reports from the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee (CASAC), and Federal Register notices. pages.text: About the National Contact Center | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content About the National Contact Center More in This Section Close Department of Labor National Contact Center About the National Contact Center Topics National Contact Center The Department of Labor National Contact Center (DOL-NCC) is an enterprise contact center that supports all of the Department’s initiatives and programs with shared customer services. We were founded on Labor Day 2001 as a part of the Enterprise Communications Initiative (ECI) under Secretary Order 2-2005. Since 2007 we have grown from providing services to 4 DOL agencies to maintaining and communicating content in our Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system for all 28 DOL agencies. The DOL-NCC interacts with customers through various communication vehicles including telephone, e-mail / e-correspondence text messaging services, callback assist, and poster fulfillment. We provide live English and Spanish speaking agents. In addition, we offer DOL agencies access to the Multilanguage Gateway where specific requirements can be specified for translation and interpretation services for more than 290 different languages. To date, the DOL-NCC has received over 30 million calls and processed over 1 million e-mails, over 1 million Job Corps brochure requests, and over 750,000 customer escalations. 1-866-4-USA-DOL (866-487-2365) is the main toll-free telephone number that serves as the universal access point for the Department and is managed by the DOL-NCC Federal staff. Our hours of operation are 8:00 am and 8:00 pm (EST) on weekdays, except Federal holidays. The DOL-NCC also provides 24x7x365 coverage for the OSHA Referral and Information Line, the MSHA Emergency and Hazard Complaint Line, and Job Corps programs. DOL-NCC also maintains and operates the toll-free telephone numbers and/or E-correspondence for the following agencies: Administrative Review Board (ARB) Benefits Review Board (BRB) Employees' Compensation Appeals Board (ECAB) Employment and Training Administration (ETA) Job Corps Mine Safety & Health Administration (MSHA) Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration and Management (OASAM) Office of the Assistant Secretary for Policy (OASP) Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Office of Disability Employment Policy (ODEP) Ombudsman for the Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program (EEOMBD) Office of the Secretary (OSEC) Veterans' Employment and Training Service (VETS) Women's Bureau (WB)
