pages.title: Cómo entender su aviso CP504 (SP) | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Usted tiene un saldo sin pagar en su cuenta. De no pagar esta cantidad inmediatamente, el IRS embargará todo reembolso de los impuestos estatales sobre los ingresos al que tenga derecho y aplicarlo al pago de su deuda.
pages.text: Cómo entender su aviso CP504 (SP) | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Cómo entender su aviso CP504 (SP) English Español Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) De qué se trata este aviso Usted tiene un saldo sin pagar en su cuenta. De no pagar esta cantidad inmediatamente, el IRS embargará todo reembolso de los impuestos estatales sobre los ingresos al que tenga derecho y aplicarlo al pago de su deuda. Lo que usted tiene que hacer Lea cuidadosamente este aviso — éste le explicará su fecha de vencimiento, cantidad adeudada y opciones de pago. Pague la cantidad adeudada para la fecha de vencimiento. Visite la página de pagos para encontrar más información sobre sus opciones de pago. Tal vez usted desee Descargar información adicional sobre su cuenta tributaria. Aprender más sobre sus opciones de pago y cómo efectuar un acuerdo de pago . Preguntas frecuentes ¿Qué me dice este aviso? Este aviso le notifica que tenemos la intención de emitir un embargo sobre su reembolso de los impuestos estatales sobre los ingresos debido a que todavía tiene un saldo que debe en una de sus cuentas contributivas. Usted tiene que pagar esta cantidad inmediatamente para evitar esto. Además, se le informa que iniciaremos una búsqueda de sus bienes para emitir un embargo. También pudiéramos presentar un Aviso de Gravamen por Impuesto Federal, si aún no lo hemos realizado. Este aviso también explica la denegación o revocación de un pasaporte de los Estados Unidos. La Ley de Reparación del Transporte Terrestre de los Estados Unidos (FAST, por sus siglas en inglés), generalmente le prohíbe al Departamento de Estado de emitir o renovar el pasaporte a un contribuyente que tiene una deuda tributaria gravemente morosa. Hay información adicional referente a la certificación del pasaporte en IRS.gov/ passports (en inglés) . ¿Qué necesito hacer? Pague la cantidad adeudada que se refleja en el aviso. Envíe por correo su pago en el sobre que le enviamos. Incluya la parte inferior de este aviso para así asegurar que le acreditamos correctamente a su cuenta. Si no puede pagar la cantidad completa ahora, llámenos al número impreso en la parte superior de este aviso para conocer si reúne los requisitos para establecer un plan de pagos a plazos. ¿Cuánto tiempo tengo? Usted tiene que pagar el saldo para la fecha de vencimiento indicada en el aviso. ¿Qué sucede si no pago o no me comunico con el IRS? Si no paga la cantidad adeudada, podemos confiscar ("embargar") todo reembolso de los impuestos estatales al que usted tenga derecho. Éste es el aviso de intención de embargo según lo estipula la sección 6331(d) del Código de Impuestos Internos. Si usted aún tiene un saldo sin pagar después que le confisquemos ("embarguemos") su reembolso de los impuestos estatales, nosotros podemos enviarle un aviso otorgándole el derecho a una vista ante la Oficina Independiente de Apelaciones del IRS, si es que usted aún no ha recibido dicho aviso. Después podemos confiscar ("embargar") o tomar posesión de su otra propiedad o de sus derechos sobre la propiedad. La propiedad incluye: Salarios, comisiones de bienes inmuebles, y otros ingresos Cuentas bancarias Bienes comerciales Bienes personales (incluyendo su automóvil y hogar) Beneficios de Seguro Social Si no paga la cantidad adeudada ni nos llama para acordar un plan de pago, podemos presentar en cualquier momento un aviso de gravamen por impuesto federal sobre su propiedad, si aún no lo hemos hecho. Si el gravamen está vigente, es posible que usted tenga dificultades para vender o pedir prestado dando su propiedad como garantía. pages.description: 详细了解联合国教科文组织的定位、愿景和成果。联合国教科文组织全称为联合国教育、科学及文化组织。我们的目标是通过国际合作促进和平与安全
pages.text: 联合国教科文组织：通过教育、科学、文化、传播和信息建设和平 Skip to main content 搜索 搜索 Quicks links : AI Response to Crisis Key Challenges ©Ramon R/Shutterstock.com 第31届联合国气候变化大会：保护水资源储备 第31届联合国气候变化大会（COP31）于2026年11月9-20日在土耳其安塔利亚举行，主题为水和海洋韧性。联合国教科文组织呼吁关注地球冰冻圈，包括冰川、冰盖、积雪、海冰和永冻土等区域。冰冻圈储存着全球近70%的淡水资源，却正迅速消融。教科文组织倡导综合性解决方案，结合科学、教育及土著和地方知识，共同保护这些珍贵资源。 阅读更多 服务和平80年 1946年11月4日，《联合国教科文组织组织法》正式生效。80年前，一个组织诞生，源于一条简单信念：和平须通过知识、对话与合作筑基于人之思想。自那时起，联合国教科文组织制定国际标准，保护遗产，捍卫言论自由，支持教育，并让科学服务于人类。让我们重温其与194个会员国一道塑造自身历史的声音与时刻。 阅读更多 © UNESCO 我们在社区的影响 了解联合国教科文组织如何在全球推动变革。 在教育中选择使用科技前，需要思考的四个问题 教育领导层中的性别差距有多大？ 信息就是生命线：支持灾区记者 守护国家记忆之声 Load more 教科文组织简介 联合国教科文组织是联合国的一个专门机构，旨在通过教育、科学、文化和传播促进全球和平。 该组织为其成员国提供关键服务，制定全球规范和标准，开发国际合作工具，生成公共政策所需的知识，并建立列入其名录的遗址和机构的全球网络。 探索 Thumbnail play_arrow © UNESCO 我们的专长领域 联合国教科文组织利用教育、科学、文化、传播和信息来促进相互理解并增进对我们地球的尊重。 我们的战略目标 联合国教科文组织的战略通过在教育、环境、社会凝聚力和技术等领域设定目标来应对全球挑战。 在紧急时期提供支持 联合国教科文组织支持受冲突和自然灾害影响的社区，确保其获得优质教育并保护文化遗产。 建设更强大的多边主义 联合国教科文组织处于国际合作的前沿，并与联合国系统的其他相关机构紧密协调。 联合国教科文组织名录与认证 联合国教科文组织的遗产地连接世界，彰显我们共同人性的最佳部分。 1273 世界遗产地 849 非物质遗产要素 797 生物圈保护区 241 世界地质公园 教科文组织《信使》杂志 联合国教科文旗舰杂志—自1948年以来，为您带来全球问题的多样化视角。当前提供超过6种联合国官方语言的版本。 探索 杂志：联合国教科文组织快报 本土知识如何推动科学发展 长久以来，本土知识一直被科学界忽视，有时甚至遭到抵制。而如今，它正重新引发人们的关注，这一转变可谓恰逢其时：全球机械化进程带来的种种后果，以及与气候变化和健康问题相关的危机，正促使我们重新审视那些长期以来被边缘化的知识体系、实践经验和专业技能。 本土知识植根于对生态系统的细致观察，并通过口耳相传的方式世代绵延，为构建可持续的未来提供了宝贵的钥匙。 探索最新一期 ©UNESCO 新闻 新闻 第三届让文化遗产“活”起来微视频征集公告 新闻 科技赋能生态保护，青年共创可持续未来 ——联合国教科文组织—比亚迪“追光者计划第三季”首站活动在黑龙江成功举办 新闻 教科文组织—赤道几内亚国际生命科学研究奖授予中国、西班牙、摩洛哥3位科学家 新闻稿 6/7记者遇害案未司法解决， 打击有罪不罚现倒退 Load more top 我们在本网站使用 cookies 以提升您的用户体验。如需了解更多关于我们如何使用 cookies 的信息，请阅读 我们的隐私声明 close

pages.title: Brand moved from Wandsworth to category C prison HMP Littlehey, his wife confirms British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The convicted rapist has been moved to HMP Littlehey, which houses sex offenders.
pages.text: Brand moved from Wandsworth to category C prison HMP Littlehey, his wife confirms Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Brand moved from Wandsworth to category C prison, his wife confirms on podcast 8 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Sima Kotecha Senior UK correspondent Press Association Russell Brand was accompanied by his wife, Laura, during his trial at Southwark Crown Court Russell Brand has been transferred to a category C prison, his wife Laura has confirmed, in her first public comments since he was jailed. On Monday, the comedian was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Over the weekend, Brand was transferred from category B HMP Wandsworth in London to HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire, which houses men convicted of sexual offences. Laura Brand returned to the couple's podcast on Sunday, saying that she had spoken to her husband in prison and he "is OK and is praying". Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US. HMP Littlehey, a category C training prison, is one of the largest prisons in Europe for men convicted of sexual offences. It held more than 1,200 prisoners as of January 2025, according to data from the Independent Monitoring Board. Before Brand's move to the prison, a source close to the disgraced comedian said he was doing "remarkably well considering the circumstances" at HMP Wandsworth and that he had been moved from isolation to a main wing. A member of staff at Wandsworth said there had been "much excitement" among the inmates about Brand's arrival, with some slamming on cell doors and shouting out his name. They added that there had also been some anger displayed about his crimes. Staff at other prisons told the BBC Brand's fame, combined with the nature of his crimes, could make him a target for other inmates. In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can seen sitting on a sofa in what looks like a conservatory. She is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her. The Russell Brand I saw in court was not the flamboyant character most people will know Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says The couple had continued their YouTube podcast during Brand's trial. They often read snippets of the Bible and discussed religion. On Sunday, Laura told their followers: "We trust his [God's] plan and everything he is doing just now, even though it's painful and obviously will take some getting used to." During the show, Laura played an episode she said had been recorded before her husband was jailed. It featured the couple singing to a recording of the American folk singer Woody Guthrie before praying together. Towards the end of the podcast, Laura returned on her own to read a message from her husband, in which he said he was not guilty of the offences he had been jailed for. He called staff at HMP Littlehey "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and he asked people to support his "treasured wife and family". Andrea Simon, the Victims' Commissioner for London, said the continued broadcast of Brand's podcast "is really problematic". Simon told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the show "will certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape". While freedom of expression allows convicted sex offenders like Brand to profess their innocence, Simon said terms of service of media platforms should regulate "the way in which they get their message out". The commissioner added that prison rules should also be reviewed to "bar those convicted of sending messages to be broadcast" unless permission is granted by the prison governor. pages.title: BLM Approves 304-Acre Forest Thinning Project to Reduce Wildfire Risk Near Adin | Bureau of Land Management Lock
pages.description: The Bureau of Land Management has approved a project to thin overgrown forest and reduce hazardous fuels on approximately 304 acres of public land, southwest of Adin, to help protect rural communities in northeastern California from wildfire.
pages.text: BLM Approves 304-Acre Forest Thinning Project to Reduce Wildfire Risk Near Adin | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM Approves 304-Acre Forest Thinning Project to Reduce Wildfire Risk Near Adin California Media Contact BLM California BLM_CA_Press@blm.gov BLM Office: Applegate Field Office November 10, 2026 ALTURAS, Calif. – The Bureau of Land Management has approved a project to thin overgrown forest and reduce hazardous fuels on approximately 304 acres of public land, southwest of Adin, to help protect rural communities in northeastern California from wildfire. The Letterbox Forest Health and Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project will restore more open ponderosa pine forests by reducing excess vegetation, improving forest health and removing fuels that can carry flames into tree canopies. Work is expected to begin in fall 2026 or spring 2027 and be completed by 2029 under a stewardship contract. “By reducing hazardous fuels and restoring more open ponderosa pine forest conditions, we can improve forest health and resilience while helping reduce the risk of severe wildfires that threaten nearby communities.” said Kevin Kunkel with the BLM’s Applegate Field Office. The project area was harvested in 1958 and 1988 to remove mature ponderosa pine trees and promote the growth of smaller trees. Since then, the forest has become densely stocked, departing from historical conditions characterized by large trees and open, park-like stands. Crews will thin trees, reduce canopy cover, and remove smaller trees and other vegetation that can act as ladder fuels, allowing flames to climb from the forest floor into tree canopies. Larger trees will be retained, while openings and tree groupings will promote forest diversity and improve wildlife habitat. Mechanical equipment will be used where terrain allows, while chainsaws will be used in steep or rocky areas. Crews may also prune retained trees to reduce vertical fuel continuity. Woody debris will be piled for burning, and suitable biomass may be chipped and transported to a nearby facility if feasible. Broadcast burning may also be used to reduce fuel loads and reintroduce fire as a natural ecological process. Prescribed burns will follow an approved burn plan and occur when conditions are appropriate. The BLM will improve approximately six miles of existing roads to support operations and may construct up to one-half mile of temporary road. Any temporary roads constructed for the project will be decommissioned within three years. The project supports the Lassen County Fire Safe Comprehensive Wildfire Protection Plan and the CAL FIRE Lassen-Modoc Unit Strategic Fire Plan. Maintenance treatments are planned for 15 to 20 years to sustain the benefits of the work. Designated treatment areas will also be available for fuelwood collection under applicable BLM requirements. More information is available on the BLM’s Letterbox Forest Health and Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project page . Contact the BLM Applegate Field Office at 530-279-6101 for more information. The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

pages.text: Understanding your CP2000 series notice | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Understanding your CP2000 series notice More In Help Interactive Tax Assistant Tools Report fraud Tax scams Identity theft Notices and letters Appeals Frequently asked questions Accessibility Contact your local IRS office Contact an international IRS office Tax topics Other languages The CP2000 notice series includes: CP2000, CP2000A, CP2000B, CP2000C, CP2000D and CP2000E. Learn what your notice is about and what to do. Why you received this notice The income or payment information we received from third parties, such as employers or financial institutions, doesn't match what you reported on your tax return. This difference may increase or decrease your tax or may not change it at all. The notice explains proposed changes to your tax return and information we used to determine them. This notice isn’t a bill and your response may be required. What you need to do Review the entire notice and follow the instructions to resolve this issue. Reply to the notice by the date listed. If a response form is included in your notice , complete and sign it. State whether you agree or disagree with the notice and include any supporting documentation. If your notice doesn’t have a response form , follow the notice’s instructions. If you agree with the notice and don’t have other income, credits, or expenses to report , follow the notice’s instructions. You don’t need to amend your return. Inicio Impacto Historia Participe Visítenos Quiénes somos La UNESCO, la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Educación, la Ciencia y la Cultura, es una agencia especializada dedicada a fortalecer nuestra humanidad compartida mediante la promoción de la educación, la ciencia, la cultura y la comunicación. Establecemos estándares, producimos herramientas y desarrollamos conocimientos para crear soluciones a algunos de los mayores desafíos de nuestro tiempo, fomentando un mundo con mayor igualdad y paz. Proteger la biodiversidad, responder a los retos de la inteligencia artificial, promover una educación de calidad, salvaguardar el patrimonio y garantizar el acceso a información confiable son algunos ejemplos del trabajo que la UNESCO realiza con sus 194 Estados Miembros en todo el mundo. Thumbnail play_arrow © UNESCO Constitución de la UNESCO "Una paz fundada exclusivamente en acuerdos políticos y económicos entre gobiernos no podría obtener el apoyo unánime, sincero y perdurable de los pueblos, y que, por consiguiente, esa paz debe basarse en la solidaridad intelectual y moral de la humanidad". La Conferencia General, con representantes de todos los Estados Miembros, determina las principales líneas de trabajo de la UNESCO. La Secretaría ejecuta el programa de la Organización bajo la autoridad del Director General . El Consejo Ejecutivo monitorea la implementación del programa de la Organización. Juntos, estos órganos dirigen los esfuerzos de la UNESCO en materia de educación, ciencia, cultura y comunicación. pages.title: North Yorkshire leaders reject police 'mega-force' plans British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Rural officers in North Yorkshire will be diverted to towns and cities, politicians warn.
pages.text: North Yorkshire leaders reject police 'mega-force' plans Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Local leaders reject police 'mega-force' plans 12 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Richard Edwards North Yorkshire political reporter EMMA GLASBEY/BBC North Yorkshire Police could be merged into a regional force if the so-called "mega force" proposals are approved Senior politicians across North Yorkshire have spoken of their opposition to proposals for so-called police "mega-forces". Sir Mark Rowley, Britain's most senior police officer, recently said policing was "heading for failure" without change and has proposed between eight and 10 regional forces should be established. But Jo Coles, York and North Yorkshire's Labour deputy mayor, warned bigger forces would jeopardise links between officers and their communities, adding that merging forces would prove a "distraction" and would "take resources from the front line". A Home Office spokesperson said the current model of policing "has not changed since the 1960s and is no longer fit for purpose". Coles, whose role is to oversee both North Yorkshire Police and North Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service, said she and York and North Yorkshire's elected mayor David Skaith were, however, not opposed to the creation of a National Police Service to tackle serious cross-border crime. Coles said the national service, plans for which were set out last January in the government's policing white paper, would save money by pulling together areas of regional expertise. Under that government proposal, the service would bring together various organisations, including the National Crime Agency, Counter Terror Policing and the National Police Air Service. Coles said: "It would drive through a lot of efficiency and save a lot of money. That is the money we think should be filtered back down into neighbourhood policing." But Coles and Skaith have argued for the existing mayoral combined authorities, set up to deliver and scrutinise the elected mayor's policy programme, to be the "default structure" for any policing reforms. BBC/RICHARD EDWARDS Jo Coles, York and North Yorkshire's Labour deputy mayor for policing, fire and crime, says merging forces would be a "distraction" North Yorkshire Council's Conservative leader Carl Les, who serves on the combined authority, said there was "a logic to joining up some services to make a stronger whole". But he warned that "losing more identifiable local forces will run the very real risk of losing a local presence, which is essential to maintaining community confidence". "Time and again, resources will be sucked away to meet needs elsewhere, especially in cities, at the expense of rural areas like North Yorkshire," he said. Coles added: "At the moment, we have some really good oversight of policing and have the ability to bring partners together who can reduce harm in communities and build public safety. That's what is at risk from a mega-force. "Criminal justice, health, housing and transport - all of those people need to be pulling together to make our communities safer. "The Home Office is looking at this through a lens of policing and policing alone, whereas actually we build public safety in partnerships with other organisations." BBC/RICHARD EDWARDS North Yorkshire Police could be merged with other forces if the proposals are put into effect Nigel Ayre, who leads City of York Council's opposition Liberal Democrat group, said it was "not very often" he agreed with Coles, who is also a city councillor. But he said: "On this one, she is absolutely right. Policing needs to be close to communities. That is when it works best. "While there needs to be cross-border collaboration on certain things like county lines drug dealing, policing needs to be in the community where it is most effective." Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM Approves Post-Fire Restoration Plan for S-1 Vya Fire Area California Media Contact BLM California BLM_CA_Press@blm.gov BLM Office: Applegate Field Office November 10, 2026 ALTURAS, Calif. – The Bureau of Land Management has approved an emergency stabilization and burned area response plan for the S-1 Vya Fire area, authorizing efforts to repair fire-damaged fencing and restore vegetation on approximately 287 acres of public and private land within the fire perimeter. The plan, approved by the BLM’s Applegate Field Office, includes repairing or replacing approximately 12 miles of allotment boundary fencing damaged by the fire and drill seeding to improve soil stability and establish perennial grass cover for wildlife, including mule deer and pronghorn. “Post-fire restoration is critical to stabilizing soils, reestablishing vegetation and protecting wildlife habitat. Repairing damaged fencing and reseeding affected areas will help the landscape recover while supporting wildlife and livestock management,” said Kevin Kunkel for the Applegate Field Office. Seeding operations are expected to begin in fall 2026 and last approximately two to three weeks. Crews will use range drills pulled by a D6 bulldozer or large tractor, with all access to project sites occurring on existing roads and routes. The BLM developed seed mixes using soil and precipitation data, along with ecological site descriptions from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service, to select vegetation suited to local conditions and the plan’s restoration objectives. Fence repairs and reconstruction are scheduled to begin in summer 2027 and be completed by fall 2028. The fencing will follow BLM specifications designed to support wildlife passage, including appropriate wire spacing and smooth wire along the bottom. The project area includes priority habitat management area designated for greater sage-grouse under the 2025 Greater Sage-Grouse Rangewide Planning Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment for Nevada and northeastern California. The project will follow the required design features for these designated areas. According to the BLM’s decision record, vegetation, soil and other public land resources are at immediate risk of erosion, degradation or additional damage following the wildfire. The agency approved the proposed action under its emergency stabilization and burned area response authorities. The decision is effective immediately and remains in effect during any appeal unless the Interior Board of Land Appeals grants a stay. More information is available through the BLM’s S-1 Vya Fire Emergency Stabilization and Burned Area Response Plan project page . Contact the BLM Applegate Field Office at 530-279-6101 for more information. The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

pages.title: Cómo entender su aviso CP71A (SP) | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Usted recibió este aviso para recordarle sobre la cantidad que adeuda en contribuciones, multas e intereses.
pages.text: Cómo entender su aviso CP71A (SP) | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Cómo entender su aviso CP71A (SP) English Español Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) De qué se trata este aviso Le recordamos de un saldo pendiente en su cuenta. Su cuenta permanecerá en estado incobrable hasta que su situación financiera cambie. Lo que necesita hacer Si su situación financiera no ha cambiado, no tiene que hacer nada en este momento. Continúe presentando sus declaraciones de impuestos a tiempo para notificarnos de cambios en su situación financiera. Tal vez le interes Infórmese sobre sus opciones de pago y cómo establecer un arreglo de pagos. El pagar tan pronto pueda minimiza, que se añadan intereses y multas a su saldo. Infórmese sobre cómo presentar un ofrecimiento de transacción ( OIC , por sus siglas en inglés). Preguntas frecuentes ¿Se me cobran intereses sobre el dinero que adeudo? Sí. se acumulan intereses a su saldo sin pagar hasta que en su totalidad. ¿Se me impondrá una multa si no puedo pagar la cantidad completa? Sí, se le impondrá multa por pago fuera de plazo. ¿Qué sucede si no puedo pagar toda la cantidad adeudada? Puede hacer arreglos para establecer un plan de pagos con nosotros si no puede pagar toda la cantidad adeudada. ¿Cómo puedo establecer un plan de pagos? Llame al número de teléfono gratuito en su aviso para discutir opciones de pago. Obtenga más información sobre arreglos de pago. ¿Qué sucede si necesito ayuda? Profesionales en impuestos independientes del Servicio de Impuestos Internos ( IRS , por sus siglas en inglés). posiblemente pueden ayudarle. Las Clínicas para Contribuyentes de Bajos Ingresos ( LITC , por sus siglas en inglés) pueden representar a personas de bajos ingresos ante el IRS o en la corte. Las LITC también pueden ayudar a personas que hablan inglés como segundo idioma. Los servicios que proporcionan las LITC son gratuitos o tienen un pequeño costo. Verifique si califica para recibir ayuda de una Clínica para Contribuyentes de Bajos Ingresos . Información útil Notifíquenos de un cambio en su dirección postal enviando el Formulario 8822 por correo. Obtenga más información sobre el proceso de colección en la Publicación 594 (SP), El Proceso de Cobro del IRS PDF Encuentre información sobre las tasas de intereses por pago insuficiente y pago en exceso de impuestos en el Aviso 746 (SP), Información Sobre su Aviso, Multas e Intereses PDF Comprenda sus obligaciones como contribuyente en la Publicación 2105, Why Do I Have to Pay Taxes ? PDF (¿Por qué debo pagar impuestos?) en inglés. Consejos para sus presentaciones de impuestos y cumplimiento de pagos en el futuro Si no paga suficientes impuestos durante el año, es posible que tenga que pagar una multa. Para evitar multas y que se utilicen sus futuros reembolsos de impuestos para compensar la cantidad que adeuda, considere ajustar su retención de impuestos. Si no paga o no paga suficientes impuestos mediante la retención de impuestos, es posible que tenga que pagar impuestos estimados. Para más información, consulte la Publicación 505, Retención de impuestos e impuestos estimados (en inglés) PDF . Considere presentar sus impuestos electrónicamente. El presentar en línea puede ayudarle a evitar errores y a encontrar créditos y deducciones para los que pudiera calificar. En muchos casos, puede presentar de manera gratuita. Obtenga más información sobre la presentación electrónica . State and Tribal Greenhouse Gas Data and Resources EPA publishes annual state and Tribal-level GHG data and resources. Learn more about each using the links below and find answers to frequently asked questions (pdf) about the data and resources. Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emission and Sinks by State EPA compiles and publishes annual state-by-state GHG data consistent with the national Inventory and international reporting guidelines, meaning state GHG totals when summed, will equal totals in the national Inventory . Learn more about EPA's state-level GHG estimates and underlying methods . State Inventory and Projection Tool EPA has also developed the State Inventory and Projection Tool (SIT) , an interactive spreadsheet tool designed to help states develop greenhouse gas emission and removal inventories and projections and lessen the time it takes to develop and/or update an inventory. The SIT uses data from the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gases and Sinks by State as well as other federal sources and allows users to customize their data inputs. Learn more about differences and planned updates (pdf) . State-level Non-CO 2 Emission Projections and Mitigation Potential EPA has developed additional state-level data to help states assess technical and economic mitigation potential for non-CO 2 GHGs from anthropogenic sources. Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) State and Tribal Fact Sheets EPA requires reporting of greenhouse gas (GHG) data and other relevant information from large GHG emission sources, fuel and industrial gas suppliers, and CO 2 injection sites in the United States. Annual GHGRP emissions data is now summarized in interactive fact sheets by state, tribal lands, or EPA region. Users can also download facility data based on the criteria selected. Facility-level data by state is a subset of overall state-level GHG emissions. Blog CESER Launches CIE Back-to-School Series: A Weekly Deep Dive into CIE Principles CESER and INL’s new learning hub will highlight one of the 12 CIE principles each week. Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response October 13, 2026 Estimated Read Time min Cybersecurity is a critical priority for energy organizations as cyberattacks continue to evolve in sophistication and frequency. Building and maintaining secure critical infrastructure today requires more than traditional reactive cyber measures. It demands the addition of engineered controls, which use engineering and physics to mitigate cyber risks. That is the foundation of Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response’s (CESER) Cyber-Informed Engineering (CIE) program. CIE guides organizations on how to embed cybersecurity into infrastructure engineering and design, effectively “engineering out” cyber risks by eliminating catastrophic consequences from cyber-enabled attacks. CESER and Idaho National Laboratory (INL) are launching the CIE Back-to-School Weekly series that offers an in-depth look at each of CIE's 12 foundational principles. Each week, new content will be added to the new CIE learning hub , giving energy professionals and engineers the opportunity to explore one principle at a time, progressively build understanding, and see how the principles build on one another. The learning hub will provide a principle overview, a case study to demonstrate application, and key questions that engineers can use to begin applying the principle to their organization’s energy systems. Explore the Learning Hub today to learn about Principle 1 (Consequence-Focused Design), and come back weekly to keep building your CIE knowledge. CESER partners with INL to build tools and resources that support CIE adoption , including a CIE Implementation Guide to navigate engineers through questions that apply CIE principles, and a web-based CIE Analysis Tool that can track responses to those questions. More tools, workbooks, and resources are available on INL’s CIE knowledge hub . As a capstone to the CIE Back-to-School Weekly Series, CESER and INL will release the CIE Handbook, a new resource that offers a simplified starting point to CIE adoption and connects users to CIE resources and research. Visit CESER’s CIE webpage for more information on the CIE program. Explore more on these topics: Energy Infrastructure Cybersecurity

pages.title: Dinosaur fossils are turning up in homes and offices of wealthy collectors | National Geographic
pages.description: These long-extinct, fearsome creatures are turning up in living rooms and corporate offices as wealthy collectors indulge a controversial hobby.
pages.text: Dinosaur fossils are turning up in homes and offices of wealthy collectors | National Geographic By Richard Conniff Photographs by Gabriele Galimberti and Juri De Luca 12 min read This story appears in the October 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. At a motel in the middle of Tucson, Arizona, a head and neck surgeon in cowboy boots and blue jeans is sitting by the pool and rhapsodizing about fossilized skulls. He brought one along in his carry-on luggage on the flight into town, and he’s plainly thrilled by the perfect state of the braincase and the openings where cranial nerves once ran. ( Cyclops Myth Spurred by 'One-Eyed' Fossils?) “I can see the optic nerve that gave vision,” he says, as if the skull’s former occupant still lives. “I can see the abducens nerve, which allowed lateral eye motion, and the trigeminal nerve, which gave sensation to the skin of the face.” The surgeon has asked not to be identified in this article. Owning a collection of fossil skulls makes him both gleefully happy and nervously discreet, like many collectors in town for the Tucson Gem and Mineral Show. He’s building a “private museum” to house the skulls, and he grins at the thought of displaying them in chronological order: the 36-inch-long Allosaurus skull, the toothy sea monster Elasmosaurus, and the most complete skull of a Pteranodon ever found. ( For the Love of Dinosaurs) Workers at Zoic, a fossil restoration firm in Trieste, Italy, reassemble an Allosaurus unearthed in Wyoming. The specimen later sold at auction in Paris for $1.4 million. Like a prehistoric nod to the sea outside, a 17-foot-long mosasaur floats above Joan and Henry Kriegstein in their home in Massachusetts. The marine reptile is one of several fossils Henry Kriegstein has collected over the past 30 years. An ophthalmologist, he tracks his love of extinct beasts to childhood. Kriegstein grew up in Manhattan, and the American Museum of Natural History was his favorite local spot. “I was amazed by these dinosaur skeletons in the middle of New York,” he says. Every summer he digs in the Dakotas, Wyoming, or Montana, often with his oldest daughter, Adie, who found the mosasaur. To him, fossils represent a key to our biological past. Being in their presence, he says, awakens “a very spiritual feeling of connection with the history of life.” Private fossil collectors are pretty common these days. Some, like the surgeon, are serious enough to pass for professional paleontologists. Others seem mainly to be indulging a boyish taste for big, scary—and expensive—monsters. A few collectors rank among the world’s megarich, such as the Chinese real estate developer haggling in Tucson for an Ichthyosaurus, a large marine reptile, offered at $750,000. More nervous privacy: The developer interrupts my question to his translator by loudly clearing his throat and marching off grimly in the direction of a three-million-dollar Stegosaurus. ( How To Find Dinosaur Bones ) The passion for paleontology among private collectors means that dinosaurs and other fossil giants can turn up in homes and businesses almost anywhere. In a waterfront summer house in Massachusetts, the shield and horns of a Triceratops skull greet weekend guests in the foyer, and a 17-foot-long mosasaur, a giant lizard of the sea, hangs from the living room ceiling. In Southern California, a monstrous Ichthyosaurus adorns the master bathroom of one collector’s house, because the living room is already full of fossils. In Dubai, an 80-foot-long Diplodocus is the star attraction of a shopping mall. And in Santa Barbara, California, one of the best Tyrannosaurus skulls ever found sits in the lobby of a software company, glowering, fangs bared, at the indifferent receptionist seated just opposite. ( Newfound Fossil Octopus and Squid Were Giants) A Triceratops skull (center, in background) and other fossils attract a crowd at the Drouot auction center in Paris. “Many of these people are not buyers,” says photographer Gabr

pages.text: Commercial Loan Service Center - Small Business Administration Skip to content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Home » About SBA » Loan and Guaranty Centers » Commercial Loan Service Center Commercial Loan Service Center Contact the SBA loan center to service commercial loans, process guaranty purchase requests or liquidate debenture and defaulted loans. 7(a) / Express servicing SBA values its 7(a) lenders in diligently servicing and maximizing recoveries on defaulted loans while addressing borrower needs. Service a 7(a) / Express loan CDC / 504 loan servicing Certified Development Companies submit hundreds of unilateral servicing actions to a Commercial Loan Service Center every month. Service a CDC/504 loan Guaranty purchase In some cases, SBA may purchas certain types of guaranteed loans as long as lenders comply with SBA requirements and practices. Submit a Universal Purchase Package 504 liquidations The Commercial Loan Service Center is responsible for the 504 liquidation process and debenture purchase requests. Read the 504 liquidation requirements Post-servicing actions Post-servicing actions consist primarily of Offers in Compromise and Charge Off actions for both Express and 504 loans. Learn more about post-servicing actions 7(a) / Express servicing SBA values its 7(a) lenders in diligently servicing and maximizing recoveries on defaulted loans while addressing borrower needs. Unilateral actions + SBA has substantially shortened the list of actions requiring prior SBA approval and standardized them across lending programs where possible in order to assist lenders in taking prompt and responsible servicing and recovery actions. Please refer to the Servicing and Liquidation Actions 7(a) Lender Matrix for additional information. Lenders must document the business reason and justification for their decisions and retain these and supporting documents, as outlined in SOP 50 57-2 , Chapter 6 and Chapter 8, in the loan file for future SBA review to determine if the actions taken were prudent, commercially reasonable (consistent with generally accepted commercial lending practices) and complied with applicable loan program requirements. When taking action that falls within a lender’s unilateral authority, the lender is encouraged to notate the loan file with a statement such as, “This action was taken under unilateral authority.” (It is recommended that the lenders retain a copy of the matrix in effect at the time of the request and attach it to the action in their file.) It is important to note that if the lender notifies SBA of a change by E-Tran, then a separate notification to the Center is unnecessary. Please email notification of unilateral servicing actions to the Commercial Loan Service Center (CLSC) . When submitting an action to SBA, lenders should reference the ten-digit SBA loan number; lenders will receive confirmation from the servicing center that the servicing request was received. This will be the only communication lenders will receive under the streamlined process for handling unilateral actions. It is very important that lenders notify SBA of all unilateral actions where SBA notification is required so SBA’s loan database can be updated. This is critical for secondary market sales. E-Tran servicing + SBA encourages all lenders to become familiar with and use E-Tran, which permits lenders to make many changes to their SBA loan record using a direct connection via the internet. E-Tran allows lenders to process the following actions without any sort of submission to the SBA: • Cancel undisbursed loan • Terminate guaranty on disbursed loan • Decrease loan amount or guaranty percentage on an undisbursed loan • Change the use of proceeds, which does not involve an increas

pages.title: Reporting Problems with Horse or other Livestock Feed/Food | FDA
pages.description: How to report problems with livestock feed (including horse feed and feed for poultry and aquaculture).
pages.text: Reporting Problems with Horse or other Livestock Feed/Food | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home Animal & Veterinary Safety & Health Report a Problem Reporting Problems with Horse or other Livestock Feed/Food Report a Problem In this section Español FDA encourages horse owners, farmers, veterinarians, and other animal health professionals to report problems with food for livestock (including horses, poultry, and aquaculture). You may report problems by: Submitting an electronic report using the Safety Reporting Portal . Please have as much of the following information available as possible when submitting your complaint: If possible, please save the original packaging until the food has been used up. The packaging contains IMPORTANT information often needed to identify the variety of food, the manufacturing plant, and the production date. For products delivered in bulk, information may be included on the bill of lading, receipt, or invoice. Exact name of the product and product description (as stated on the product label) Type of container (e.g., bag, bale, block, bulk, drum, etc.) Lot number - This number is often hard to find and difficult to read. It is stamped onto the product packaging and typically includes a combination of letters and numbers, and is always in close proximity to the best by/before or expiration date (if the product has a best by/before or expiration date). The lot number is very important as it helps us determine the manufacturing plant as well as the production date. Best by, best before or expiration date UPC code (also known as the bar code) Net weight Purchase date and location Results of laboratory tests performed on the product or on the animals, if any How the food was stored, prepared, and handled Description of the problem with the product. Examples include: Foul odor, off color, inconsistent texture Foreign material found in the product. If you think animals have become sick or injured as a result of consuming a specific food, you may also provide information about the animals, including: Species (e.g., horse, cattle, swine, poultry, fish, other) Age, weight, breed, production, pregnancy, lactation status and housing Previous health status of the animals including any known pre-existing conditions Other foods, or drugs the animals received Clinical signs observed (e.g., diarrhea, lethargy, staggering) How soon after consuming the product the clinical signs appeared Your veterinarian or other consulted professional’s contact information, diagnosis and medical records How many animals consuming the product were affected and how many were not Why you suspect the product caused the illness Content current as of: 05/18/2026 Feedback Back to Top

pages.title: Como entender su aviso CP87A (SP) | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Le enviamos este aviso porque recibimos una declaración de impuestos de otro contribuyente que reclama un hijo a cargo o calificado con el mismo número de Seguro Social que un hijo a cargo o calificado que aparece en su declaración de impuestos. Los últimos cuatro dígitos del número del Seguro Social para cada hijo dependiente o calificado que nos preocupa se muestran en el aviso para su revisión.
pages.text: Como entender su aviso CP87A (SP) | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Como entender su aviso CP87A (SP) English Español Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) De qué trata este aviso Recibimos una declaración de impuestos de otro contribuyente que reclama un hijo a cargo o calificado con el mismo número de Seguro Social que un hijo a cargo o calificado que aparece en su declaración de impuestos. Enumeramos los últimos cuatro dígitos del número de Seguro Social para cada hijo dependiente o calificado que nos preocupa en el aviso para su revisión. Lo que usted debe hacer Compare los números del Seguro Social de su aviso con los de la tarjeta del Seguro Social para cada hijo dependiente o calificado que usted incluyó en su declaración de impuestos. Revise las reglas para reclamar cada hijo dependiente o calificado. Después de revisar las reglas: Si encuentra que tiene derecho a reclamar al dependiente, no necesita escribirnos ni enviarnos nada. Si usted encuentra a alguien en la lista que no califica como su hijo dependiente o calificado, tiene que corregir su declaración presentando un Formulario 1040-X, Declaración Enmendada del Impuesto Estadounidense Sobre los Ingresos Personales . Las instrucciones de este formulario le guiarán a través de los pasos para corregir su declaración. Envíe su declaración enmendada al centro de servicio del Servicio de Impuestos Internos ( IRS , por sus siglas en inglés) que aparece en las instrucciones. Tal vez desee Revisar este aviso con su preparador de impuestos si utilizó uno. Revisar las reglas para reclamar un hijo dependiente o calificado en la Publicación 501, Dependientes, Deducción Estándar e Información de Presentación (en inglés) . Guarde este aviso para sus registros. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Quién es la otra persona que reclamó al mismo dependiente que yo en su declaración de impuestos? (actualizada el 30 de enero de 2025) Las leyes de divulgación nos prohíben revelar el nombre del contribuyente que utilizó el mismo número de Seguro Social que su hijo dependiente o calificado. ¿Qué pasa si los números de la tarjeta del Seguro Social y mi aviso no coinciden? (actualizada el 30 de enero de 2025) Usted utilizó un número de Seguro Social incorrecto en su declaración original que duplicó uno utilizado en otra declaración. No necesita ponerse en contacto con nosotros ni tomar ninguna acción. Asegúrese de utilizar el número de Seguro Social correcto en su próxima declaración de impuestos. ¿Qué pasa si los números de la tarjeta del Seguro Social y mi aviso coinciden? (actualizada el 30 de enero de 2025) Revise las reglas acerca de lo que califica a alguien como hijo dependiente o calificado porque puede estar incluyendo a alguien que no califica. Si determina que reclamó incorrectamente al hijo dependiente o calificado, es posible que necesite corregir (enmendar) su declaración de impuestos presentando un Formulario 1040-X (en inglés) PDF . ¿Qué necesito enviar para demostrar que tengo derecho a reclamar el hijo dependiente o calificado? En este momento no necesita tomar ninguna acción ni enviarnos ningún documento. ¿Qué pasa si no presenté una declaración de impuestos reclamando el hijo a cargo o calificado y otra persona está usando mi nombre y número de Seguro Social? (actualizada el 30 de enero de 2025) Contáctenos al número que aparece en su aviso. También puede consultar la página central de robo de identidad del IRS para obtener más información. ¿Qué reglas aplican cuando otra persona reclama el mismo número de Seguro Social que el hijo dependiente o calificado que reclamé? pages.text: 隐私通告 | 联合国 Skip to main content 隐私通告 UN.ORG数据保护和隐私通告 本声明适用于UN.ORG域名下的所有网站(“联合国各网站”)。联合国重视您的隐私，也重视个人数据保护。本数据保护和隐私声明介绍了联合国关于通过联合国各网站收集和共享个人数据的政策。访问联合国某网站，即表示您接受这一政策中所述的做法。 秘书长公报 联合国各网站遵循着一套关于个人数据保护和隐私的原则，它们由秘书长关于联合国秘书处的数据保护和隐私政策的公报( ST/SGB/2024/3 )确立。 联合国收集哪些信息？ 网站正常使用 一般来说，您可以浏览联合国某网站，而无需说明自己的身份或透露自己的任何个人信息。 我们的系统在一般浏览过程中自动收集访客的一些匿名信息。其中包括网络技术信息，比如您上网显示的IP(互联网协议)地址、域名、当前使用的浏览器类型、操作系统以及其他信息，比如自哪个网站跳转到联合国某网站、从联合国各网站下载的文件、在联合国各网站浏览过的页面、访问联合国各网站的日期/时间。 联合国各网站会不时使用第三方提供的网站分析服务，以评估联合国各网站的使用情况，面向网站运营商和要求传送相关统计报告的政府间机构编制网络活动报告，提供与网站活动和互联网使用有关的其他服务。由该等第三方收集的信息，包括您的IP地址会存储在该等第三方的服务器上，受该等第三方自身的隐私政策和适用的任何法律法规约束。 个人数据 联合国各网站仅在您知情的前提下收集个人数据。 您在订阅通讯稿、登录联合国特定网站、订购书籍或其他商品、索要信息、提供反馈、申请工作、加入讨论群组或电子邮件列表时，可能会被要求提供个人信息，比如姓名、邮政地址和(或)电子邮件地址。 加入电子讨论群组可能意味着讨论群组的其他参与者(包括非联合国职员)会看到您自愿提供的个人信息。就公开讨论群组而言，此类信息是公开的。 当您进行交易比如订购商品或预约参观联合国总部时，也可能被要求提供详细的信用卡信息。该等详细信息将传输到由第三方托管的安全在线支付服务平台。联合国不保留信用卡信息。 Cookies(小型文本文件) 联合国各网站可能使用cookies来抓取统计数据，以此帮助为您提供最佳网站体验。 联合国如何处理收集的信息？ 网站正常使用 在一般浏览联合国网站期间，用“cookies”或“网络信标”自动收集信息。与互联网连接有关的IP地址和访问的网页等信息被用来分析联合国各网站的趋势和使用情况，提高网站的实用性。您的IP地址与任何个人数据之间没有关联。 个人数据 联合国可能将您提供的个人数据用于收集个人数据所要达到的目的，比如： 与您联系——回应查询或建议，或者寄送通讯稿、文件、出版物等； 管理和处理您的工作申请； 确认您在网站上进行的购买和注册； 要求您(通过信用卡)为网上购买的物品付款； “记住”您的线上个人资料和偏好； 帮助您根据自身兴趣迅速搜寻对您适用的信息，帮助我们创建与您最为切合的网站内容； 开展统计分析。 如果我不想提供个人数据呢？ 你可选择是否在联合国网站上提供个人数据。如果你不提供个人数据，你可能无法进行某些操作，例如购买物品、注册通讯或申请工作。 不想提供个人数据怎么办？ 在联合国某网站提供个人数据不是强制的。如果您选择不提供个人数据，可能会无法执行特定操作，比如购买物品、订阅通讯稿或申请工作。 联合国如何保护您的个人数据？ 我们从不出售经由联合国各网站收集的任何信息。我们通常不会与任何第三方分享联合国网站上收集的任何个人数据，但这不包括安全传输给第三方服务提供商的信息，比如在联合国某网站购物所涉及的信用卡处理商。我们采用一系列技术和安全措施来保护自有系统上留存的信息，以防止信息的丢失、滥用、未经授权访问或披露、更改或破坏。 掌握个人数据访问权限、涉及个人数据处理业务的联合国所有工作人员均有义务遵守联合国所有数据的分类和处理规则，包括以公务身份经手的个人数据保密规则。其中囊括了 ST/SGB/2024/3 里面的规则。 联合国把您的个人数据保留多长时间？ 我们仅在为实现本声明所载目的所必须的期限内保留您的个人数据。个人信息的存储期限取决于所涉及的个人信息和用途，以及有无任何关于保留个人信息的行政或监管要求。 pages.text: mapeadora's Diary | Ten Years After São Paulo: A Chronicle of a State of the Map LATAM at Home (SotM LATAM 2026, Mexico City) | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close mapeadora's Diary Ten Years After São Paulo: A Chronicle of a State of the Map LATAM at Home (SotM LATAM 2026, Mexico City) Posted by mapeadora on 7 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 8 November 2026. Ten years ago, I attended my first State of the Map LATAM in São Paulo, thanks to a travel grant. Until then, for me, OpenStreetMap was just the group we’d formed in Mexico out of the legendary Rancho Electrónico, Mexico City’s hackerspace. During those days, I discovered it was so much more: a regional community, with faces, stories, perspectives, and generosity. I understood why these in-person gatherings matter so much. They gave rise to friendships that have lasted a decade—sometimes in person and mostly online—and I believe that through these networks we’ve accomplished important things. From that very first time, together with other women, we also decided to promote inclusion and diversity in the community, and that’s how Geochicas was born. That’s why, when I decided to lead the Mexican edition, I did so with great enthusiasm. It was a whole year of intense emotions, thinking about bringing well-known figures and new people from across the region to my city, happy at the idea that they would experience the city at its best and, hopefully, learn more about its cultural details. A priority from the very beginning was to secure enough sponsorship to fund a significant number of scholarships, allowing even those from the most distant countries in the Southern Cone to attend. More than half of the funds went toward scholarships. Some scholarships could not be used due to visa issues, but the effort was worth it. There were 272 attendees, 113 of whom were women, and three days of technical, community, and personal exchange, with affordable food and drinks. We also wanted the event to be inclusive: there was a quiet room and a workspace for those who needed a break, to relieve stress, or to concentrate. We made a conscious choice to hold it in the Historic Center, at Patio Chico, UNAM: we wanted it to be more than just a conference, but an experience with maximum interaction among people. And it coincided with the Day of the Dead, when the entire city beats to the same rhythm of empathy and remembrance, with open hearts to honor those we have loved. It was beautiful to see so many people discover this cultural tradition and experience new emotions. It was also a very intense intellectual and practical gathering: new technologies, methods, and mapping topics, building on the work done in Belén and Medellín while introducing its own innovations. A self-organized, women-led event The event was led by women. Many people participated, but we devoted all our energy to it for a year, with the intensity building as we neared the end. Let’s make it normal to recognize those who contribute the most and who, because their efforts are so all-consuming, don’t get to appear in photos or speak into the microphone. None of this would have been possible without Yasmila (Mila) Saenz Herrera, who played a central role in organizing the last two SotMs here: together, we made it happen. Thanks also to: Miriam Gonzalez-Sanchez, for securing the sponsorships, which were essential to everything. Adriana Ávila Farfán and Andrea Berrocal, from UNAM-Patio Lab. Zeltzin Palacios and her UAM community. Alma Rangel Macías, from Codeando México. Sandra Lucía Hernández Zetina, Benita Hernández Carbajal, and the volunteers from UAEMex, who handled all the logistics. And many more. A thousand thanks to our partners: the UNAM General Directorate for the Dissemination of Science, Patio Lab, the Autonomous University of the State of Mexico, and SEDATU (Secretariat of Agrarian, Territorial, and Urban Development). Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/publications/leveraging-undergraduate-mathematics-and-physics-curriculum-strengthen-advanced PUBLICATIONS Leveraging the Undergraduate Mathematics and Physics Curriculum to Strengthen the Advanced Manufacturing Workforce Pipeline Published November 10, 2026 Author(s) Treena Basu , Brad Conrad , Aaron Bell, Jeremiah Forshey, Robert Foy, Ashley Smith-Schoettker, Joseph Long Abstract This report provides faculty with advanced manufacturing terminology and data to articulate the occupational relevance of their teachings, without changing curriculum. The MFG USA Competency Framework can be used to make mathematics and physics certifications more accessible to employers and hiring managers. Undergraduate mathematics and physics courses develop abstraction, modeling under constraints, and reasoning with uncertainty, which are skills applicable to a wide range of advanced manufacturing career pathways. The academic language used to describe these skills can make it challenging for employers to interpret academic course relevance in the competency-based terms more familiar to industry. To address this systemic issue, the Manufacturing USA Advanced Manufacturing Occupation and Competency Framework (MFG USA Competency Framework) provides an industry-validated framework that outlines occupations, competencies, and knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSAs) in advanced manufacturing. By mapping the skills developed in familiar undergraduate coursework onto the framework's industry-wide and sector-specific competencies, this analysis highlights relevant connections between academic training and entry-level advanced manufacturing roles—connections that are often implicit to faculty but not immediately apparent to hiring managers, workers, and employers. pages.description: Para reducir su riesgo de cáncer de piel, proteja su piel del sol y evite el bronceado.

Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. 29 agosto del 2024 English (US) Concientización sobre el cáncer de piel Qué necesita saber La exposición excesiva a los rayos ultravioleta (UV) causa la mayoría de los casos de melanoma, el tipo de cáncer de piel más mortal. Para reducir su riesgo de cáncer de piel, proteja su piel del sol y evite el bronceado en interiores. Vistazo El verano está lleno de actividades al aire libre. Probablemente usted se pone filtro solar y se lo pone a sus hijos cuando van a la piscina o a la playa. Pero, ¿sabía que debe proteger su piel con algo más que el filtro solar cada vez que está al aire libre? La protección solar es importante durante todo el año, y lo mejor es usar varios tipos diferentes. Cuando esté trabajando en el jardín, viendo un evento deportivo o caminando por la tarde, haga que la protección solar sea un hábito diario para que pueda evitar las quemaduras solares y reducir su probabilidad de tener cáncer de piel. La seguridad frente al sol Video en baja resolución Este video explica cómo proteger su piel del sol. ¿Qué lleva en su bolso de playa? Aquí le ofrecemos un consejo para ayudar a que usted y su familia estén protegidos del sol. Prepárese para el verano con un bolso de playa lleno de cosas que lo ayuden a protegerse de varias formas. Mantenga el bolso a la mano para que lo pueda agarrar cuando salga a disfrutar las actividades del verano. ¡Haga que la protección solar sea un hábito diario! Proteja su piel del sol y evite el bronceado en interiors para reducir su riesgo. Estas son algunas cosas importantes que debe empacar: Una camisa liviana de manga larga o una salida de baño. Un sombrero de ala ancha que le proteja la cara, la cabeza, las orejas y el cuello. Lentes de sol que bloqueen tanto los rayos UVA como los UVB. Filtro solar con factor de protección (FPS) de 15 o más alto y que ofrezca protección contra los rayos UVA y los rayos UVB (protección de amplio espectro). Más consejos para protegerse del sol Busque la sombra, especialmente desde las últimas horas de la mañana hasta media tarde. ¿No puede quedarse en la sombra? Vístase con una camisa de manga larga y pantalones para proteger su piel. Recuerde volver a aplicarse filtro solar como mínimo cada 2 horas y después de nadar, sudar o secarse. Datos breves sobre el cáncer de piel El cáncer de piel es el cáncer más común en los Estados Unidos, e incluye diferentes tipos. Los rayos del sol pueden dañar la piel desprotegida en solo 15 minutos. Aunque el día esté fresco y nublado, usted necesita protección solar. Son los rayos del sol, no la temperatura, lo que causa el daño. Cualquier persona puede tener cáncer de piel, pero algunos factores lo ponen en mayor riesgo. Los signos más comunes de cáncer de piel son los cambios como la aparición de un bulto nuevo, tener una llaga que no sana o tener un lunar que cambia de aspecto. pages.text: The American flag and other national symbols | USAGov Skip to main content The American flag and other national symbols Get the facts about the U.S. flag and when to fly it at half staff. Learn about other national symbols. History of the American flag The flag of the United States is a symbol of freedom before which Americans recite the pledge of allegiance . The flag's 13 red and white stripes represent the 13 original colonies. Its 50 white stars on a blue background represent the 50 states. Each of the colors on the flag has a meaning: Red: valor and bravery White: purity and innocence Blue: vigilance, perseverance, and justice A star is added to the flag when a new state joins the United States. The flag was last modified on July 4, 1960, when Hawaii was incorporated as a state. Learn more about the evolution of the American flag and its earlier designs. How to raise the flag Follow these guidelines to properly display the American flag [PDF, 162KB]. When to fly the flag at half-staff The American flag flies at half-staff or at half-mast when the country or a state is in mourning. The president, a state governor, or the mayor of the District of Columbia can order flags to fly at half-staff. In most cases, an American flag flying at half-staff marks one of three observances: The death of a government official, military member, or emergency first responder A national tragedy Memorial Day or another national day of remembrance The Great Seal The Great Seal of the United States is a national symbol used in official documents such as treaties and commissions. The final design was approved in 1782 and includes a bald eagle, an olive branch, arrows, a flag-like shield, the motto E Pluribus Unum (which translates to "out of many, one") and a constellation of stars. Learn more about the Great Seal. The bald eagle The bald eagle was designated as the national emblem by the U.S. Congress in 1782. Since then, it can be found on official documents, the presidential flag, the Great Seal, military insignia, and coins and bills. Learn more about the bald eagle [PDF, 66KB]. pages.title: Pat McFadden backs legal right to job support for young people British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The work and pensions secretary said the level of support currently on offer was too vague.
pages.text: Pat McFadden backs legal right to job support for young people Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Minister backs legal right to job support for young people 1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Paul Seddon Political reporter Watch: Pat McFadden refuses to rule out that some young people might lose benefits The work and pensions secretary has backed the idea that the government should legally guarantee young people help to get into employment. Pat McFadden told the BBC that job support should be given a "legislative underpinning", adding the level of assistance on offer was currently "vague". McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed. But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers. It comes ahead of a long-awaited review by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn, which will recommend on Tuesday that under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work. His report is also expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to health conditions, under the plans. Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Milburn said the government should divert money away from the benefits system to boost work support, adding he wanted to see "billions" extra spent on help over the next decade. However, the idea of reducing the entitlement of existing benefit claimants could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who scuppered a previous benefits-cutting plan under Sir Keir Starmer last year. Milburn said the reduced entitlement for some should be accompanied by a new "duty on government" to provide jobs support to young people, such as apprenticeships, college places, job coaching, or a job. He added that the temporary nature of previous job support schemes, including the Kickstart programme during the Covid pandemic, meant that they had been less effective as reducing long-term joblessness. How the new guarantee would work in practice is not yet clear, with McFadden adding it would have to be "carefully" drafted. Although local councils have some specific legal duties, including in the areas of child protection and homelessness, duties on central government currently tend to be much broader, such as operating a "comprehensive" health service. Watch: Helen Whately says legal guarantee of work or training for under-25s 'doesn't make sense' Asked on the same programme whether he agreed with the idea of a guarantee, McFadden said: "I do think we need some legislative underpinning to this." He added that the offer of support "needs to be more firm," adding: "People need more certainty about what they are entitled to." He confirmed that the government planned to move younger claimants onto a new benefits system when they undergo scheduled reassessment, and some of them would not receive "what they would get today". Other claimants, such as those with long-term disabilities, would receive an increased amount, he added. Also speaking to Kuenssberg, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said her party backed moves to reduce welfare spending. But she criticised the proposed legal guarantee of work support, arguing it might "sound a nice thing to do," but ministers would be better off reducing taxes and regulations on businesses to help youngsters find "real jobs". Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions Celebrate OHV Safety Week at Indian Valley Management Area California Media Contact BLM California BLM_CA_Press@blm.gov BLM Office: Ukiah Field Office November 9, 2026 UKIAH, Calif. – The Bureau of Land Management Ukiah Field Office and partners invite the public to celebrate OHV Safety Week at the Indian Valley Management Area on Saturday, Nov. 14, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. This free, family-friendly event is open to everyone, and no registration is required. The event begins at 10 a.m. at the Walker Ridge Day Use Area, located just north of the State Highway 20/Walker Ridge Junction. Staff and volunteers will be available to answer questions and discuss ways visitors can enjoy off-highway vehicle recreation while riding safely and responsibly. Visitors can learn about OHV safety, first aid tips, responsible riding practices and available training opportunities. Free trail maps, safety checklists, information about current land use regulations and brochures highlighting the area and responsible recreation practices will also be available. Light refreshments will be provided. All attendees will receive BLM OHV and fire educational material as a thank you for attending. Participants are encouraged to bring snacks or sack lunch, sun protection, and any required off-highway vehicle safety gear. North of State Highway 20, on the eastern edge of Lake County, the Indian Valley Management Area offers an abundance of recreational possibilities. Rolling chaparral covered hills dotted with oak and pine make an ideal setting for hunting, camping, bicycling, hiking, and equestrian use. Popular game animals include blacktail deer, black bear, quail, dove, and wild turkey. For wildflower enthusiasts, pockets of the rare Indian Valley Brodiaea and Adobe Lily can be found within the area. There are numerous routes offering majestic views of the area. Visitors are reminded to stay within designated riding areas, respect other recreationists, and use extra caution when traveling on foot near OHV routes. The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

GHGRP Reported Data For reporting year (RY) 2023, over 8,000 facilities and suppliers reported to the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP). Among these reporters, 7,544 facilities in nine industry sectors reported direct emissions; Reported direct emissions totaled 2.58 billion metric tons carbon dioxide equivalent (CO 2 e); 995 suppliers of fossil fuels and industrial gases reported; and 81 facilities reported injecting CO 2 underground (Subpart UU). Figure 1: Direct GHG Emissions Reported by Sector (2023) Select chart view By Emissions By Number of Facilities Click on legend items below the chart to show or hide sectors. View this information in FLIGHT . GHGRP Data Highlights Summary Sections View Emissions Trends View Emissions by GHG View Emissions by Location View Emissions Ranges Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program Background Download Overview Profile View All Sector Profiles Background information about GHGRP has been broken into several sections on this page. These sections include: GHGRP Calculation Methods Used Report Verification For More Information All greenhouse gas data presented here reflect the information reported to EPA as of August 16, 2024. The reported emissions exclude biogenic CO 2 . GHG data displayed are in units of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO 2 e) and reflect the global warming potential (GWP) values from Table A-1 , which is generally based on the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change ( IPCC)’s Fourth Assessment Report (AR4) . The GWPs for some fluorinated GHGs that did not have GWPs in the AR4 are from the IPCC’s Fifth Assessment Report. As directed by Congress, EPA’s Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) collects annual greenhouse gas information from the top emitting sectors of the U.S. economy (Table 1). The GHGRP is the only dataset containing facility-level greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions data from large industrial sources across the United States. With 13 consecutive years of reporting for most sectors, GHGRP data are providing important new information on industrial emissions—showing variation in emissions across facilities within an industry, variation in industrial emissions across geographic areas, and changes in emissions over time at the sector and facility level. EPA is using this facility-level data to improve estimates of national greenhouse gas emissions in the U.S. Greenhouse Gas Inventory . This document summarizes national industrial sector emissions and trends. The GHGRP does not represent total U.S. GHG emissions, but provides facility level data for large sources of direct emissions, thus representing the majority of U.S. GHG emissions. The GHGRP data collected from direct emitters represent about half of all U.S. emissions. When including greenhouse gas information reported to the GHGRP by suppliers, emissions coverage reaches approximately 85–90% (See Figure 2). The Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks: 1990-2022 contains information on all GHG emissions sources and sinks in the United States. Learn more about the differences between the Inventory and the GHGRP . Figure 2: U.S. Greenhouse Gas Inventory and the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program Suppliers report the quantity of GHGs that would be emitted if the fuels and industrial GHGs that they place into the economy each year are used/released. Reporting by suppliers helps account for the greenhouse gas emissions by the numerous low-emitting sources that are not required to report emissions under the GHGRP (e.g., mobile sources, residential sources). Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/publications/us-manufacturing-trends-performance-and-competitiveness-annual-report-manufacturing PUBLICATIONS U.S. Manufacturing Trends, Performance, and Competitiveness: Annual Report on the Manufacturing Economy, 2026 Published November 9, 2026 Author(s) Douglas Thomas Abstract This report provides a statistical review of the U.S. manufacturing industry. There are three aspects of U.S. manufacturing that are considered: (1) how the U.S. industry compares to other countries, (2) the trends in the domestic industry, and (3) the industry trends compared to those in other countries. The report discusses forecasts for U.S. manufacturing and provides means for advancing national manufacturing competitiveness. Eight primary means for advancing U.S. competitiveness are identified. They organize into four pillars: Target, Accelerate, Learn, and Protect. The eight methods provide a systematic approach to advancing manufacturing competitiveness by focusing resources where they can generate the greatest returns. pages.title: Shoplifting measures welcomed by Birmingham traders British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Business owners say they are losing thousands of pounds and help is "well overdue".
pages.text: Shoplifting measures welcomed by Birmingham traders Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Shoplifting measures welcomed by traders 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Bob Hockenhull West Midlands Getty Images The government pilot in the West Midlands will focus on prolific offenders Shopkeepers in the West Midlands have welcomed the announcement of new measures to cut shoplifting. The region is one of 16 police force areas chosen as part of a government pilot to target prolific retail offenders, which could see persistent thieves tagged and banned from high streets. Mani Gill, vice-chair of the Soho Road Business Improvement District (BID), Birmingham, said shoplifting was a daily occurrence, with small businesses least able to absorb the costs. Alex Goss, lead for retail crime at the National Police Chief's Council , said he welcomed the pilot to tackle prolific retail crime offenders "who continue to cause harm to businesses, retail workers and local communities". The new measures announced by the Home Secretary on Wednesday will focus on about 500 of the country's most prolific offenders, who the government said were "responsible for a disproportionate amount of shop theft". It said they could face restrictions on their movements including the use of GPS tags, along with being banned from the high street. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "A small number of offenders commit a disproportionate amount of shop theft. "They wreak havoc on our high streets, leave businesses out of pocket and make retail workers scared to go to work." The 12-month, £2.5m pilot will also look at the "drivers of offending" including drug and alcohol addiction. Goss said the pilot would give police forces and their partners "additional support to tackle some of the most prolific retail crime offenders". A recent BBC investigation found that 28,415 recorded offences had been linked to just 270 suspects between 2020-21 and 2025-26. Amjad Farook said his staff had been assaulted by shoplifters Amjad Farook, who runs the Wah Wah Mirchi grocery store said his staff had been attacked and help was "well overdue". Farook said he was losing thousands of pounds and thieves were targetting his store on a weekly basis. The majority of items taken were high-value, he said, but they could range down to packets of butter or spices. He said he suggests his staff do not physically confront thieves, but just make sure they know they are being watched. But he said sometimes thieves become violent. He said: "One member of our staff got attacked the other week and he was bleeding, it wasn't a nice thing. It is a worrying thought for my staff." 'People becoming desperate' Gill said Soho Road was suffering just the same as anywhere else and the problem of shoplifting was increasing. He said most of the businesses the BID represents are small businesses and for them it was "harder to digest because their pockets aren't as large". He said getting to the root of the problem was important and any government support should make sure it was not just moving the problem somewhere else. "I think with the cost of living and people struggling to make ends meet... I do think that people are getting more desperate," he said. Mani Gill said smaller shops were less able to absorb the cost of shoplifting Simon Roberts, Sainsbury's chief executive, said retail crime was a "national emergency which requires a national response and targeted action from government and police against the prolific offenders". He said more arrests and prosecutions were needed. Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the British Retail Consortium, said retailers welcomed the pilot and approved of "robust enforcement with targeted support to tackle the root causes". Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM and USWFS Launch Prescribed Burn Season in Central California Reducing wildfire risk and improving the health of public lands California Media Contact BLM California BLM_CA_Press@blm.gov BLM Office: Central California District Office November 9, 2026 EL DORADO HILLS, Calif. — The Bureau of Land Management and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service will begin prescribed fire operations throughout Amador, Calaveras, El Dorado, Mariposa, Nevada, Placer, Sacramento, Stanislaus, Tuolumne, and Yuba counties as weather, fuel, and air quality become favorable. Operations will start as early as Nov. 10 and will continue throughout the fall and winter. These treatments are carefully planned to reduce hazardous fuels, protect nearby communities, and restore native ecosystems. Information about specific upcoming and active burns is available online . Techniques range from broadcast burning, which is the application of fire to an entire area, to hand and machine pile ignitions. These burns focus on increasing safety in the wildland-urban interface and restoring ecological function to the landscape. Targeting built-up fuels and residual materials from previous thinning operations decreases the load of dead trees, branches, and underbrush that pose significant wildfire risks. What the public should know Smoke may be visible from nearby communities and to motorists traveling near project areas while prescribed fire operations are underway. Smoke may settle in low-lying areas overnight. Residents are encouraged to close windows at night to avoid smoke impacts. When driving in smoky areas, drivers should slow down and turn on headlights. People with heart or lung disease, asthma or other chronic conditions should ask their doctors about protecting themselves from smoke and monitor their local air quality map. Burns are conducted only when weather, fuel and air quality conditions are within established parameters. Firefighters use natural features and constructed control lines to keep prescribed fire contained and minimize smoke impacts on nearby communities. All burns are carried out when weather, fuel conditions, and air quality are within specific parameters. Firefighters use a combination of natural features and constructed control lines to keep the fire contained, with protocols in place to minimize smoke impacts on nearby communities. For more information, contact the BLM Mother Lode Field Office at (916) 941-3101, BLM_CA_Web_ML@blm.gov . The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
