pages.title: CESER and Idaho National Laboratory are Testing Power Transformers Against Earthquakes | Department of Energy Lock
pages.description: INL is conducting the first ever seismic testing on electric grid equipment to determine how transformers perform during an earthquake.
pages.text: CESER and Idaho National Laboratory are Testing Power Transformers Against Earthquakes | Department of Energy Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Blog CESER and Idaho National Laboratory are Testing Power Transformers Against Earthquakes INL is conducting the first ever seismic testing on electric grid equipment to determine how transformers perform during an earthquake. Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response September 29, 2026 Estimated Read Time min The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) and Office of Electricity (OE) have partnered with Idaho National Laboratory (INL) to conduct the first ever seismic testing on an operational 230-kV power transformer. Testing will take place at the University of California San Diego’s Large High-Performance Outdoor Shake Table (LHPOST)—the world's most powerful earthquake simulator. CESER and OE’s seismic testing work aligns with President Trump’s executive order on “ Achieving Efficiency Through State and Local Preparedness ,” which highlights making U.S. infrastructure, communities, and economy resilient to global and dynamic threats and hazards. Critical infrastructure can be impacted when earthquakes hit, and among the most vital and vulnerable components of the U.S. electric grid are large power transformers. Replacing a damaged full-scale transformer can take five years or more. If several transformers are damaged during an earthquake, entire communities could be left without power for months, immobilizing hospitals, water supply systems, and emergency response. “Securing the U.S. electric grid against all hazards, including extreme seismic events, is fundamental to national security,” said CESER Director Andrew McClure. “This pioneering research will allow us to strengthen transformer design, mitigate vulnerabilities, and ensure our critical energy systems can endure major earthquakes.” INL’s seismic testing will provide insight into how transformers behave during an earthquake: Seismic testing will allow INL to observe an operational transformer during earthquake conditions. Engineers can then accurately model and predict an earthquake event, allowing them to optimize future designs and update seismic specifications for high-risk zones. Bushings, critical insulators that carry electrical connections through the transformer, are the most common transformer component damaged during an earthquake. Seismic testing will enable INL to evaluate a new decoupler retrofit designed to relieve stress on bushings during an earthquake. Evidence suggests base isolation can significantly reduce seismic risk across vulnerable components; however, it has never been tested on a transformer. Seismic testing will put this concept to the test under real-world scale and weight constraints. Seismic testing data will inform the Simulated Ground Motion Database (SGMD) , which provides public access to important earthquake simulation data. Testing results will also play a significant role in guiding grid equipment designs and strengthening earthquake mitigation strategies. Visit INL’s website to learn more about this project. pages.description: Actúe ahora para denunciar, prevenir y recuperarse del robo de identidad relacionado con impuestos.
pages.text: Guía de robo de identidad para personas físicas | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Guía de robo de identidad para personas físicas English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Personas físicas Negocios (en inglés) Profesionales de impuestos (en inglés) Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) Actúe ahora para denunciar, prevenir y recuperarse del robo de identidad relacionado con impuestos. Aprenda cómo proteger su información para que nadie pueda obtener su reembolso, presentar una declaración en su nombre o acceder a su cuenta en línea. En esta página Pasos que puede seguir ahora Si recibió una carta del IRS, una notificación o un fax Señales de advertencia Consejos para la prevención Permítanos ayudarlo Pasos que puede seguir ahora Si le robaron su identidad: Deje de interactuar con el ladrón de su identidad. Cuelgue. No les de dinero ni información personal o financiera. No haga clic en enlaces, no abra archivos adjuntos ni vaya a páginas de internet con direcciones extrañas o que no conoce. Si lo hizo, utilice un software antivirus. Actualiza su contraseña de su cuenta en línea para persona físicas . Genere una contraseña compleja y única. Siga las instrucciones del IRS de su carta, aviso o representante. Denuncie el robo de identidad . Siga los pasos de recuperación en RobodeIdentidad.gov . Obtenga un PIN para la protección de identidad (IP PIN, por sus siglas en ingles) para proteger su cuenta de impuestos. Mantenga registros de cartas, llamadas telefónicas y correos electrónicos. Presente declaraciones y pague impuestos como siempre. Consulte con su agencia estatal tributaria (en inglés) para conocer otros pasos. Tome medidas adicionales para tipos específicos de robo de identidad: Robo de identidad de persona fallecida Presente la declaración o declaraciones de impuestos finales de la persona fallecida (en inglés) cuando corresponda. Envíe a las agencias de crédito una copia del certificado de defunción. Para que active una “alerta de fallecido” en los informes de crédito. Monitore los informes para detectar actividades inusuales. Evite poner demasiada información en un obituario que los ladrones de identidad podrían usar. Robo de identidad del dependiente Un dependiente es un hijo o pariente calificado que depende de usted para obtener apoyo financiero. Su información puede ser utilizada para obtener un crédito tributario. Si le robaron la identidad de su dependiente: Actúe ahora . Compruebe si debe presentar el Formulario 14039, Declaración Jurada sobre el Robo de Identidad . Si su dependiente fue reclamado en otra declaración en el mismo año tributario: Podría deberse a un malentendido, error o delito como robo de identidad o fraude: Antes de presentar una declaración, determine quién puede reclamar al dependiente (en inglés) . Asegúrese que la información del dependiente este correcta en la declaración. Si recibió un rechazo de su presentación electrónica ( e-file ), aún puede presentar su declaración electrónicamente ( e-file ). A partir de las declaraciones del año 2024, el IRS aceptará los Formularios 1040, 1040-NR y 1040-SS presentados electrónicamente ( e-file ), incluso si ya se ha reclamado a un dependiente. Si el contribuyente principal de la segunda declaración incluye un número de identidad personal para la protección de la identidad ( IP PIN , por sus siglas en inglés) válido, la declaración no será rechazada por duplicidad de dependientes. El dependiente no necesita un IP PIN , a menos que se le haya emitido uno previamente. pages.description: A calculator that allows users to translate abstract greenhouse gas amounts into concrete terms that are easy to understand.
pages.text: Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator | US EPA Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator Convert emissions or energy data into concrete terms you can understand — such as the annual CO 2 emissions of cars, households, and power plants. The Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies calculator allows you to convert emissions or energy data to the equivalent amount of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions from using that amount . The calculator helps you translate abstract measurements into concrete terms you can understand, such as the annual emissions from cars, households, or power plants. This calculator may be useful in communicating your greenhouse gas reduction strategy, reduction targets, or other initiatives aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Updated November 2024 These estimates are approximate and should not be used for emission inventories or formal carbon emissions analysis. See Calculations & References for equations and sources used. Step 1 - Enter and convert data Select data to convert: There are two options for entering data into this calculator: energy data or emissions data . When you enter energy data, the calculator converts these values into carbon dioxide-equivalent greenhouse gas emissions based on emission factors for energy consumption or electricity reductions. Then, it provides equivalent ways to express those emissions. When you enter emissions data, the calculator provides equivalent ways to express those emissions. Energy data For electricity, the calculator uses different emissions factors depending on whether the electricity is avoided or consumed. The calculator uses a non-baseload emissions factor for avoided electricity and an average emissions factor for electricity consumption. It then displays equivalent ways to express those emissions. See the Calculations & References . Emissions data Enter data: Unit Amount Gallons of gasoline Gasoline-powered passenger vehicles While passenger vehicles are not a unit of energy consumption, they do consume energy. For the calculator’s purposes, passenger vehicles are defined as 2-axle 4-tire vehicles, including passenger cars, vans, pickup trucks, and sport/utility vehicles. To see the methodology used to determine annual greenhouse gas emissions per passenger vehicle, visit the Calculations & References page for equations and sources used. Kilowatt-hours avoided Kilowatt-hours used MCF of natural gas Therms of natural gas Enter ZIP Code for regional weighted marginal emission rate (lb/MWh) Please enter a valid 5-digit zip code so the calculator can estimate emissions avoided using an emissions factor specific to your region. If you don’t enter a ZIP code or you enter an invalid ZIP code, the calculator will use a national average avoided emissions rate, which may not be accurate for your region. Please enter a valid 5-digit zip code so the calculator can estimate emissions using an emissions factor specific to your region. If you don’t enter a ZIP code or you enter an invalid ZIP code, the calculator will use a national average emissions rate, which may not be accurate for your location. We could not find your ZIP code in our database. The calculator will use the national weighted marginal emission rate (lb/MWh) value. Convert data * The Equivalencies Calculator uses different emissions factors for electricity depending on whether it is avoided or consumed; at typical scales, energy efficiency and renewable energy programs and projects do not affect baseload power generation, so the calculator uses a non-baseload emissions factor. For electricity consumption, the calculator uses an average emissions factor that includes both baseload and non-baseload generation. Note

Close mapeadora's Diary Diez años después de São Paulo: crónica de un State of the Map LATAM en casa (SotM LATAM 2026, Ciudad de México) Posted by mapeadora on 7 November 2026 in Spanish (Español) . Hace diez años asistí a mi primer State of the Map LATAM, en São Paulo, gracias a una beca de viaje. Hasta entonces, para mí OpenStreetMap era el grupo que habíamos formado en México a partir del mítico Rancho Electrónico, el hackerspace de la CDMX. En esos días descubrí que era mucho más: una comunidad regional, con rostros, historias, perspectivas y generosidad. Entendí por qué importan tanto estos encuentros presenciales. De ahí salieron amistades que han durado una década, a veces en persona y sobre todo en la virtualidad, y creo que con esas redes hemos hecho cosas importantes. Desde esa primera vez, junto con otras mujeres, decidimos también impulsar la inclusión y la diversidad en la comunidad, y así nació Geochicas. Por eso, cuando me convencí de liderar la edición mexicana, lo hice con emoción. Fue un año entero de sentimientos intensos, pensando en traer a mi ciudad a gente conocida y a personas nuevas de toda la región, feliz a la idea de que iban a vivir la ciudad en su mejor periodo y ojala conocer más detalles culturales. Una prioridad desde el inicio fue conseguir patrocinios suficientes para financiar un buen número de becas, que permitieran venir incluso a quienes están en los países más lejanos del Cono Sur. Más de la mitad de los fondos fue a becas. Algunas no pudieron usarse por problemas de visas, pero el esfuerzo valió la pena. Fueron 272 asistentes, 113 de ellas mujeres, tres días de intercambio técnico, comunitario y humano, con comida y bebida accesibles. Quisimos además un evento que cuida: hubo un salón silencioso y una sala de trabajo para quienes necesitaban pausa, bajar el estrés, o concentrarse. Elegimos hacerlo en el Centro Histórico, en Patio Chico, UNAM, de manera consciente: que no fuera solo una conferencia, sino una experiencia con máxima interacción entre personas. Y coincidió con Día de Muertos, cuando la ciudad entera late en una misma frecuencia de empatía y memoria, con el corazón abierto para honrar a quienes hemos querido. Fue hermoso ver a tantas personas descubrir ese rasgo cultural y sentir cosas nuevas. Fue también un encuentro intelectual y práctico muy intenso: nuevas tecnologías, métodos y temas de mapeo, con continuidad respecto a Belén y Medellín y con novedades propias. Un evento autogestivo y liderado por mujeres El evento fue liderado por mujeres. Participaron muchas personas, pero dedicamos toda nuestra energía durante un año, con una intensidad creciente hacia el final. Normalicemos nombrar a quienes más aportan y que, por lo absorbente de su esfuerzo, no alcanzan a salir en las fotos ni ante el micrófono. Nada de esto habría sido posible sin Yasmila (Mila) Saenz Herrera, central en el desarrollo de dos SotMs para acá: juntas lo sacamos adelante. Gracias también a: Miriam Gonzalez-Sanchez, por conseguir los patrocinios, esenciales para todo. Adriana Ávila Farfán y Andrea Berrocal, de UNAM-Patio Lab. Zeltzin Palacios y su comunidad UAM. Alma Rangel Macías, de Codeando México. Sandra Lucía Hernández Zetina, Benita Hernández Carbajal y las y los voluntarixs de UAEMex, que apoyaron toda la logística. Y muchas más. Mil gracias a nuestros aliados: la Dirección General de Divulgación de la Ciencia de la UNAM, Patio Lab, la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de México y la Sedatu (Secretaría de Desarrollo Agrario, Territorial y Urbano). Gracias también a las juventudes mapeadoras y a nuestros patrocinadores, que le dan el salto a todo esto: Overture Maps Foundation, TomTom, HERE Technologies, Development Seed, Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team y OpenStreetMap US. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/publications/enhanced-gain-extrapolation-technique PUBLICATIONS The Enhanced Gain Extrapolation Technique Published November 6, 2026 Author(s) Joshua Gordon , Benjamin Moser Abstract We present an overview on a recently developed technique for performing antenna gain measurements with gain extrapolation that uses significantly fewer data points and at shorter distances than traditional gain extrapolation. This enhanced technique purposely incorporates third-order mutual coupling between antennas, which can be thought of as a useful homodyne signal, rather than an unwanted degradation of the antenna-to-antenna coupling signal as has been the historically accepted viewpoint. From Wacker's fundamental extrapolation equations, we give the development of the third-order signal which underpins this technique. From the third-order signal the framing of gain extrapolation can be approached as a measure of interference fringes, as opposed to a by-rote curve fitting problem, and thus provides ways of specifying the number of required data points and measurement distances so as to reduce both significantly from the traditional gain extrapolation approach. The truncation order of the full signal expansion, as it relates to the conditioning of the problem, is presented in light of the behavior of the design matrix that defines the gain extrapolation scenario and the orders of scattering, thus leading to fewer required samples. Along with considerations of the matrix conditioning, guidelines are presented from the thirdorder signal and interference fringes for sampling criteria and sampling accuracy criteria. These aid in choices of measurement system accuracy and precision requirements based on known values of the operating frequency, wavelength, and antenna dimensions. Bounds for gain uncertainty based on these sampling criteria are also given. Results comparing NIST reference antenna measurements made with the traditional gain extrapolation and enhanced gain extrapolation technique are presented. It is shown that the enhanced technique can produce gain values in agreement and within uncertainties of the traditional technique for the reference antennas. pages.title: Questions over Warwickshire Chief Constable appointment process British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Warwickshire's PCC withdraws the preferred candidate status from the chief constable named in June 2026.
pages.text: Questions over Warwickshire Chief Constable appointment process Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Questions over police chief recruitment after candidate dropped 5 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Joan Cummins and Alec Blackman , West Midlands BBC/ Richard Forbes Emma Bond is currently the assistant chief constable of Police Scotland The Warwickshire Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) is facing questions over the recruitment of a new chief constable after withdrawing the preferred candidate's job offer. Emma Bond, currently Assistant Chief Constable at Police Scotland, was named in May as the preferred choice to replace Alex Franklin-Smith following his retirement in April. But more than four months later, the PCC announced that Bond's preferred candidate status had been withdrawn, meaning she will no longer take up the role. In a statement, Warwickshire PCC Philip Seccombe said no further comment would be made. However, the decision to effectively withdraw the job offer, which was subject to vetting, raises questions about the leadership of the county force. It comes after David Gardner, the current Acting Chief Constable, has already been appointed as the new head of Staffordshire Police, following a four week recruitment process. The PCC said arrangements would be announced to "to ensure continuity of leadership for Warwickshire Police", but gave no timetable. BBC/ Marian McNamee Philip Seccombe has been the Police and Crime Commissioner for Warwickshire since May 2016 Under amendments made to the Police Regulations made in 2026, vetting must take a maximum of six months. Bond had previously been named as the preferred candidate for the £188,656 role in June 2026, while Gardner was named as the new Chief Constable of the Staffordshire force in October . At the time of writing, no date has been set for Gardner to take up his new role and leave his position at the Warwickshire force. More Coventry and Warwickshire news 'Police did not investigate bullet hitting my home' Public used ladders to rescue people from flat fire 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize However, the delay in making an appointment of Chief Constable for Warwickshire, is worrying, according to the Labour MP for Warwick and Leamington, Matt Western. He told the BBC "It is concerning that Warwickshire remains without a permanent Chief Constable over six months after the previous holder left the force. "I have written to the Police and Crime Commissioner to express such concerns and hope he will be able to provide reassurances that he will be able to conduct a complete and timely recruitment process." The BBC has asked the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for Warwickshire for further comment and clarification. They confirmed they have nothing further to add to the statement previously issued. Follow BBC Coventry & Warwickshire on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram . pages.description: Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument offers hunting, fishing, and wildlife-viewing opportunities across 344,000 acres of public land. The article highlights how these outdoor traditions help people connect with nature, learn about conservation, and create lasting memories while supporting stewardship of public lands.

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Explore, Learn, and Connect Through Outdoor Traditions at Berryessa Snow Mountain Nov 10, 2026 Hunting and Fishing in Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument The traditions of hunting and fishing remain deeply rooted in America's public lands, connecting generations of outdoorsmen and women with the landscapes, wildlife, and waters that make these places special. At Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument, visitors can experience those traditions across 344,000 acres of public land stretching through some of Northern California's most diverse and scenic terrain. From oak woodlands and chaparral-covered hills to remote mountain forests and clear-running streams, the monument offers opportunities to explore remarkable landscapes while pursuing some of California's most sought-after game species and fisheries. Hunters come in search of black-tailed deer, wild turkey, wild boar, and California's distinctive Tule elk, while anglers appreciate the headwaters of the Eel River, one of the last strongholds for steelhead trout and coho salmon in Northern California. These outdoor experiences reflect the spirit of All Americans Outside, a Bureau of Land Management initiative that helps connect more people to their public lands through four pathways: Explore, Learn, Serve, and Work. Whether someone is hiking to a remote hunting area, casting a line in a mountain stream, learning about local wildlife, or volunteering to improve public access, public lands provide opportunities to connect with nature, support health and wellness, and create lasting memories outdoors. Overview of hunting and fishing in Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument video Outdoor Traditions on Public Lands For many visitors, hunting and fishing are about more than recreation. They are opportunities to pass traditions from one generation to the next, learn outdoor skills, and build a deeper connection to the land. At Berryessa Snow Mountain, those traditions unfold among some of California's richest wildlife habitat. The monument's diverse ecosystems support healthy populations of game species, including black-tailed deer, wild turkey, wild boar, and the unique Tule elk, the only elk subspecies found exclusively in California. The area's varied habitats also make it one of the most biologically varied landscapes in the state. Wildlife enthusiasts may spot golden eagles soaring overhead, native songbirds serenading in the trees, reptiles sunning on boulders, and a wide variety of mammals that depend on the monument's forests, grasslands, and river corridors. The monument is home to forests, grasslands, and river corridors. These habitats provide unique experiences for visitors to explore. (Photo by former employee Bob Wick) Fishing Waters Worth Protecting The monument's waterways offer equally memorable experiences. The headwaters of the Eel River provide habitat for steelhead trout and coho salmon, species that depend on clean water and intact ecosystems to survive. These fisheries give anglers the chance to test their skills while experiencing a watershed that plays a critical role in Northern California's natural heritage. Fishing opportunities throughout the monument provide visitors with a chance to slow down, spend time outdoors, and reconnect with nature amid some of the state's most spectacular scenery. pages.text: Impuestos. Seguridad. Unidos. Todos tenemos un papel que desempeñar en la protección de sus datos | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Impuestos. Seguridad. Unidos. Todos tenemos un papel que desempeñar en la protección de sus datos English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Presentar Individuos Quién debe presentar Pasos para presentar sus impuestos Presente su declaración de impuestos Obtener una prórroga Enmendar la declaración Actualice mi información Acontecimientos de la vida (en inglés) Estudiantes Empleados Padres Militares Jubilados y Personas de edad avanzada Negocios y trabajadores por cuenta propia Organizaciones caritativas y sin fines de lucro Contribuyentes internacionales Enlaces gubernamentales (en inglés) Gobiernos federales, estatales y locales (en inglés) Gobiernos tribales indígenas (en inglés) Bonos exentos de impuestos (en inglés) Números de identificación del contribuyente (TIN) Necesitamos su ayuda. El IRS, las agencias tributarias estatales y la industria tributaria, trabajando en conjunto como la Cumbre de Seguridad, han logrado un progreso significativo en la lucha contra del robo de identidad relacionado con los impuestos. Desde el 2015, esta sociedad colectiva ha tomado muchos pasos para mejorar la protección de sus datos. A pesar de estos logros, el robo de identidad continúa siendo una amenaza. Hay mucho trabajo que hacer, pero no lo podemos hacer solos. Le pedimos a ustedes – contribuyentes, profesionales de impuestos y negocios – que se unan a nosotros para crear una sociedad colectiva mucho más fuerte. Nuestra campaña de concientización "Impuestos. Seguridad. Unidos." es un esfuerzo por informarle mejor acerca de las acciones que usted puede tomar para proteger sus datos personales. Eventos y campañas Semana Nacional de Concientización sobre la Seguridad Tributaria de 2024 Proteja a sus clientes; Protéjase a sí mismo – Verano de 2024 Campañas de años anteriores Semana Nacional de Concientización sobre la Seguridad Tributaria Campañas de concientización Cómo pueden ayudar los contribuyentes Le hemos anotado algunas sugerencias de sentido común que pueden tener un gran impacto. Consulte la Publicación 4524 (SP), Conocimientos sobre la seguridad para los contribuyentes PDF . Algunos puntos destacados: Siempre utilice programas de seguridad con " firewall " y protección antivirus. Asegúrese de que el programa de seguridad esté siempre activado y pueda actualizarse automáticamente. Encripte archivos confidenciales, como son los registros de impuestos que almacena en su computadora. Utilice contraseñas seguras y únicas para cada cuenta. Si usted prepara sus propios impuestos en línea, utilice la opción de autenticación de múltiples factores de su proveedor para proteger su cuenta en línea. Esta autenticación de dos o de múltiples factores ayudará a prevenir que los ladrones puedan acceder su cuenta tributaria en línea y robar su información. La autenticación de múltiples factores se ofrece ahora más comúnmente para proteger otras cuentas, tal como los medios sociales, correo electrónico y otras. Por favor, utilice la autenticación de múltiples factores mientras se le ofrezca como una opción. Aprenda a reconocer y evitar correos electrónicos de phishing , llamadas y mensajes de texto amenazantes de los ladrones haciéndose pasar por organizaciones legítimas como su banco, compañía de tarjeta de crédito e inclusive el IRS. No haga clic en enlaces ni descargue archivos adjuntos de correos electrónicos desconocidos o sospechosos. Proteja sus datos personales. No lleve habitualmente su tarjeta de Seguro Social y asegúrese de que sus archivos de impuestos estén seguros. Al hacer compras en línea, utilice comercios que tengan buena reputación. Trate su información personal como trata a su dinero en efectivo; no lo deje tirado por ahí. Overview of Greenhouse Gases Greenhouse Gas Emissions Overview, by Type of Gas: 2022 Total U.S. Emissions in 2022 = 6,343 Million Metric Tons of CO₂ equivalent (excludes land sector). Percentages may not add up to 100% due to independent rounding. Land Use, Land-Use Change, and Forestry in the United States is a net sink and offsets 13% of these greenhouse gas emissions. This net sink is not shown in the above diagram. All emission estimates are sourced from the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks: 1990–2022 . Image to save or print On this page: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Overview Greenhouse Gas Effects on Climate Gases that trap heat in the atmosphere are called greenhouse gases. This section provides information on emissions and removals of the main greenhouse gases to and from the atmosphere. Click on a greenhouse gas below to learn about its emissions in more detail. Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) : Carbon dioxide enters the atmosphere through burning fossil fuels (coal, natural gas, and oil), solid waste, trees and other biological materials, and also as a result of certain chemical reactions (e.g., cement production). Carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere (or "sequestered") when it is absorbed by plants as part of the biological carbon cycle. Methane (CH 4 ) : Methane is emitted during the production and transport of coal, natural gas, and oil. Methane emissions also result from livestock and other agricultural practices, land use, and by the decay of organic waste in municipal solid waste landfills. Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) : Nitrous oxide is emitted during agricultural, land use, and industrial activities; combustion of fossil fuels and solid waste; as well as during treatment of wastewater. Fluorinated gases : Hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulfur hexafluoride, and nitrogen trifluoride are synthetic, powerful greenhouse gases that are emitted from a variety of household, commercial, and industrial applications and processes. Fluorinated gases (especially hydrofluorocarbons) are sometimes used as substitutes for stratospheric ozone-depleting substances (e.g., chlorofluorocarbons, hydrochlorofluorocarbons, and halons). Fluorinated gases are typically emitted in smaller quantities than other greenhouse gases, but they are potent greenhouse gases. With global warming potentials (GWPs) that typically range from thousands to tens of thousands, they are sometimes referred to as high-GWP gases because, for a given amount of mass, they trap substantially more heat than CO 2 . Additional compounds in the atmosphere including solid and liquid aerosol and other greenhouse gases, such as water vapor and ground-level ozone can also impact the climate. Learn more about these compounds and climate change on our Basics of Climate Change page . See Emissions Information and Reduction Strategies by Gas Carbon Dioxide Methane Nitrous Oxide Fluorinated Gases Greenhouse Gas Effects on Climate Each gas's effect on climate change depends on three main factors: How abundant are greenhouse gases in the atmosphere? Greenhouse Gases and Climate Visit EPA’s Basics of Climate Change page to learn more about the effect of greenhouse gases on the Earth’s climate. Concentration, or abundance, is the amount of a particular gas in the air. Larger emissions of greenhouse gases lead to higher concentrations in the atmosphere. Greenhouse gas concentrations are measured in parts per million, parts per billion, and even parts per trillion. Blog CESER Holds Industry Engagement Webinar Covering Recent Bulk-Power System Executive Order New executive order protects bulk-power system against national security risks and foreign-adversary threats. Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response September 10, 2026 Estimated Read Time min President Trump recently issued an executive order “ Declaring a National Emergency to Secure the United States Bulk-Power System ,” putting America’s energy security first by protecting the bulk-power system against national security risks and foreign-adversary threats. The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is actively engaging with utilities, states, equipment manufacturers, and industry partners to gather input, ensure clear guidance, and provide a predictable path forward for both existing equipment and future transactions. The department issued a request for information (RFI) seeking input on approaches to enhance the security and resilience of the nation’s bulk-power system. The RFI supports DOE’s efforts to implement the recent executive order and invites industry and other stakeholders to provide insights that will strengthen critical energy infrastructure. DOE’s Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) aims to gather detailed comments on the challenges, opportunities, and practical considerations involved in mitigating supply chain vulnerabilities, improving situational awareness, and reducing national security risks. Visit DOE's website for more information on the bulk-power system executive order. Bulk-Power System Executive Order Webinar CESER hosted an informational public webinar on September 16 that provided an overview of the RFI, highlighted the subjects on which DOE is seeking input, and explained how the public can submit responses. pages.text: Harry Wood's Diary | Blue Posts pub + Next Tuesday The Volunteer | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close Harry Wood's Diary Blue Posts pub + Next Tuesday The Volunteer Posted by Harry Wood on 6 November 2026 in English . Next Tuesday the OSMLondon pub meet-up will be at “The Volunteer” pub near Baker Street! Last time we were at the Blue Posts near Tottenham Court Road. We’ve been there many times before, but not for several years (we’ve been avoiding Sam Smiths for reasons, as I explained last time ). It didn’t seem to have changed much though. We took over a large part of the pleasantly quiet upstairs area. I think someone else took a photo, so I didn’t bother (?). Anyway we had maptastic chit-chat as always. I noted down a couple of interesting conversation topics: We talked about a recurring topic: Should we send automated welcome emails after users sign up? It’s pretty odd that we don’t do this, if we compare ourselves to just about any other user sign-up website, but I think the counter-argument has always been that we’re a very international community, and so we can do this by providing data on new contributors in a region, and letting local communities craft much better more friendly language and context-aware welcome emails. I’m sure this topic has been re-hashed many times over the years. A leading welcoming tool is “OpenStreetMap Welcome Tool” https://welcome.osm.be from LCCWG. I’ve not tried it. I see it’s not enabled for UK/GB/England (I think some UK people are welcoming new mappers in small areas using OSMCha) but a key feature would seem to be the ability to mark a recipient as “has been welcomed”. I was thinking an alternative hack would be to always welcome user’s via a discussion on their first changeset, just as a “weird trick” to turn it into a publicly viewable rather than private message, so we can see who’s been welcomed. But anyway I personally think the idea of a brief automated welcome email on registration should still be considered, because manually welcoming seems unlikely to reach everyone, and also there’s that frustrating fact that many users sign up then never get as far as making an edit. And speaking of these internal channels of promotion, Firefishy was plotting and scheming to do some experiments with homepage banners (like the graphics you may have seen for promoting SOTM). We now have the ability to show these in a location-dependant way, which raises questions about how to organise the promotion of events, but Firefishy was pondering doing an experiment with a banner to promote a particular editor in a particular region, and see what kind of shift in the editor usages stats would happen as a result. Kind of like an “A-B testing” experiment. We talked about updating shops/POIs data , and how we should really try to drive more use of the FHRS data . There’s some handy comparison tools. But we talked about maybe gamifying this a bit more, or perhaps presenting rankings by council regions to encourage competitive mapping. Those were some things I noted, but there were many other topics besides. If you fancy joining in with this kind of discussion face-to-face in a pub… come along! The next OpenStreetMap London pub meet-up will take place Tuesday 10th at “The Volunteer” pub on Baker Street. It’s 293 metres north of Baker Street tube, which isn’t a very inaccessible watering hole , but with a name like that I couldn’t resist! See you there? Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/publications/traceable-validation-calculable-quantum-based-rf-waveforms PUBLICATIONS Traceable Validation of Calculable Quantum-Based RF Waveforms Published November 4, 2026 Author(s) Jeremy Thomas , Nathan Flowers-Jacobs , Anna Fox , Johannes Hoffmann, Paul Dresselhaus Abstract We compare the calculated, quantum-based output of a radio-frequency Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (RF-JAWS) with its measured output that is calibrated through the established NIST RF power traceability path, a necessary first step towards quantum-based RF metrology. An array of 1,500 Josephson junctions (JJs) is used to synthesize sinusoids from 50MHz to 3 GHz, each with a nominal output power of -49.67dBm and a demonstrated quantum-locking range (QLR). We perform a two-tier calibration of two-port vector network analyzer (VNA) measurements of the RF-JAWS waveforms with uncertainty analysis: (1) the VNA wave parameters are referenced to a NIST-calibrated coaxial power sensor, and (2) a cryogenic probe station, together with on-chip superconducting calibration standards, establishes an on-chip reference plane at the JJ-array. The calibrated measurement of the forward- and backward-propagating power is compared with the expected, calculated outputs, and, after accounting for high-frequency roll-off, we observe agreement within the expanded (k = 2) uncertainty limits for most frequencies. Acerca de la División de Prevención y Control del Cáncer 30 de sep. del 2026 English (US) VISTAZO GENERAL La División de Prevención y Control del Cáncer (DCPC) de los CDC lidera esfuerzos para prevenir el cáncer, encontrarlo en su etapa inicial y mejorar la salud de los sobrevivientes de cáncer. Lo que hacemos En los Estados Unidos, cada año 1.6 millones de personas reciben un diagnóstico de cáncer, y 600 000 personas mueren por su causa. Los cuidados para el cáncer cuestan $185 mil millones cada año. El cáncer es la segunda causa principal de muerte en el país, pero más de la mitad de las muertes por cáncer probablemente se podrían prevenir al reducir las causas del cáncer y al aumentar las pruebas de detección y la administración de vacunas. La División de Prevención y Control del Cáncer trabaja para reducir los factores que aumentan el riesgo de cáncer, y promueve las pruebas de detección de cáncer. Estas actividades ayudan a que cada persona tenga igualdad de oportunidades de obtener la mejor salud posible. Prioridades Recolectar datos sobre los casos y tratamientos del cáncer La División de Prevención y Control del Cáncer dirige el Programa Nacional de Registros del Cáncer y coordina con otras agencias federales para recolectar datos sobre casi todos los casos de cáncer en los Estados Unidos. Estos datos se usan para ayudar a guiar los esfuerzos a fin de prevenir el cáncer y detectarlo de forma temprana. Los datos del Programa Nacional de Registros del Cáncer se pueden usar para responder preguntas como las siguientes: ¿Hay más o menos personas con cáncer de colon este año, en comparación con el año pasado? ¿Hay mujeres en ciertas áreas geográficas con más probabilidades de presentar cáncer de mama en etapa tardía, cuando es más difícil de tratar? ¿Qué grupos de personas tienen más probabilidades de tener cáncer de piel? Promover las pruebas de cáncer colorrectal El cáncer colorrectal es una de las causas principales de muerte por cáncer en los Estados Unidos, pero no tiene por qué ser así. Las pruebas de detección del cáncer colorrectal pueden encontrar pólipos precancerosos (crecimiento de tejido anómalo en el colon o el recto) para que sean extirpados antes de que se conviertan en cáncer. Las pruebas de detección también ayudan a encontrar el cáncer colorrectal en sus primeras etapas, cuando el tratamiento es más eficaz. El Programa de Control del Cáncer Colorrectal de los CDC financia 21 estados, 8 universidades, 3 organizaciones tribales y 6 organizaciones más para aumentar las tasas de pruebas de detección del cáncer colorrectal en las personas de 45 a 75 años. Promover las pruebas de detección del cáncer de mama y de cuello uterino Hacerse mamografías, pruebas de Papanicoláu y del virus del papiloma humano (VPH) de manera regular puede reducir su riesgo de morir por el cáncer de mama o de cuello uterino. Estas pruebas pueden encontrar el cáncer en una etapa temprana, cuando el tratamiento es más eficaz. Las pruebas de detección de cáncer de cuello uterino también pueden prevenir el cáncer al encontrar lesiones precancerosas (crecimiento de tejido anómalo) antes de que se convierta en cáncer. El Programa Nacional de Detección Temprana del Cáncer de Mama y de Cuello Uterino (NBCCEDP) de los CDC otorga fondos a los 50 estados, el Distrito de Columbia, Puerto Rico, 5 islas del Pacífico afiliadas a los EE. pages.text: PSNI taking 'more robust' approach to e-bikes and scooters Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live PSNI taking 'more robust' approach to e-bikes and scooters 6 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Barry O'Connor , Claire Quinn and Niall Glynn , BBC News NI Third Street Studios Police helicopter footage shows a child on an e-scooter in Belfast city centre E-Scooters and e-bikes have "become a challenging issue" for the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI), the lead road safety officer has said. From 1 January until 31 October 2026 provisional figures show 473 of the machines were seized by the PSNI, 379 of which were e-scooters. In the two years between 1 September 2024 and 31 August 2026, provisional police figures also show there were 150 collisions involving e-scooters reported to the PSNI. There were two fatalities in that time and 45 people sustained serious injuries. "We have taken a more robust approach in dealing with the issue," Ch Supt Sam Donaldson said. Police Service of Northern Ireland Chief Superintendent Sam Donaldson said police are taking a robust approach "It's crucial there is a consistent approach by officers across Northern Ireland when dealing with the issue," he added. During a three-day operation in September, a six-year-old child was among those stopped by police and 65 e-bikes and e-scooters were seized. Donaldson said reports to police are rising and seizures have "dramatically increased". The issue of illegal e-bikes and e-scooters is highlighted in the new series of the BBC's Peelers: The PSNI For Real, which returns to screens on Wednesday. In the series, presenter Stephen Nolan sees officers responding to complaints about e-bikes and e-scooters in public spaces - and the scale of the problem they face. In one episode, a police helicopter monitors a child driving an e-scooter recklessly in Belfast city centre. Third Street Studios Peelers: The PSNI For Real gives an insight into the realities, pressures and unexpected moments that officers face in their work Footage shows him weaving in and out of traffic, doing wheelies and driving the wrong way down one-way streets. The air support is deployed because officers on the ground fear that if they chase the suspect, he could fall off and injure himself or others. The helicopter tracks the boy to his home, to which officers are sent to arrest him and confiscate the e-scooter. What is an e-scooter? Watch:Stephen Nolan joins high-speed police chase An e-scooter is an electrically-powered vehicle consisting of a narrow foot platform mounted on wheels, attached to a long, narrow steering column with handlebars. Users travel by standing on the platform, known as a deck, and are propelled forward by an electric motor powered by a rechargeable battery. Owning, buying or selling an e-scooter is not illegal in Northern Ireland but they can only be used on private land and only if the landowner gives their permission. Last year, police said there was "no specific offence" for using an e-scooter on public roads in Northern Ireland. But officers can enforce other rules in relation to them, such as having no vehicle excise duty - usually referred to as car tax or road tax - or insurance, which the user is unlikely to have for an off-road vehicle. "We need the public to understand the legalities in relation to e-scooters, as we see how children are using them as a toy, similar to bikes and how they're bought as presents, for example birthdays or at Christmas," Ch Supt Donaldson said. "Adults use e-scooters as a means to get from place-to place, e.g. work, to the shop, and as a cheap and environmentally friendly mode of transport. "We also see how e-scooters are used as a vehicle for those involved in anti-social behaviour. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Swainson’s Hawks: a remarkable return to California’s Central Valley Oct 19, 2026 Swainson’s Hawks are medium-to-large raptors renowned for their elegant flight and extraordinary migratory journeys. Each year, these hawks travel thousands of miles between their breeding grounds in the western United States and Canada and their wintering sites in Central and South America. California’s Central Valley is especially critical to their life cycle, with 95 percent of the state’s Swainson’s Hawks nesting there. Upon arrival in the Central Valley, Swainson’s Hawks select nest sites near grasslands or agricultural fields, which offer abundant prey and shelter. During the breeding season, their diet consists mainly of rodents, rabbits, reptiles, and small birds, which are essential for raising their young. Outside the breeding season, they adapt by feeding primarily on insects such as grasshoppers, demonstrating remarkable versatility. An adult male Swainson’s Hawk returns to the nesting area with a rodent. An adult female Swainson’s Hawk delivers a fledgling bird to the nest. Despite their adaptability, Swainson’s Hawks have faced significant challenges. In 1983, they were listed as Threatened in California due to habitat loss and declining numbers, with only about 375 breeding pairs remaining from an estimated historical population of 17,000. But thanks to conservation and habitat restoration efforts, the population has rebounded, with recent estimates suggesting that around 1,000 breeding pairs now reside in the Central Valley. However, Swainson’s Hawks remained absent from parts of their historic range for decades. Notably, they had not nested in the Central Valley portion of Shasta County since at least 1980, with the nearest recorded nesting pair prior to 2026 located about 40 miles south in Glenn County. This absence underscored the need for habitat restoration and innovative partnerships to encourage their return. In 2024, a grant from the state of California Wildlife Conservation Board enabled the BLM and River Partners to restore riparian and floodplain habitat near Battle Creek, a vital tributary of the Sacramento River in Shasta County. The project replaced a fallow walnut orchard with native vegetation, supporting the broader vision of the Floodplain Forward Memorandum of Understanding, a multi-agency agreement to expand floodplain projects in the Sacramento River Basin. These efforts aim to improve flood protection, habitat, groundwater recharge, and agricultural resilience. Habitat growth was slow in 2025 but accelerated in 2026, creating diverse environments for wildlife, including Swainson’s Hawks. Removal of the old walnut orchard Swainson’s Hawk fledglings at about four weeks old The impact of restoration was soon evident. In May 2026, a pair of Swainson’s Hawks was observed circling the creek in the newly restored area, even engaging in dramatic behaviors such as dive-bombing juvenile bald eagles. On June 15th, a nest was discovered. Over the following weeks, observers witnessed aerial food transfers, with the male delivering rodents and birds to the female, who then brought food to the nest. Eventually, two nestlings were confirmed, marking a significant milestone for the species in Shasta County. The restoration area during the second year By mid-July, the young hawks had fledged and were seen flying along the creek with their parents nearby. pages.description: Verificamos su reclamación por robo de identidad y hemos colocamos un indicador en su cuenta. Monitorearemos la actividad en su cuenta de impuestos para ayudarle a prevenir fraudes en el futuro.
pages.text: Cómo entender su aviso CP01 (SP) | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Cómo entender su aviso CP01 (SP) English Español Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) De qué se trata este aviso Verificamos su reclamación por robo de identidad y hemos colocamos un indicador en su cuenta. Monitorearemos la actividad en su cuenta de impuestos para ayudarle a prevenir fraudes en el futuro. Lo que usted debe hacer No necesitamos ninguna acción adicional de su parte. En el futuro, tendrá que presentar sus impuestos con un PIN para la protección de la identidad (IP, por sus siglas en inglés). En diciembre o enero de cada año, le enviaremos por correo su IP PIN – usted tendrá que utilizar ese PIN para presentar sus impuestos. Cada año recibirá un IP PIN nuevo. Si prefiere tener un IP PIN más rápido, puede solicitarlo en línea . Una vez que solicite su IP PIN en línea, usted queda registrado automáticamente en la asignación sin papel del IP PIN. Tendrá que iniciar sesión en su cuenta anualmente para recuperar su número de IP PIN. Tal vez usted desee Revisar la página del IRS sobre la Centro informativo sobre el robo de identidad para obtener más información. Revisar RobodeIdentidad.gov en el sitio web de la Comisión Federal de Comercio (FTC, por sus siglas en inglés), Monitorear todas sus cuentas financieras personales. Monitorear su informe de crédito por actividad sospechosa o no autorizada. Usted o una tercera persona autorizada pueden solicitar una copia editada (una con alguna información oculta) de la declaración fraudulenta que fue presentada y aceptada por el IRS utilizando su nombre y número de Seguro Social. Para obtener más información sobre cómo solicitar una copia de la declaración fraudulenta, consulte las Instrucciones para solicitar copia de declaraciones fraudulentas (en inglés) . Además de proteger su información de identificación personal (PII, por sus siglas en inglés), la información de su dependiente puede estar comprometida. Si la identificación personal (PII) de sus dependiente fue comprometida, presente una queja con la FTC en RobodeIdentidad.gov y reciba orientación paso a paso. Si el acceso al internet no es una opción, usted puede llamar a la FTC al 877-438-4338 ; TTY 866-653-4261 . Preguntas frecuentes ¿Qué efecto tiene en mi cuenta indicador de robo de identidad? (actualizada el 25 de octubre de 2024) El indicador no tiene efecto en su capacidad de presentar su declaración de impuestos, realizar pagos o recibir un reembolso. Sin embargo, usted tendrá que presentar con un IP PIN mientras el indicador permanezca en su cuenta. ¿Por cuánto tiempo se mantiene el indicador en mi cuenta? El indicador permanecerá en su cuenta de impuestos para protegerle porque usted fue una víctima de robo de identidad, a menos que usted específicamente nos solicite que sea eliminado. ¿Qué sucede si alguien más utiliza mi número de Seguro Social para presentar una declaración de impuestos fraudulenta? El indicador que colocamos en su cuenta nos alertará para realizar una búsqueda y asegurarnos de que el formulario presentado con su número de Seguro Social es válido. Si consideramos que la declaración de impuestos es inválida, no la tramitaremos. ¿Con quién debo comunicarme si tengo más preguntas sobre mi cuenta relacionadas con el robo de identidad? Llame al 800-908-4490 para recibir asistencia especializada acerca del robo de identidad relacionado con su cuenta. También puede encontrar el número en su aviso. Para otras preguntas relacionadas con su cuenta de impuestos, visite nuestra página Permítanos ayudarl e o llame al 800-829-1040 . ¿Dónde puedo encontrar más información sobre cómo prevenir el robo de identidad? Sources of Greenhouse Gas Emissions On this page: Sources of Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Overview Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trends: All Sources Sources of Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Overview Greenhouse gases trap heat and make the planet warmer. Human activities are responsible for almost all of the increase in greenhouse gases in the atmosphere over the last 150 years. 1 The largest source of greenhouse gas emissions from human activities in the United States is from burning fossil fuels for electricity, heat, and transportation. EPA tracks total U.S. emissions by publishing the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks . This annual report estimates the total national greenhouse gas emissions and removals associated with human activities across the United States by source, gas, and economic sector. Total U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions by Economic Sector in 2022 Total U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions by Economic Sector Total U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions by Economic Sector Including Electricity End-Use Indirect Emissions Total emissions in 2022 are 6,343.2 Million Metric Tons of CO₂ equivalent . Percentages may not add up to 100% due to independent rounding. Greenhouse gas emissions from the commercial, residential, and industrial sectors increase substantially when indirect emissions from electricity end-use are included, due to the relatively large share of electricity use by buildings (e.g., heating, ventilation, and air conditioning; lighting; appliances and plug load) and use of electricity for powering industrial machinery. More information is also in the electricity end-use emissions section of the Electric Power sector page . Land Use, Land-Use Change, and Forestry in the United States is a net sink and offsets 13% of these greenhouse gas emissions. This net sink is not shown in the above diagrams. All emission estimates are sourced from the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks: 1990–2022 . What are the primary sources of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions and sinks in each economic sector? Transportation – Greenhouse gas emissions from transportation primarily come from burning fossil fuel for cars, trucks, ships, trains, and planes. Over 94% of the fuel used for transportation is petroleum based, which includes primarily gasoline and diesel and results in direct emissions. 2 The transportation sector is the largest source of direct greenhouse gas emissions and second largest source when indirect emissions from electricity end-use are allocated across sectors. The transportation sector is an end-use sector for electricity but currently represents a relatively low percentage of total electricity use. Indirect emissions from electricity are less than 1 percent of direct emissions. Electricity production – Electric power includes emissions from electricity production used by other end use sectors (e.g., industry). In 2022, 60% of our electricity comes from burning fossil fuels, mostly coal and natural gas. 3 Industry – Greenhouse gas emissions from industry primarily come from burning fossil fuels for energy, as well as greenhouse gas emissions from certain chemical reactions necessary to produce goods from raw materials. Industrial emissions are the third largest source of direct emissions. If indirect emissions from electricity use are allocated to the industrial end-use sector (e.g. to power industrial buildings and equipment), industrial activities account for a much larger share of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions as shown above. pages.text: CESER Secures Critical Infrastructure Through Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management | Department of Energy Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Blog CESER Secures Critical Infrastructure Through Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management CESER's Energy Cyber Sense program helps identify and engineer out cybersecurity vulnerabilities across the energy supply chain Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response June 26, 2026 Estimated Read Time min In today's interconnected world, nearly every operation relies on a complex web of digital components—from hardware and firmware to software and services. This reliance can introduce significant vulnerabilities. The Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response’s (CESER) Energy Cyber Sense program aims to improve the nation’s ability to identify and engineer out cybersecurity vulnerabilities across the energy supply chain through partnerships with manufacturers and energy infrastructure technology users. Robust Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) programs are especially critical as they aid in identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks. Historically, C-SCRM programs have focused on software supply chains. However, evolving cyberattack vectors have demonstrated broader implications for both hardware and firmware. Security needs for these technologies are intricate, depending on their installation, configuration, and maintenance. Addressing risk must go beyond technical security measures and must encompass the processes required to deploy, operate, and maintain these digital components. A recent IEEE Security & Privacy magazine article showcased CESER’s work in this space including several contributions that would improve C-SCRM. The article explains why practitioners must align on consistent terminology to clearly discuss C-SCRM problems and determine solutions. Additionally, it outlines how experts should classify digital component cyberattacks based on their lifecycle stage and type (hardware, firmware, software, services) to provide a clear understanding of different threat classes and available options for mitigation and response. The article also highlights key obstacles that C-SCRM programs currently face: Organizational Obstacles: Organizations have greater control over products specially designed to meet their needs, while commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) products are cheaper, widely adopted, and easier to use and manage. The widespread adoption, trust, and influence of COTS products can expose organizations to common-mode vulnerabilities, which can lead to more cyberattacks. Technical Obstacles: Organizations frequently lack adequate visibility into implicit dependencies among their digital components. This makes it difficult to assess and manage evolving vulnerabilities. Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs) and Software Composition Analysis (SCA) can serve as resources to combat this problem, but they are often plagued with accuracy and usability issues. Procedural Obstacles: Specialization across multiple tiers of suppliers can create silos, increasing the complexity of coordinating mitigation and response efforts. Systems marketed for a specific function to one stakeholder group often possess broader functionality as general-purpose computers support a versatile feature set. This further complicates risk assessment and management. CESER delivers timely, actionable information to the energy sector through programs like Energy Cyber Sense. With a dedicated focus on infrastructure hardening efforts, CESER will continue to provide technical assistance to drive innovation on energy hardware, software, and equipment solutions. pages.text: Sandip Saha Joy, Instructor | Coursera Sandip Saha Joy Former Data Scientist IBM sandipsahajoy Bio Sandip Saha Joy worked as a Data Scientist for IBM. After completing high school from Bangladesh, he studied Computer Science at the University of Alberta, Canada. His areas of focus are Computer Vision, Machine Learning and Statistical Modeling. As a Data Scientist at IBM, he learnt and applied Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. pages.title: Linear Rail Kinematic Calibration using a Legendre Polynomial Model | NIST Lock
pages.description: Linear motion components are widely used in antenna metrology positioning systems, but long motion ranges can reduce positioning accuracy due to the difficulty
pages.text: Linear Rail Kinematic Calibration using a Legendre Polynomial Model | NIST Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/publications/linear-rail-kinematic-calibration-using-legendre-polynomial-model PUBLICATIONS Linear Rail Kinematic Calibration using a Legendre Polynomial Model Published November 4, 2026 Author(s) Benjamin Moser , Joshua Gordon , Andrew J. Petruska Abstract Linear motion components are widely used in antenna metrology positioning systems, but long motion ranges can reduce positioning accuracy due to the difficulty of eliminating rail component non-linearity. Further, offset device-under-test (DUT) mounting can magnify rotation errors arising from slight variations of rail parallelism not captured by a strictly linear motion model. We present methods to reduce position and rotation inaccuracy through kinematic calibration using a Legendre polynomial model. The motion range of the rail system is conditioned for use over an appropriate evaluation range. The calculation of calibrated coefficients is detailed for an individual rail calibration and is further integrated in a pose-error minimization calibration framework for general robotic implementation. This approach is validated using experimental 6 degree-of-freedom (DoF) measurements collected using Large Antenna Positioning System robotic antenna range. Compared to a strictly linear rail model, the Legendre polynomial model reduced the RMS position error by 67.7% to 27.90 um and RMS rotation error by 29.9% to 84.92 urad. pages.title: BLM Fishing Derby brings Americans Outside for recreation and stewardship in Imperial Valley, California | Bureau of Land Management Lock
pages.description: BLM’s annual Fishing Derby unites families, first‑time anglers, and partners for a day of recreation, stewardship, and community connection across Imperial Valley’s public lands in California.
pages.text: BLM Fishing Derby brings Americans Outside for recreation and stewardship in Imperial Valley, California | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM Fishing Derby brings Americans Outside for recreation and stewardship in Imperial Valley, California Oct 13, 2026 In a region best known for its off-highway vehicle adventures, the BLM California's El Centro Field Office hooked a different type of recreator for its second annual Fishing Derby Cast and Clean-up event. More than 100 members of the local community gathered for the event on Saturday, Sept. 26, bringing together recreation, community engagement, and public-land stewardship on BLM-managed public lands in Imperial County, California. The fishing derby took place at the Hot Springs Long-Term Visitor Area and on BLM-managed lands adjacent to the Highline and All-American canals. For many attendees, it was their first fishing opportunity, and several first-time anglers caught their first fish. As they fished, participants also collected trash from the surrounding public lands, demonstrating their commitment to responsible recreation and care for the areas they enjoy. Siblings Gabriel and Kayla Orozco pose with BLM El Centro employees during the fishing derby. (Photo by BLM) The event was the brainchild of BLM Park Ranger Damian Montaño, an Imperial Valley native who recognized an opportunity to engage Imperial County’s passionate fishing community and create an experience for families to build lasting connections to public lands and outdoor recreation. “I've fished in this area my whole life, so I know how important it is to our community,” said Montaño. “We have a strong fishing culture, with people who care deeply about our resources and teaching the next generation to respect the land.” Partners, including the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW), Hispanic Access Foundation, Fort Yuma Quechan Indian Tribe, and Imperial Irrigation District, helped make the event possible and strengthened the event’s connection to community, outdoor recreation, and stewardship. CDFW staff member Jose Muños highlighted the community's need for a recreation event centered on fishing, stating, “The Imperial Valley deserves an annual fishing event.” The event featured adult and youth fishing divisions, with first-, second- and third-place awards recognizing participants in the bass and catfish categories. Nine major prizes were awarded to winners, including a first-time angler who placed third in the youth catfish division. The event introduced new anglers to fishing, creating opportunities for youth in support of All Americans Outside , a nationwide BLM initiative to help more Americans, regardless of ability, enjoy their public lands. Youth fish for bass and catfish during the BLM Fishing Derby Cast and Clean-up event. (Photo courtesy of Hispanic Access) Youth enjoy the outdoors and fishing during the BLM Fishing Derby Cast and Clean-up event. (Photo courtesy of Hispanic Access) Local fishing organizations were key to the event’s success, helping boost participation and deepen community involvement. The BLM recognizes the contributions of the Imperial Valley Desert Fishing Club, Imperial Valley Heavy Action Anglers, Radfin Outdoors and Imperial Valley Bass Addicts, for their support of the event and dedication to the local fishing community. Some of the strongest connections to public lands start with a first fish. Sobre los defectos de nacimiento Para todos 10 de nov. del 2026 English (US) Puntos clave Los defectos de nacimiento son cambios estructurales que están presentes al nacer. Los defectos de nacimiento pueden variar de condiciones médicas leves a graves. Los defectos de nacimiento pueden diagnosticarse durante el embarazo o después del nacimiento. Lo que son Los defectos de nacimiento son cambios estructurales que están presentes al nacer y que pueden afectar casi cualquier parte del cuerpo, como el corazón, el cerebro o los pies. Pueden afectar la apariencia y el funcionamiento del cuerpo, o las dos cosas. El lenguaje es importante. Si bien "defecto de nacimiento" es un término médico, no significa que una persona sea "defectuosa". Se refiere a condiciones que se presentan en un bebé antes del nacimiento. En un intento por ser precisos y sensibles, siempre que sea posible tratamos de usar el nombre específico de la condición presente al nacer. Los defectos de nacimiento pueden variar de leves a graves. Los efectos en la salud y la expectativa de vida dependen de cuál parte del cuerpo está involucrada y cómo se ve afectada. Los defectos de nacimiento pueden ocurrir en cualquier etapa del embarazo. La mayoría ocurre en los primeros 3 meses, cuando los órganos del bebé se están formando. Sin embargo, algunos defectos de nacimiento ocurren más adelante en el embarazo a medida que los tejidos y los órganos continúan desarrollándose. Incidencia Los defectos de nacimiento son comunes y afectan a 1 de cada 33 bebés nacidos en los Estados Unidos cada año. Factores de riesgo Para algunos defectos de nacimiento, como los trastornos del espectro alcohólico fetal , conocemos la causa. Pero en el caso de la mayoría, no se sabe qué los causa. Creemos que la mayoría de los defectos de nacimiento son causados por una mezcla compleja de factores, incluidos nuestros genes, nuestros comportamientos y nuestro ambiente. Pero no se sabe completamente cómo estos factores podrían interactuar y causar defectos de nacimiento. Riesgos conocidos Aunque tenemos más trabajo por hacer, hemos aprendido mucho. Sabemos que algunas cosas pueden aumentar las probabilidades de tener un bebé con un defecto de nacimiento, como las siguientes: Fumar, consumir alcohol o consumir ciertas drogas durante el embarazo. Tener ciertas condiciones médicas, como diabetes no controlada . Tomar ciertos medicamentos, como isotretinoína (usado para el tratamiento del acné). Tener alguien en la familia con un defecto de nacimiento. Contraer ciertas infecciones durante el embarazo, como el citomegalovirus o Zika . Tener fiebre superior a los 101 o F o tener una temperatura corporal elevada. La edad en la que tiene un hijo o una hija también puede influenciar el riesgo de defectos de nacimiento. Algunos defectos se ven más frecuentemente entre madres jóvenes (gastrosquisis). El riesgo de algunos otros defectos (malformaciones cromosómicas, como síndrome de Down) aumenta con la edad. Puede tener un bebé con un defecto de nacimiento si no tiene ninguno de estos riesgos conocidos. Y tener uno de estos factores de riesgo no significa que su bebé tendrá un defecto de nacimiento. Es importante hablar con su médico sobre su salud y todos los factores de riesgo y formas de mantenerse saludable durante el embarazo. ¡Hable con su médico sobre mantenerse saludable por usted y por su bebé! pages.text: Reportable Food Registry for Industry | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home Food Compliance & Enforcement (Food) Reportable Food Registry for Industry Compliance & Enforcement (Food) In this section The Reportable Food Registry (RFR or the Registry) is an electronic portal for Industry to report when there is reasonable probability that an article of food will cause serious adverse health consequences. The Registry helps the FDA better protect the public health by tracking patterns and targeting inspections. The Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 (Pub. L. 110-085), section 1005 directs the FDA to establish a Reportable Food Registry for Industry. The RFR applies to all FDA regulated categories of food and feed, except dietary supplements and infant formula. For Industry/Regulators Submit a Report For Consumers Contact FDA Who Should Use the Reportable Food Registry? Registered Food Facilities that manufacture, process, pack, or hold food for human or animal consumption in the United States under section 415(a) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 350d) are required to report when there is a reasonable probability that the use of, or exposure to, an article of food will cause serious adverse health consequences or death to humans or animals. Federal, state, and local government officials may voluntarily use the RFR portal to report information that may come to them about reportable foods. Reportable Food Registry Policy Information Video RFR At A Glance Reportable Food Registry (RFR) At a Glance - English RFR At A Glance - Español (Spanish) RFR At A Glance - 中文 (Chinese) RFR At a Glance - Francais (French) RFR Commodity Definitions Policy Information Draft Guidance for Industry: Questions and Answers Regarding the RFR as Established by the FDA Amendments Act of 2007 (Edition 2) Information on the FDA Reportable Food Registry (RFR) for Foreign Governments Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act (FDAAA) of 2007 RFR Dashboard and Data Reportable Food Registry Annual Report Reportable Food Registry Public Data Dashboard Where Should Consumers, Food Retailers and Food Service Operators Report a Problem with Food? Consumers who have symptoms should contact their health care provider to report their symptoms and receive care. To report a complaint or adverse event (illness or serious allergic reaction), visit Industry and Consumer Assistance . What to Do if the Safety Reporting Portal is Not Operating If you are not able to use the Safety Reporting Portal, you may also call 1-888-INFO-FDA and follow the prompts to report a problem. If you require the use of a Relay Service, please call the Federal Relay Services at 800-877-8339. This is a toll-free relay service to call federal agencies from TTY devices. FDA further recommends that a report be submitted by the responsible party to the Safety Reporting Portal as soon as it resumes operation. Solo utilice este servicio si le enviamos un aviso de la serie CP5071 o una carta 5447 (C/SP) . Antes de empezar Tenga a mano su aviso del IRS. Si usted presentó una declaración: Tenga su declaración original o enmendada del Formulario serie 1040 correspondiente al año que aparece en la carta. Si no lo tiene, consulte con su software de impuestos o consulte con su preparador de declaraciones de impuestos. Si no presentó una declaración: Utilice este servicio para notificarnos. Es posible que alguien haya intentado presentar una declaración con su información. Si es menor de 18 años de edad: Contáctenos . Inicie sesión para verificar su identidad y declaración de impuestos Inicie sesión o crea una cuenta, y responde algunas preguntas para verificar su declaración. Si usted creo una cuenta, es posible que tenga que volver a iniciar sesión para completar su verificación de declaración. Iniciar sesión o crear una (en inglés) Obtenga ayuda para crear una cuenta Temas de Ayuda Ayuda para iniciar sesión Obtén ayuda para iniciar sesión o crear una Si no puede verificar en línea Siga las instrucciones de su aviso serie CP5071 o carta 5447(C/SP) ​​ Proteja su identidad Para evitar que alguien presente una declaración con su número de Seguro Social (SSN, por sus siglas en inglés) o número de identificación personal del contribuyente del IRS (ITIN, por sus siglas en inglés), obtenga un PIN para la protección de la identidad (IP PIN, por sus siglas en inglés) . Su reembolso Espere 2-3 semanas después de usar este servicio para revisar su reembolso . Puede demorarse hasta 9 semanas para procesar su declaración después de que usted lo verifique. pages.description: OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
pages.text: Harry Wood's Diary | The Albert Pub & Geomob + Blue Posts tonight | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close Harry Wood's Diary The Albert Pub & Geomob + Blue Posts tonight Posted by Harry Wood on 23 September 2026 in English . Last updated on 11 November 2026. Tonight’s London pub meet-up is at the Blue Posts . An old favourite! Last time I said I was going to be adventurous with pub choices, and we went to The Albert in Victoria. I’m sorry I didn’t bother writing down any notes about interesting OpenStreetMap discussions from the evening. Rest assured many interesting OpenStreetMap discussions were discussed. My diary entry last time was just about pub choices, and this one will be no different! Actually I do remember there was a lot of conversation about delivering election leaflets, since we had at least three different people in attendance who do a lot of campaigning, and using OpenStreetMap for that. It’s quite a nice use of OSM since you can boost the addressing coverage in the area of interest, and then use it, and then fix issues while using it, in a nice localised virtuous circle, and the use involves visiting every address, so perfect for filling in any map gaps. So this was a new pub, and it worked pretty well. I decided to follow a theory I had, that pubs can be less overcrowded and more pleasant when they are further away from tube stations . The Albert pub was about half way between Victoria and Westminster tubes. Not sure it really worked in terms of avoiding the crowds, but it was spacious enough upstairs. There was a very big screen showing the wimbledon which we had to try not be distracted by. I described this “further away from tube stations” theory to Matt Amos, and he crunched the numbers, rendered the maps, and dedicated a entire geomob talk investigating the “Watering Holes of inaccessibility” concept , including comparing OSMLondon pub choices over the past 18 years to conclude that we do indeed tend to go to pubs which are relatively far from tube stations! Not always though. One of the pubs we’ve been to many times is The Blue Posts on Newman Street. This one is 363 metres from the Tottenham Court Road tube station. Pretty close. Certainly it always felt very central, but I suppose it is actually almost equidistant to Oxford Circus. We haven’t been back there in quite a long time because we decided Sam Smiths pubs are a bit weird and we should maybe take our business elsewhere. They’re opposed to mobile phones and social media sharing, which could be inconvenient for tech meet-up! And as organisation they have a track record of making annoying cantankerous decisions. [Update: I also just remembered Joe lycett has this funny explanation ] This seems largely thanks to their annoying cantankerous boss, Humphrey Smith. But he died recently, so maybe it’s time to forgive and forget, or at least see how they’re getting on. Maybe they’ll have done away with all those dusty traditional ideas, and strung up TVs in all the corners! Or maybe we’ll be getting there before that enevitably happens. In any case, I’m quite looking forward to going back to this old favourite, maybe just this once. See you there tonight?
