Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Congenital Zika Syndrome and Other Birth Defects For Everyone Oct. 26, 2026 What to know Zika virus can spread from an infected pregnant woman to her fetus. Infection during pregnancy can lead to congenital Zika syndrome and other birth defects. Zika virus infection does not impact future pregnancies. Overview of Zika-associated birth defects Zika virus infection during pregnancy can cause birth defects of the brain or eye. These birth defects can occur alone or with developmental problems in a particular pattern called congenital Zika syndrome. The following conditions can occur in a baby with congenital Zika virus infection: Smaller than expected head size, called microcephaly Problems with brain development Feeding problems, such as difficulty swallowing Hearing loss and vision problems Seizures Decreased joint movement, called contractures Stiff muscles, making it difficult to move Not all babies born with congenital Zika syndrome will have all of these conditions. Some infants who do not have microcephaly at birth may develop it later. In addition, some babies might look healthy at birth but can develop long-term health problems as they grow. Microcephaly Microcephaly is a birth defect in which a baby's head is smaller than expected when compared to babies of the same sex and age. Babies with microcephaly often have smaller brains that might not have developed properly. View Larger Download Babies with microcephaly have a smaller head than expected for their age and sex. Recommended screenings If your baby was born with congenital Zika infection, they should receive recommended screenings even if they appear healthy. Babies and children affected by Zika virus may have lasting special needs. They may require specialized care from many types of healthcare providers and caregivers as they age. Frequency of Zika-associated birth defects Zika virus does not cause birth defects for every baby exposed to the virus before birth (i.e., in utero). Infection with Zika virus during pregnancy simply increases the chances for these problems. Among women with confirmed or possible Zika infection during pregnancy in U.S. states and territories, Zika-associated birth defects occurred in about 5% of babies. 1 View Larger Download Zika-associated birth defects occurred in about 5% of babies born to women with Zika while pregnant. Zika symptoms and birth defects Zika-associated birth defects can occur whether or not the pregnant woman had symptoms of the infection during pregnancy. In the U.S. states and territories, about 1 in 20 (5.3%) people with symptoms of Zika virus infection during pregnancy had a baby with Zika-associated birth defects, compared with about 1 in 25 (4.2%) people infected with Zika virus but had no symptoms during pregnancy. 1 Timing of Zika during pregnancy Zika-associated birth defects are more common among infants born to women with exposure early in pregnancy. The highest risk of Zika-associated birth defects is with infection during the first and second trimesters. In the U.S. states and territories, about 2 in 25 (8%) pregnant women with confirmed Zika virus infection in the 1st trimester had babies with Zika-associated birth defects. 1 View Larger Download Risk of birth defects is highest in the first and second trimesters. Future pregnancies Zika virus infection in a woman who is not pregnant does not pose a risk for future pregnancies. pages.description: The BLM is seeking public feedback on a proposal to expand Class 1 e-bike access on mountain bike trails in the Colorado River Valley Field Office. Review the draft environmental assessment and comment by Dec. 14.
pages.text: BLM Invites Community Feedback on Proposed E-Bike Use on Mountain Bike Trails in CO | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Press Releases BLM Invites Community Feedback on Proposed E-Bike Use on Mountain Bike Trails in CO Organization: Bureau of Land Management BLM Office: Colorado River Valley Field Office Media Contact: BLM Colorado BLM_CO_News@blm.gov Nov 13, 2026 Class 1 e-bikes provide electric assistance only while the rider is pedaling, with motor assistance ending at 20 miles per hour. The proposal would apply only to Class 1 e-bikes on designated mountain bike trails. SILT, Colo. – The Bureau of Land Management is considering whether to significantly expand Class 1 e-bike access on designated mountain bike trails across the Colorado River Valley Field Office, including some of the region's most sought-after riding opportunities to e-bike users. The proposal is outlined in a draft environmental assessment that examines several alternatives, including maintaining current trail designations. The public is invited to review the alternatives and help shape the future of e-bike access on these trails by providing feedback during a 30-day comment period beginning Nov. 13. Of the more than 220 miles of designated single-track mountain bike trails managed by BLM, approximately 18 miles at the Grand Hogback Trail System north of Rifle are currently open to Class 1 e-bikes. The draft environmental assessment analyzes three alternatives: The Proposed Action would open 118 additional miles of existing trails in designated recreation areas and near the Hardscrabble-East Eagle Special Recreation Management Area A second alternative would open 187 additional miles that are currently under consideration No Action Alternative would leave current e-bike designations unchanged During the scoping period for this project held in spring of 2026, commenters expressed both support for expanded e-bike access and concerns about potential impacts. Supporters emphasized opportunities for riders of different ages and physical abilities, while others raised questions about trail user conflicts, wildlife disturbance, enforcement and increased use of sensitive areas. Some commenters also suggested a more selective approach, including limiting e-bikes to certain trails, establishing directional routes and improving signage and rider education. “Public feedback played an important role in shaping the alternatives we're now evaluating,” said Colorado River Valley Field Manager, Lisa Dawson . “This next comment period gives people an opportunity to review the analysis, weigh in on the different options and help us determine how best to balance recreation opportunities with trail safety and resource protection.” The review also supports the goals of the BLM's All Americans Outside initiative, which encourages people of all abilities to explore and enjoy public lands. By considering expanded e-bike access, the BLM is exploring opportunities to make outdoor recreation more accessible while balancing trail safety and resource protection. The draft environmental assessment, maps and supporting documents are available on the BLM National NEPA Register . Comments must be submitted through the “Participate Now” feature on the project webpage by Dec. 14. “Every trail system is different, and what works in one area may not work in another,” said BLM Colorado Outdoor Recreation Planner, Alan Czepinski . “Comments about specific trails, user experiences and conditions on the ground are especially helpful as we evaluate where expanded access may be appropriate.” Public comments will be considered

pages.title: Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act A worker is entitled to minimum wage and overtime pay protections under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) when there is an employment relationship between the worker and an employer and there is coverage under the FLSA. Employers are responsible for determining whether a worker is an employee under the FLSA. Misclassification occurs when an employer treats a worker who is an employee under the FLSA as an independent contractor. Misclassifying employees as independent contractors is a serious problem because misclassified employees may not receive the minimum wage and overtime pay to which they are entitled under the FLSA or other benefits and protections to which they are entitled under the law. As part of its efforts to address misclassification, the Wage and Hour Division on January 10, 2024 published a final rule , effective March 11, 2024, revising its guidance on how to analyze whether a worker is an employee or independent contractor under the FLSA. This guidance is available in the form of regulations at 29 CFR Part 795. Employers and workers may consult these regulations and the additional resources listed below to help analyze a worker’s status as an employee or independent contractor under the FLSA. The Wage and Hour Division’s final rule also rescinds the Independent Contractor Status Under the Fair Labor Standards Act rule ( 2021 IC Rule , 86 FR 1168) that was published on January 7, 2021. EPA Announces Public Availability of 24 HHCB Studies and Opens 30-Day Comment Period Released on November 13, 2026 U.S. Environmental Protection Agency is announcing the availability of 24 studies considered in the Agency’s draft risk evaluation for HHCB , also known as galaxolide, under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). HHCB is a synthetic musk used widely in fragrances and in household products such as detergents, cleaners, and air fresheners. Because this chemical is used so broadly, EPA’s review needs to reflect the full body of available science and give the public an opportunity to review the same information EPA used in its draft assessment. During the public comment period for the draft HHCB risk evaluation, EPA identified an administrative issue in its Health and Environmental Research Online, or HERO, database that temporarily made 24 industry-submitted studies inaccessible to the public. These studies had already been considered in the draft risk evaluation. EPA resolved the issue on October 14, 2026, and the studies are now publicly available in HERO. To ensure the public has an opportunity to review the newly available materials, EPA is opening a 30-day public comment period. Interested persons may review the studies in the context of the draft HHCB risk evaluation and submit comments. This comment period is limited to the newly available materials and does not reopen the entire draft risk evaluation. EPA remains committed to transparency and to using the best available science in its TSCA risk evaluations. The Agency will carefully consider any comments received on the newly available studies as it works to finalize the HHCB risk evaluation. Upon publication of the Federal Register notice, a list of the 24 studies will be included in the HHCB Data Availability Memorandum in docket EPA-HQ-OPPT-2018-0430 . The public comment period will close December 16, 2026. En esta página, encontrará información de como acceder a sus trascripciones mediante: Cuenta en línea Obtenga una transcripción por correo o a través de nuestro servicio telefónico automatizado Servicios de transcripción en general Transcripciones a través de la cuenta en línea para personas físicas P1. ¿Cómo obtengo una transcripción en línea? (actualizada el 16 de agosto de 2024) Una vez que se haya registrado exitosamente en su cuenta Login.Gov y su cuenta de IDMe, podrá iniciar sesión en su cuenta en línea para personas físicas. Desde allí, acceda a los registros tributarios y luego el enlace de transcripciones, Si no tiene una cuenta en línea para personas físicas, puede crear una cuenta fácilmente. P2. ¿Qué sucede si no puedo verificar mi identidad y utilizar cuenta en línea para personas físicas? (actualizada el 16 de agosto de 2024) Consulte Tipos de transcripción y métodos de pedirlas para obtener las alternativas. P3. ¿Por qué no puedo obtener mi carta de verificación de que no he presentado una declaración para el año tributario actual? La carta de verificación de que no ha presentado una declaración para el año tributario actual no está disponible hasta el 15 de junio. P4. ¿Qué hago si no puedo ver mi carta de verificación de que no he presentado una declaración cuando pulso en un año tributario disponible? (agregada el 5 de septiembre de 2024) Si obtiene un mensaje de error que indica que se produjeron dificultades técnicas al intentar ver su carta de que no ha presentado una declaración, tendrá que solicitarla presentando el Formulario 4506-T, Solicitud de Transcripción de la Declaración de Impuestos, (en inglés) . P5. ¿Por qué mi transcripción de salarios e ingresos indica que “no hay registros de una declaración presentada” para el año tributario actual? (actualizada el 4 de febrero de 2026) Si ve un mensaje de “No record of return filed” (no hay registros de una declaración presentada) para el año tributario actual, significa que la información todavía no se ha trasladado a la transcripción. Vuelva a verificar a principios de febrero. P6. ¿Por qué recibo un mensaje diciendo que mi solicitud de transcripción de salarios e ingresos no puede ser tramitada en línea? (actualizada el 16 de agosto de 2024) La transcripción está limitada a aproximadamente 85 documentos de ingresos. Si tiene más documentos que eso, la transcripción no se generará. Recibirá una notificación en línea en la que se le indicará que su solicitud de transcripción no ha podido ser tramitada y que debe llenar y presentar el Formulario 4506-T, Solicitud de transcripción de la declaración de impuestos (en inglés) . P7. ¿Puedo obtener una transcripción para mi negocio? Yes, encuentre como obtener una transcripción para su negocio (en inglés) . pages.title: MikeHur's Diary | Wandering Around: a browser game that turns OSM into a walkable world | OpenStreetMap
pages.description: OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
pages.text: MikeHur's Diary | Wandering Around: a browser game that turns OSM into a walkable world | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close MikeHur's Diary Wandering Around: a browser game that turns OSM into a walkable world Posted by MikeHur on 3 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 8 November 2026. I’ve been building Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk around any town or city on Earth. The whole world comes from OpenStreetMap, so I’d like to share how it uses OSM data and ask this community for feedback. Play it here: https://wanderingaround.games (works on phone and desktop, no account needed) News and updates: https://ko-fi.com/wanderingaroundtheworld Screenshots and a short video: https://mikehur.itch.io/wandering-around How the map is built Streets, buildings, water, parks and bridges come from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (zoom 14, OpenMapTiles schema). The game fetches the tiles around the player, decodes them in the browser, stitches buildings that are split across tile edges and turns everything back into OSM-style features with tags. The game logic works on those tags, so it is the same code whether the data comes from tiles or (as a fallback) from Overpass. 2D and 3D: the same data drives a 2D map and a 3D eye-level view. Building heights come from OSM where they are tagged. Transit: train routes and stations, city buses, ferries and signposts come from Overpass queries, so you can travel between real stops and stations. Country map: towns, airports and ferry ports within 100 km come from pre-built tiles made from Overture, OurAirports and Natural Earth. What the game adds itself Vector tiles leave out some details, such as single trees, benches, crossings, traffic lights and roof shapes. The game fills those in itself so streets don’t look empty. These are decoration, not data: they are never written back anywhere. Wikidata postcards Every feature with a wikidata tag (and, in the Netherlands, ref:rce for national monuments) becomes a landmark. When you visit one you get a postcard with: a photo from Wikimedia Commons (P18), with the photographer and licence shown, year built (P571), height (P2048) and floors (P1101), a summary from Wikipedia in your language. In the 3D view the game uses the Wikidata height for the building and takes the facade colour from the photo. So a good wikidata tag on a building directly improves what players see. What I’d love feedback on Does your own area look right? Missing buildings, odd water or bridges, or stops in strange places usually point to a tagging pattern I don’t handle yet. How do performance and rendering hold up in very dense city centres, compared with rural areas? Any ideas for using more OSM data in a game in a way that is fun and encourages people to improve the map. Thanks to everyone who maps. Without your work this game would be an empty grey square. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors · tiles by OpenFreeMap · Wikidata · Wikipedia · Wikimedia Commons Location: Waterkwartier, De Hoven, Zutphen, Gelderland, Netherlands, 7204 VA, Netherlands Discussion Comment from frederik_nlp on 5 November 2026 at 15:09 The “Wikipedia summary in your language” is the feature that made me stop and read the whole entry. It’s the same entity - a building, a bridge, a park - accessible from any language, and this is the first place I’ve seen that done in a way that feels natural rather than bolted on. The 3D facade colour from the photo is a nice touch too; a good wikidata tag does double duty. I’ll try it in Aarhus this week and report back on how the Danish summaries come through - danwiki is small but it covers the major landmarks, so it should be a decent test case for the less-resourced end of the spectrum. For the “encourage people to improve the map” question: the postcard mechanic is already doing that quietly. November 22, 2024 Diagnosis of Birth Defects Key points If the result of a screening test is abnormal, providers usually offer further diagnostic tests. These diagnostic tests are also offered to women with higher risk pregnancies. Certain birth defects might not be diagnosed until after the baby is born. Why get tested You may or may not want to know if your baby has a health condition before birth. If you decide to have a diagnostic test, you can learn more about your baby’s condition. You can also learn how to care for your baby after birth. You may need to make plans to give birth in a hospital that can give your baby special medical care. Who should be tested If you receive an abnormal screening test result, your provider will discuss diagnostic test options. These diagnostic tests are also offered to women with higher risk pregnancies, which may include: Women who are 35 years of age or older. Women who have had a previous pregnancy affected by a birth defect. Women who have chronic diseases such as lupus, diabetes, or epilepsy. Women who use certain medications. Types of tests High resolution ultrasound An ultrasound creates pictures of the baby. This type of ultrasound is used to look in more detail for possible birth defects or other concerns with the baby. It is usually completed between weeks 18 and 22 of pregnancy. Ultrasounds and other prenatal tests can help diagnose some birth defects. Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) CVS testing involves collecting and testing a tiny piece of the placenta, called chorionic villus. This test can check for chromosomal or genetic disorders in the baby. An amniocentesis is completed between 10 and 12 weeks of pregnancy. Amniocentesis Amniocentesis is a prenatal test that takes amniotic fluid from around your baby in the uterus. The fluid is then tested to measure the baby's protein levels. Cells in the fluid can be tested for chromosomal disorders, such as Down syndrome, and genetic problems, such as cystic fibrosis. Amniocentesis is completed between 15 and 18 weeks of pregnancy. There are several proteins for which an amniocentesis tests, which can indicate certain birth defects. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is one of the proteins the baby produces. A high level of AFP in the amniotic fluid may indicate a defect with an opening in the tissue. This could be a neural tube defect (anencephaly or spina bifida), or a body wall defect, such as omphalocele or gastroschisis. Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is an enzyme that the baby produces. This enzyme can pass from the baby to the amniotic fluid if there is an opening in the neural tube. After the baby is born Whether your baby is diagnosed during pregnancy or after birth, they may need special care as they grow. Parents can prepare for their child's needs by learning about their child's condition. This knowledge can equip you to make the best possible choices for your child's health. Children with special healthcare needs can benefit from the medical home approach to care . This personalized approach supports working together to make sure that medical and nonmedical needs of children and families are met. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Press Releases BLM Invites Additional Public Feedback for March 2027 Oil and Gas Lease Sale in Colorado Organization: Bureau of Land Management Media Contact: Levi Spellman BLM_CO_News@blm.gov Nov 10, 2026 Two BLM employees work near oil and gas pipes with a mountain and the setting sun in the background. LAKEWOOD, Colo. – The Bureau of Land Management opened a 30-day public comment period today to receive public input on plans to include 38 oil and gas parcels totaling 65,900 acres in Colorado in a March 2027 sale. The comment period ends Dec. 10, 2026. The BLM completed scoping on these parcels in October 2026 and is now seeking public comment on the parcels and related environmental analysis. The BLM will use input from the public to help complete its review of each parcel. Leasing is the first step in the process to develop federal oil and gas resources. Before development operations can begin, an operator must submit an application for permit to drill detailing development plans. The BLM reviews applications for permits to drill, posts them for public review, conducts an environmental analysis and coordinates with state partners and stakeholders. All parcels that are included in a federal oil and gas lease sale include appropriate stipulations to protect important natural resources. Information on current and upcoming BLM leases is available through the National Fluid Lease Sale System . BLM lease sales are held online through Efficient Markets . The parcels BLM is analyzing, as well as maps and instructions on how to comment, are available on the BLM’s ePlanning website at: https://eplanning.blm.gov/documents/?id=5549EBB4-89AB-F111-AAAC-001DD802F839&spid=c549ebb4-89ab-f111-aaac-001dd802f839 . The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

pages.text: Family and Medical Leave Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Family and Medical Leave Act The FMLA entitles eligible employees of covered employers to take unpaid, job-protected leave for qualifying family and medical reasons and requires continuation of their group health benefits under the same terms and conditions as if the employee had not taken leave. Check with your State Labor Department to determine if you have additional or greater protections under state law. What Does the FMLA Provide? For eligible employees, up to 12 workweeks of leave in a 12-month period for any of the following qualifying reasons: The birth of a child and to care for the newborn child within one year of birth, The placement with the employee of a child for adoption or foster care and to care for the newly placed child within one year of placement, To care for the employee's spouse, child, or parent who has a serious health condition, A serious health condition that makes the employee unable to perform the functions of his or her job, and Any qualifying exigency arising out of the fact that the employee's spouse, son, daughter, or parent is a covered military member on covered active duty or call to covered active duty status. An eligible employee who is the spouse, son, daughter, parent, or next of kin of a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness may take up to 26 workweeks of leave during a single 12-month period to care for the servicemember. Eligible employees may use FMLA leave intermittently or on a reduced schedule when medically necessary and for qualifying exigencies. An employee also may use FMLA leave intermittently or on a reduced leave schedule for bonding with a newborn or newly placed child when the employer and employee agree. Expand All ▼ Covered Employers and Employee Eligibility The FMLA applies to covered employers, which include: Private-sector employers who employ 50 or more employees in 20 or more workweeks in either the current calendar year or the previous calendar year, Public agencies (including federal, state, and local government employers), regardless of the number of employees, and Local educational agencies (including public school boards, public elementary and secondary schools, and private elementary and secondary schools), regardless of the number of employees. Learn more about when two (or more) businesses may simultaneously employ an employee . Employees are eligible if they: Work for a covered employer for at least 12 months, Have at least 1,250 hours of service with the employer during the 12 months before their FMLA leave starts, and Work at a location where the employer has at least 50 employees within 75 miles. In determining employee eligibility, the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) requires that a person reemployed under its provisions be given credit for months and hours of service he or she would have been employed but for the USERRA-covered service. Airline flight crew employees have special hours of service eligibility requirements. Qualifying Leave Reasons and Family Relationships The FMLA provides job-protected leave from work for certain qualifying family and medical reasons . An eligible employee may take up to 12 workweeks of leave in a 12-month period for: A serious health condition affecting the employee or the employee’s child, parent, or spouse, The birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child, Qualifying exigencies when the employee’s child, parent, or spouse is on covered active duty or under an impending call to covered active duty. An eligible employee may take up to 26 workweeks of military caregiver leave during a single 12-month period if the employee is the child, parent, spouse, or next of kin of a: Current servicemember with a serious injury or illness , or Covered veteran with a serious injury or illness . EPA’s 2026 Mercury Inventory Finds Major Reductions in Mercury in Products and Manufacturing Released November 6, 2026 Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) published the 2026 Mercury Inventory Report on the supply, use, and trade of mercury in the United States. The release of this report further underscores the Trump Administration’s commitment to radical transparency and gold standard science by informing the public about mercury use trends in the United States and strengthening the scientific basis EPA uses to protect Americans. Mercury is a persistent neurotoxin that does not break down in the environment and can cause serious health problems, which is why EPA tracks every remaining use and why the sharp declines in this report matter. The report describes the supply, use, and trade of mercury in the United States during calendar year 2024 and helps EPA, researchers, industry, and the public understand overall trends in mercury use, including where mercury still remains in commerce. Overall, the supply, use, and trade of mercury in the United States are declining. A small number of limited uses remain in certain manufacturing processes and in some components of electrical equipment, and EPA continues to work to reduce and replace these uses as alternatives become available. Highlights of the report include: A 48% decrease in mercury used in products made in the United States and a 58% decrease in mercury used in products sold in the United States. A 56% decrease in the total amount reported for the manufacture of elemental mercury. A 99% decrease in the total amount reported for the import of mercury compounds. The data in the 2026 report will help the United States implement the Minamata Convention on Mercury , a global treaty that protects people and the environment from exposure to mercury. The Inventory of Mercury Supply, Use, and Trade in the United States 2026 Report presents combined data from 2024 submitted on imported mercury, mercury manufactured in the United States, imported mercury-added products, mercury-added products made in the United States, and mercury used in manufacturing processes. The inventory report also provides a broad view of U.S. mercury stored, sold, and exported, as well as identifies industry sectors and trading partners involved in the supply, use, and trade of mercury. Read the report: Inventory of Mercury Supply, Use, and Trade in the United States 2026 Report . Background In March 2017, EPA published the initial inventory report of mercury supply, use, and trade in the United States with information available from public sources. On June 27, 2018, EPA published a final rule which established reporting requirements to support EPA’s development of triennial inventories under TSCA and requires reporting from persons who manufacture (including import) mercury or mercury-added products, or otherwise intentionally use mercury in a manufacturing process. This means that the data in the report comes directly from the companies that are using, manufacturing, or importing mercury, providing EPA and the public with more reliable and complete information on the supply, use, and trade of mercury in the United States. The 2020 Mercury Inventory Report was the first inventory published after finalizing the mercury inventory reporting rule (the initial 2017 inventory was limited to only publicly available data). Blog CESER and Sandia National Laboratory Test Super Intelligence Systems to Support Grid Resilience STAISYS evaluates cutting-edge super intelligence technologies under operational stress and adversarial threats. Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response November 16, 2026 Estimated Read Time min The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) has partnered with Sandia National Laboratory (SNL) on Scaled Testing for Artificial Intelligence Systems (STAISYS). This cyber-physical testing ground is designed to evaluate cutting-edge super intelligence (SI) technologies under operational stress and adversarial threats. STAISYS is part of CESER’s Artificial Intelligence For Operationally Resilient Technologies and Systems (AI-FORTS) program. This project helps researchers test SI capabilities in critical infrastructure, emulate cyber activity alongside physical grid behaviors, and run automated experiments across numerous operating configurations. STAISYS’ core capabilities include: Cyber-Physical Testbed Integration:Embedding advanced SI tools into emulated environments that faithfully mirror physical power equipment, control protocols, and network architectures. Adversarial Threat Modeling and SI Kill Chains: Developing structured threat workflows to evaluate how malicious actors might manipulate training pipelines, inject malicious sensor telemetry, exploit control logic, or target underlying computing infrastructure. Statistical Evaluation at Scale: Conducting continuous, high-throughput experimentation to quantify operational uncertainty, measure systemic blast radii, and evaluate resilience across diverse attack surfaces. As the energy sector embraces automated decision-making and next-generation intelligence, ensuring verifiable security is a national imperative. CESER and SNL will use STAISYS to evaluate these technologies deployed across critical energy infrastructure and under cyber threats. This work aims help organizations identify vulnerabilities and strengthen grid resilience to defend America’s power grid. Learn more about STAISYS on SNL’s website . Explore more on these topics: Unleashing American Energy Innovation Cybersecurity Energy Security Super Intelligence

También puede presentar electrónicamente (e- file ) las declaraciones de impuestos sobre la nómina corregidas, Formulario 941-X , Formulario 943-X y Formulario 945-X . El programa de presentación electrónica (e- file ) del Formulario 940 permite que un contribuyente presente electrónicamente (e- file ) un Formulario 940 enmendado. Beneficios de la presentación electrónica: Le ahorra tiempo. Es segura y exacta. Usted recibe un acuse de recibo dentro de 24 horas. Para obtener más información sobre el programa de presentación electrónica (e- file ) del IRS, visite la Plataforma de presentación electrónica modernizada (MeF, por sus siglas en inglés) (en inglés) . Si desea presentar electrónicamente su formulario de impuestos sobre la nómina, elija una de las dos opciones siguientes: Opción 1: Deseo presentar los formularios yo mismo Tendrá que comprar el software aprobado por el IRS. Esta lista de proveedores (en inglés) ofrece las opciones con base en el año tributario correspondiente. Es posible que deba pagar un cargo para presentar electrónicamente las declaraciones. El software requerirá su firma para presentar electrónicamente (e- file ) la declaración. Dependiendo el software que haya adquirido, tendrá una o ambas de las siguientes opciones: Aplicar por un PIN de firma en línea para la 94X (en inglés) (Permita que transcurran por lo menos 45 días para recibir su PIN) Escanee y adjunte el Formulario 8453-EMP, Informe del impuesto sobre el ingreso personal de los Estados Unidos por medio de la presentación electrónica del IRS (e- file ) (en inglés) . Opción 2: Deseo que un profesional de impuestos presente la declaración por mí Utilice el Servicio autorizado de localización de proveedores de presentación electrónica del IRS e-file (en inglés) para encontrar un profesional de impuestos que pueda presentar los formularios por usted. Se requiere depósito electrónico Los depósitos de impuestos federales tienen que realizarse mediante transferencias electrónicas de fondos (EFT, por sus siglas en inglés). Usted puede realizar pagos a través de su cuenta de impuestos de negocios, a través de Pago Directo (Direct Pay) para negocios , utilizando el sistema de pago electrónico del impuesto federal (EFTPS, por sus siglas en inglés) gratuito del gobierno o o mediante uno de los siguientes métodos que pueden tener cargos adicionales: Solicite a su institución financiera que inicie un pago de crédito de la cámara de compensación automatizada (ACH, por sus siglas en ingles) en su nombre. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to this park navigation Skip to the main content Skip to this park information section Skip to the footer section National Park Service Katmai National Park & Preserve Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Katmai National Park & Preserve Contact Us Frequently Asked Questions Directions and Logistics Where is Katmai? Katmai National Park & Preserve ( map ) is located in the northern Alaska Peninsula, northwest of Kodiak Island and southwest of Homer. The park's headquarters is in King Salmon, about 290 miles southwest of Anchorage. How do I get to Katmai? Can you drive? Unlike most parks in the United States, there are no roads connecting the park to the rest of the state -- you cannot drive to Katmai, Brooks Camp, or King Salmon from Anchorage. Most visitors fly or boat to the park. Most destinations are directly accessed via air taxi flights from Anchorage, Dillingham, Homer, King Salmon, Kodiak, and other nearby Alaska towns and villages. Regularly scheduled commercial flights to King Salmon (AKN) are available from Ted stevens Anchorage International Airport (ANC) via Alaska Airlines. Boats can access the Pacific coast of Katmai. Brooks Camp and other locations along the Naknek River drainage can be reached by power boat from the villages of Naknek and King Salmon. Please see Katmai's Directions Page for more information. When is the park open? The park and preserve are open year-round. At Brooks Camp, National Park Serivce and concessioner services are offered June 1 to September 17. How do I reserve air taxis, bear guides, and other commercial services? The NPS Alaska Region's commercial services webpage has a link for authorized visitor service operators within Katmai National Park and Preserve. There you will find names and contact information for air taxis, bear watching guides, and other commercial services. How do I visit the Pacific Coast of Katmai? Most people who visit the Pacific side of Katmai arrive via a chartered airplane from Anchorage, Homer, Kodiak and other nearby towns, cities, and villages. Private and chartered boats can also access many places on the coast as well. The Pacific coast of Katmai offers a combination of amazing scenery, wilderness, and wildlife viewing opportunities. Most people who visit this area of the park go to watch bears, but there are many opportunities for sport fishing and wilderness trekking too. Go to the NPS Alaska Region's commercial services webpage for an updated list of authorized commerical visitor services. Is there a fee for backcountry use? No. Backcountry areas do not have fees or facilities. No backcountry permits are required. Please visit the backcountry hiking and camping pages for more information. Brooks Camp How do I get to Brooks Camp? With no roads in, most people who visit Brooks Camp fly from Anchorage to King Salmon on a commercial airline ( Alaska Airlines ) and fly or boat from King Salmon to Brooks Camp using one of the many authorized transportation providers. For a complete list of commercial service providers visit our Directory of Commercial Visitor Service Providers . Where do you see bears at Brooks Camp? In July and September, bears are everywhere at Brooks Camp. They can be found walking trails, fishing in the river, and even napping on the beach. During July, many bears can be seen fishing at Brooks Falls which is about 1.2 miles (1.9 km) from the Brooks Camp Visitor Center. In September, most bears are seen at the mouth of the Brooks River. Please note that in June and August few bears, if any, can be seen at Brooks Camp. Please

pages.text: FLSA Protections to Pump at Work | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content FLSA Protections to Pump at Work Revised January 2026 Coverage for certain employees of rail carriers and motorcoach services operators begins December 29, 2025. Employees may be exempt if an employer demonstrates that compliance would require significant expense or results in unsafe conditions. The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) requires employers to provide reasonable break time for an employee to express breast milk for her nursing child for one year after the child's birth each time such employee has need to express the milk. Employees are entitled to a place to pump at work, other than a bathroom, that is shielded from view and free from intrusion from coworkers and the public. What You Should Know Under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA): Most nursing workers are entitled to reasonable break time and a private space to pump at work for up to one year after their child’s birth. Most employers are required to provide covered employees with space that is functional for pumping milk, shielded from view, free from intrusion, available as needed and not a bathroom. Learn more about Employer Responsibilities . New Law Expanding Pumping at Work Protections On December 29, 2022, the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023 became law. This legislation introduced the PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act (“PUMP Act”), expanding these rights to more nursing employees, including agricultural workers, nurses, teachers, truck and taxi drivers, home care workers and managers. Pump at Work “Know Your Rights” and Employer Materials These materials can be printed and used in workplaces to ensure that workers understand their rights and employers understand their responsibilities under the law. EPA Finalizes Updates to Formaldehyde Emission Standards, Adds New Quality Control Test Method for Composite Wood Products Released October 23, 2026 U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is adding a new quality control test method for measuring formaldehyde air emissions from composite wood products as part of routine updates to its Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). Formaldehyde is a component of resins and adhesives used to make composite wood products such as plywood, particleboard, and medium-density fiberboard, which are found in furniture, cabinets, flooring, and building materials. It can be released into indoor air from these products. The Formaldehyde Standards for Composite Wood Products Act of 2010 directed EPA to set emission limits for these products to reduce exposure and protect public health. The method for ISO 12460-2:2024(en) Wood-based panels — Determination of formaldehyde release Part 2: Small-scale chamber method, provides manufacturers and testing laboratories with an additional, internationally recognized tool to help ensure consistent, high-quality emissions data across the industry. Along with adding this new method, EPA is finalizing technical updates to align the rule’s voluntary consensus standards with the most current standards for safety and exposure to formaldehyde in composite wood products issued by national and international organizations, including the American National Standards Institute (ANSI), the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM), the British Standards Institute (BSI), the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). These updates aim to maintain consistency with industry practices, provide greater clarity for wood product manufacturers, and help ensure Americans continue to have access to the products they rely on. They do not alter any existing health or safety protections for consumers or workers and are unrelated to the agency’s ongoing TSCA risk evaluation for formaldehyde. This is the fourth time EPA has updated voluntary consensus standards since the 2016 final rule. Formaldehyde is widely used as an adhesive in wood products such as furniture, flooring, cabinets, bookcases, and building materials including plywood and wood panels. The Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products Act of 2010 directed EPA to establish emission standards for formaldehyde emitted from these materials to reduce exposure and protect public health. The following updated voluntary consensus standards are included in the final rule: ANSI A190.1-2022, Product Standard for Structural Glued Laminated Timber (ANSI) ASTM D5582-22, Standard Test Method for Determining Formaldehyde Levels from Wood Products Using a Desiccator (ASTM) ASTM D6007-22, Standard Test Method for Determining Formaldehyde Concentrations in Air from Wood Products Using a Small-Scale Chamber (ASTM) ASTM E1333-22, Standard Test Method for Determining Formaldehyde Concentrations in Air and Emission Rates from Wood Products Using a Large Chamber (ASTM) ISO 12460-3:2023(E), Wood-based panels—Determination of formaldehyde release—Part 3: Gas analysis method (BS EN ISO) PS 1-22, Structural Plywood (NIST) Read a prepublication version of the final rule . pages.title: Using a Form 94x online signature PIN to e-file employment tax forms | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Learn how to apply for a 10-digit signature PIN and become an IRS Authorized Signer. You would use the PIN to electronically sign your employment tax returns using IRS-approved software
pages.text: Using a Form 94x online signature PIN to e-file employment tax forms | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Using a Form 94x online signature PIN to e-file employment tax forms More In File Individuals Businesses and self-employed Business tax account Employer ID numbers Business taxes Business structures Operating a business Self-employed Small business Industries and professions Small business events Online learning Large business Charities and nonprofits International taxpayers Governmental liaisons Federal, state and local governments Indian tribal governments Tax exempt bonds Taxpayer identification numbers (TIN) You can apply for a 10-digit signature PIN and become an IRS authorized signer. You would use the PIN to electronically sign your employment tax returns, using IRS-approved software . You must be: Sole Proprietor for a sole proprietorship Partner with 5% or more interest in a partnership or person authorized to act in legal and or tax matters President, vice president, secretary or treasurer of a corporation Other: The principal for an entity that is not a sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation must be an individual authorized to act in legal and or tax matters As an IRS authorized signer, you are stating that you are a person or principal who can legally bind the entity. You are authorized to sign and act in tax matters on behalf of the business identified on your application. Steps to apply and use your PIN: Complete the on-line signature PIN registration process, which is in your software package. Once approved, IRS will send you a 10-digit PIN. You will receive the PIN in a sealed and uncompromised envelope. Sign the statement of receipt and return it to the address shown on the letter within 10 business days from the date of the letter. Use the designated PIN to sign your employment tax returns electronically. This authenticates that you are the IRS authorized signer when the returns are submitted electronically. When to contact the help desk You know or suspect your PIN was compromised. The name of the authorized signer, EIN or name of the business has changed. Change of address Deactivate your PIN Contact the E-help Desk at 866-255-0654 between Monday–Friday 6:30 a.m.– 6 p.m. Central Time. Additional information You are the only authorized signer for your own employment tax returns. You cannot electronically send returns directly to the IRS. You can only send returns by a third-party transmitter using approved software. Select the company you would like to use to file your employment tax forms electronically. Note: Electronic return originators must use Form 8879-EMP, IRS e-file Signature Authorization for Forms 940, 940-PR, 941, 941-PR, 941-SS, 943, 943-PR, 944, and 945 to electronically sign employment tax returns. pages.text: Meet NPR's Planet Money! : Planet Money : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Meet NPR's Planet Money! : Planet Money Planet Money is the most entertaining way to understand the economy. Or that's what someone told us once, anyway. NPR Planet Money LISTEN & FOLLOW NPR App Apple Podcasts Spotify YouTube Amazon Music iHeart Radio RSS link Planet Money About 'Planet Money' April 1, 2010 11:00 AM ET Imagine you could call up a friend and say, "Meet me at the bar and tell me what's going on with the economy." Now imagine that's actually a fun evening. That's what we're going for at Planet Money . We find creative, entertaining stories that make sense of the big, complicated forces that move our economy and shape your life. That's why we made a t-shirt and traced the supply chain around the world from cotton field to factory; bought 100 barrels of crude oil — paying cash out of a briefcase for fun — then followed it from ground to gas tank; launched a satellite ; and built an adorable algorithmic trading Twitter bot , and adopted an abandoned superhero and built a merchandising empire and created a record label so we could see inside streaming payouts. Since Planet Money launched in 2008 during the financial crisis, it has won many awards including a Peabody and a couple Edward R. Murrow Awards, one for our investigation into Wells Fargo's retaliation against whistle-blowers and one for our "innovative" TikTok . In 2017, we launched The Indicator , a short daily podcast that takes a number or a term from the news and finds context and big ideas behind it in 10 minutes or less. pages.title: What to Expect from Your Employer When You're Expecting | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: What to Expect from Your Employer When You're Expecting | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content What to Expect from Your Employer When You're Expecting Workers who are pregnant, have recently given birth and/or are nursing should know that several federal laws may apply and provide different employment protections at the same time. Check with your State Labor Department to determine if you have additional or greater protections under state law. Selections below are designed to provide a brief overview of federal laws that provide protections to workers who are pregnant and those who have recently given birth and may have related needs such as pumping breast milk upon return to work. What You Should Know During Pregnancy The Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA) requires covered employers to provide “reasonable accommodations” to a worker’s known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions, unless the accommodation will cause the employer an “undue hardship.” Find Out More: What You Should Know About the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act | U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (eeoc.gov) The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) provides eligible employees job-protected leave for prenatal care or when a pregnant worker is unable to work because of the pregnancy. For adoptive or foster parents, the FMLA provides a right to take leave for required counseling, court appointments and related travel prior to foster care placement or adoption. Find Out More: Fact Sheet 28P: Taking Leave from Work When You or Your Family Member Has a Serious Health Condition under the FMLA. Title VII of the Civil Rights Act (Title VII) prohibits discrimination and harassment based on pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions in any aspect of employment including hiring, firing, pay, promotions, training and more. Find Out More: Fact Sheet: Pregnancy Discrimination The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) prohibits discrimination against a job applicant or employee based on a disability, including pregnancy-related disabilities such as diabetes that develops during pregnancy. An employer has to make reasonable accommodations for a worker’s pregnancy-related disability, absent undue hardship. Title VII , the PWFA , and FMLA also protect workers from discrimination or retaliation when they question employer practices or assert their rights. Birth, Bonding Time, and Returning to Work The Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA) requires covered employers to provide “reasonable accommodations” to a worker’s known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, unless the accommodation will cause the employer an “undue hardship.” The protections of the PWFA also apply to postpartum and pumping workers. Find Out More: What You Should Know About the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act | U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (eeoc.gov) The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), as amended by the PUMP Act , requires most employers to provide covered workers reasonable break time and a private space, other than a bathroom, to pump breast milk for one year after the baby’s birth. Find Out More: Fact Sheet #73: FLSA Protections for Employees to Pump Breastmilk at Work Title VII of the Civil Rights Act (Title VII) prohibits discrimination and harassment based on pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions in any aspect of employment including hiring, firing, pay, promotions, training and more. Find Out More: Fact Sheet: Pregnancy Discrimination The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) provides a right to unpaid, job-protected leave for the baby’s birth or the placement of a child with adoptive or foster parents. This right is afforded not only for the birth, but for an extended time to bond with the child within the first year after birth or placement. October 25-31 is National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week Released October 22, 2026 Next week is National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week (NLPPW). Each year, NLPPW brings together individuals, organizations, industry, and state, Tribal, territorial, and local governments to reduce childhood exposure to lead through increased awareness and education. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development developed community resources for NLPPW. The resources include sample social media, key information about lead and lead poisoning, and customizable materials can be used by companies, organizations, governmental entities, and individuals to plan and implement local events and activities about preventing lead exposure. The NLPPW theme for 2026 is “ Keep Kids Safe from Lead ,” which focuses on three key messages: Get the Facts – Learn about lead hazards in your environment Get Your Child Tested – Ensure early detection through a blood lead test Get Your Home Tested – Identify and address potential lead sources Additionally, EPA is hosting a webinar for anyone interested in learning more about lead and protecting children from lead exposure. By the end of the webinar, participants will recognize potential sources of lead exposure, understand its effects, know simple actions to reduce lead exposure, and understand the importance of testing children’s blood lead levels. There will be time at the end for questions from participants. The webinar will take place on Tuesday, October 27 from 2-3 p.m. EST. Register for the webinar . El Formulario 2290 (sp) no puede ser presentado electrónicamente. Únicamente el Formulario 2290, en inglés, puede ser presentado electrónicamente. Sin embargo, recomendamos la presentación electrónica para cualquier persona que deba presentar el Formulario 2290 (sp) y desee recibir su Anexo 1 sellado y con filigrana más rápidamente. Con e-file, lo recibirá casi inmediatamente después de nosotros aceptar su Formulario 2290 presentado electrónicamente. Paso 1: Reúna su información Número de identificación del empleador (EIN, por sus siglas en inglés). No puede utilizar su número de Seguro Social. ¿No tiene un EIN? Solicítelo ahora ; permita cuatro semanas para que registremos su EIN nuevo en nuestros sistemas antes de presentar su Formulario 2290. Utilice el mismo nombre. El nombre de control de e-file tiene que ser el mismo que su nombre según su EIN. Número de identificación del vehículo de cada vehículo. Peso bruto tributable de cada vehículo. Consulte las Instrucciones para el Formulario 2290 (sp) para saber cómo calcular el peso bruto tributable. Paso 2: Elija un proveedor de e-file para los Formularios 2290 y presente su formulario Repase la lista de proveedores comerciales de software participantes (en inglés) y elija uno para el año tributario actual que mejor le convenga según su situación. Los servicios y las tarifas de cada proveedor varían. No se puede presentar el Formulario 2290 electrónicamente en IRS.gov. Tiene que utilizar el software de uno de los proveedores comerciales participantes. Siga las instrucciones del software para completar, firmar, y presentar su declaración electrónicamente. Precaución: el proveedor tercero que usted elija para presentar su Formulario 2290 no le cobra el impuesto que usted adeuda. El proveedor tercero le cobra únicamente sus honorarios. Paso 3: Elija una opción de pago Pague sus impuestos con tarjeta de crédito o débito . Puede pagar por internet, por teléfono o por medio de un dispositivo móvil. Retiro electrónico de fondos . Puede autorizar el débito directo como parte del trámite de e-file. Sistema de Pago Electrónico de Impuestos Federales (EFTPS, por sus siglas en inglés) . Tiene que estar preinscrito; asegúrese de permitir de cinco a siete días laborables para inscribirse. Usted recibirá su Anexo 1 con la filigrana de parte de su proveedor de e-file a través del correo electrónico después de que aceptemos su Formulario 2290. pages.text: Reader information on affiliate links | Information | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Information Reader information on affiliate links Fri 8 Dec 2023 05.27 EST First published on Wed 1 Nov 2017 12.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Guardian publishes reviews of a variety of products and services. Our selections are unbiased and are made independently by our journalists. Some of our content contains affiliate links which means the Guardian earns a small commission from the retailer (also known as “affiliate revenue”) when a reader clicks a link in our content and buys a product or signs up to a service. Any article that contains an affiliate link is clearly labelled. Our journalism is never influenced by advertisers or commercial teams and is not written for the purpose of promoting a product. For information on content funding please see our guidelines. The revenue generated through affiliate links in our content helps support our independent journalism. What is affiliate revenue? Affiliate revenue is a small percentage of commission shared between retailers, publishers and affiliate networks that connect them. When a product featured on the Guardian is linked to affiliate revenue, we will always make this clear to readers with a statement at the top of the page on our website. How does it work? The Guardian works with a third-party affiliate aggregator called Skimlinks, who have a relationship with thousands of retailers and publishers. When a product is linked from a Guardian article or gallery, Skimlinks automatically places tracking code in the retailer link if the retailer has an affiliate programme. When a reader clicks on an affiliate link, the tracking code assigns the user’s click a randomly generated number which Skimlinks then uses to identify subsequent purchases. Skimlinks then attributes a commission from the sale to the Guardian. The Guardian is also part of the Amazon Associates programme. We use Skimlinks’ technology to add the Guardian’s unique Associate ID to Amazon affiliate links in our content. This Associate ID is assigned to a user’s click. Amazon then uses this Associate ID to identify subsequent purchases and attribute commission from the sale to the Guardian. How will reader data be used by Skimlinks and Amazon? When a product is linked from a Guardian article or gallery, if the retailer has an affiliate programme, then the link will redirect to the retailer website through the Skimlinks’ network. When a reader clicks on a link, Skimlinks will identify which page the click came from and assign it a randomly generated number or Associate ID. This is communicated to the retailer and associated with any subsequent purchase. Skimlinks or Amazon then reconcile the list of clicks from links on the Guardian with purchases on the retailer’s site. This is used in order to calculate the commission. We do not drop third or first party cookies, or otherwise access local storage through our affiliate links. Instead we use a type of link that redirects users into Skimlinks’ network. This means we are tracking and identifying the click, rather than individuals. Skimlinks will use IP addresses to direct readers to the geographically relevant affiliate link. The IP address and user agent are anonymised and truncated by Skimlinks. Third party sites including Amazon and retailers and sites in Skimlinks’ network may place cookies or collect additional information. Details about Skimlinks use of data is set out in their privacy policy . Details of Amazon’s use of data is set out in their UK and US privacy policies. We do not collect any reader data for the purposes of personalised advertising through our affiliate links. For more information on how we use your data, please visit our privacy policy . See the terms and conditions page for the terms of use of the Guardian site. Explore more on these topics Information Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed

pages.title: New clues reveal the devastation the day the dinosaurs died | National Geographic
pages.description: Unusual traces found in Texas show what happened when the Chicxulub asteroid vaporized a thick bed of rock, unleashing superheated gas that kicked off a calamitous period of climate changes.
pages.text: New clues reveal the devastation the day the dinosaurs died | National Geographic An asteroid impact about 66 million years ago forever changed the trajectory of life on Earth. Now scientists have used bits of ancient debris to measure the blazing temperatures of the dust and gas that spread from the impact site. Illustration by DETLEV VAN RAVENSWAAY, Science Source SCIENCE New clues reveal the devastation the day the dinosaurs died Unusual traces found in Texas show what happened when the Chicxulub asteroid vaporized a thick bed of rock, unleashing superheated gas that kicked off a calamitous period of climate changes. By Maya Wei-Haas Published March 22, 2022 • 8 min read Tiny flecks of white dot a section of crumbly rocks along Texas's Brazos River . To a casual observer, the grains may seem like unremarkable bits of sand, but within their oddball shapes lie clues to the most catastrophic day in our planet's history. Some 66 million years ago, a six-mile wide asteroid slammed into the ocean off the coast of Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula, carving out a 110-mile wide crater known as Chicxulub. In an instant, the trajectory of life on Earth was forever changed . The impact kicked off wildfires and tsunamis across thousands of miles. Then swings in global climate—a dramatic period of cooling followed by a long period of warming—ushered in the extinction of some 75 percent of all species, including the non-avian dinosaurs. ( Dinosaurs' Gaseous Emissions Warmed Earth?) Now a study published in the journal Geology uses the tiny white specks in Texas, known as lapilli, to reveal intriguing new details about what happened in the minutes after that fateful impact: The asteroid struck with so much power it instantly vaporized a thick bed of carbonate rocks below, sending a superheated gaseous plume billowing upward along with a curtain of rocky fragments blasted from the surface. The lapilli formed somewhere in this geologic jumble of vapor and dust and then rained down on what is now Mexico, Belize, Texas, and even New Jersey . "They're forming in essentially an instant of time," says Gregory Henkes , a geochemist at Stony Brook University in New York and author of the new study. A chemical analysis revealed that the lapilli formed when temperatures soared to some 311 degrees Fahrenheit, hinting at a zone of devastation that reached more than a thousand miles from the crater's center within minutes, the team writes in the study. The lapilli may also hold clues to how much carbon dioxide remained in the atmosphere after the impact, which eventually caused a period of global warming that continued, by one estimate, for as long as 100,000 years . The ancient ripples through Earth's ecosystems from this climactic shift remain relevant today. Humans are essentially "running our own experiments" as we pump greenhouse gasses into the sky, notes Brandon Johnson , a planetary scientist at Purdue University who was not part of the new study. "If we can understand what it did 66 million years ago, we might be able to better understand what it can do today." Chemical thermometers The lapilli analyzed in the new study were collected in the 1990s from a small outcropping of rock in central Texas along the Brazos River. The tiny bits of rock have since posed many mysteries, including how they formed in the first place. Lapilli are well known in deposits from some types of volcanic eruptions , where they grow in the ash plumes as clumps of glassy fragments get bound together by water. "It's actually kind of similar to how a hailstone might grow," Johnson says. 6:50 Lapilli are also found around some impact craters , but whether they form the same way is less clear. Analysis of carbon and oxygen isotopes in the new study provides support for one previously suggested mechanism: The condensed gasses from the vaporized carbonate rocks may act like lapilli glue, holding the tiny clumps together. NIST leads the way in federal engagement in 5G standards development. NIST leads in advanced communications R&D and testing enhanced spectrum. NIST leads efforts to secure advanced communications. NIST Advanced Communications: By the Numbers 200+ NIST staff and associates in the Communications Technology Laboratory 30+ NIST experts leading global standards development organizations including 3GPP, IEEE, IETF, ITU, ORAN, ATIS, ISO-IEC/JTC1, FIDO Alliance, and WinnForum 180+ participants from 80+ industry, academia and government organizations led by NIST in the 5G mmWave Channel Model Alliance to enhance 5G performance and spectrum sharing and coordinate U.S. positions on international standards 320+ technical publications in advanced radio frequency electromagnetics and advanced wireless since 2015, along with leading the U.S. government Future Generation Wireless R&D Development Gaps Analysis NIST leads the way in federal engagement in 5G standards development Providing leadership and technical expertise in the most significant advanced communications related standards bodies — Over 30 NIST experts lead and participate in global standards and specification development organizations such as 3GPP, IEEE, IETF, ITU-T, ORAN, ATIS, ISO-IEC/JTC1, FIDO Alliance and WinnForum. These experts are a subgroup of over 400 NIST staff that participate in over 1,000 standards development activities in over 110 standardization organizations around the world. Ensuring federal cybersecurity needs are represented in 5G standards — NIST leads the efforts to share information and facilitate coordination among federal agencies and with the private sector on standards for cybersecurity and 5G. NIST has informed interagency discussions on standards engagement, by analyzing and sharing data and information about U.S. participation in some select standards organizations vis-à-vis that of China and Chinese companies. NIST has organized and conducted training for interagency staff on standards-related issues, including effective standards engagements in standards bodies. Enabling industry coordination and outreach — Working with National Economic Council leadership, NIST organized a focus session on 5G standardization at the 2018 White House 5G Summit. Industry speakers from CTIA, ITIC, TIA, ATIS, ANSI, Qualcomm and Oracle identified opportunities and challenges in 5G standardization. On behalf of the National Security Council and NEC, NIST has facilitated interagency discussions and exchanges with the U.S. private sector on 5G and related security standards in partnership with the Information Technology Industry Council, Telecommunications Industry Association and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. NIST leads in advanced communications R&D and testing enhanced spectrum NIST’s role as an independent, impartial measurement organization enables NIST to provide robust test processes and validated measurement data necessary to develop, evaluate and deploy spectrum sharing technologies that can increase access to the crowded frequency spectrum by both federal agencies and nonfederal users. Grüße Hanno Sombach, Tel. +49 (8106) 309060 oder -61. account/diary improvements Posted by dankarran on 3 June 2007 in English . I'm working on (currently planning the way ahead, then will start trying to implement) some improvements to the user account pages and diaries. pages.title: Comment on Proposed Regulations and Submit Petitions | FDA
pages.description: Information about finding and commenting on FDA regulations, how to submit comments electronically via regulations.gov, and submitting petitions to the FDA.
pages.text: Comment on Proposed Regulations and Submit Petitions | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home Regulatory Information Dockets Management Comment on Proposed Regulations and Submit Petitions Dockets Management In this section Making Your Voice Heard at FDA Submit Comments Online You can submit your comments on many of FDA's proposed regulations at Regulations.gov (See Instructions for using Regulations.gov ) Proposed Rules | Electronic Submission of Comments | Petitions As a regulatory agency, FDA publishes rules that establish or modify the way it regulates foods, drugs, biologics, cosmetics, radiation-emitting electronic products, tobacco products and medical devices--commodities close to the daily lives of all Americans. FDA rules have considerable impact on the nation's health, industries, and economy. These rules are not created arbitrarily or in a vacuum, rather they are formed with the public's help. By law, anyone can participate in the rulemaking process by commenting on regulatory actions that FDA proposes. FDA carefully considers all relevant and timely-submitted comments. Proposed Rules When FDA plans to issue a new regulation or revise an existing one, it places an announcement in the Federal Register on the day the public comment period begins. Published every weekday, the Federal Register is available online. Issues open to public comment often are reported by the news media and can also be found at regulations.gov . Instructions for finding Federal Register documents and submitting comments are found on the Federal Dockets Management System Instruction Sheet . In the Federal Register , the "notice of proposed rulemaking" describes the planned regulation and provides background on the issue. It also provides instructions for submitting comments and the name of the person to contact for more information. Also noted is the "comment period," which specifies how long the agency will accept public comments on the proposed rule. The docket usually us open for comments for 60 days, although some comment periods have been as short as ten days or as long as nine months. Weekends and holidays are included in the comment period. Electronic Submission of Comments The Federal Dockets Management System Instruction Sheet tells how to submit comments electronically at regulations.gov . Here are some other suggestions for helping make sure your comment has the greatest possible impact: Clearly indicate if you are for or against the proposed rule or some part of it and why. FDA regulatory decisions are based largely on law and science, and agency reviewers look for reasoning, logic, and good science in comments they evaluate. Refer to the docket number, listed in Federal Register notice (i.e., FDA-20XX-X-XXXX). Include a copy of articles or other references that support your comments. (Electronic attachments will not be forwarded if the "Comment" box is left empty.) Only relevant material should be submitted. If an article or reference is in a foreign language, it must be accompanied by an English translation verified to be accurate. Translations should be accompanied by a copy of the original publication. To protect privacy when submitting medical information, delete names or other information that would identify patients. When a comment is received, it is logged in, numbered, and placed in a file for that docket. It then becomes a public record and is available for anyone to examine at regulations.gov or in FDA Dockets Management Staff's public reading room (5630 Fishers Lane, Room 1061, Rockville, MD 20852). Under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), visitors to the reading room can receive free copies of comments up to 50 pages if their request is for noncommercial use. After that, each page costs 10 cents. Another option is to send FDA a FOIA request ( http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/foi/FOIRequest/index.cfm ) and have copies of comments emailed or mailed to t

pages.description: Katmai National Park & Preserve
pages.text: Katmai National Park & Preserve - Katmai National Park & Preserve (U.S. National Park Service) Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to this park navigation Skip to the main content Skip to this park information section Skip to the footer section National Park Service Katmai National Park & Preserve Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Katmai National Park & Preserve Contact Us Katmai National Park & Preserve Resumen Parque Nacional y Reserva Katmai El Monumento Nacional Katmai fue creado en 1918 para preservar el afamado Valle de las Diez Mil Humaredas, un área espectacular de cuarenta millas cuadradas (104 km²), con una capa de 100 a 700 pies (31 a 213 m) de cenizas depositadas por el volcán Novarupta. Katmai, parque nacional y reserva desde 1980, aún es famoso por sus volcanes, pero también por sus osos pardos, sus prístinos cursos de agua con abundancia de peces, su vida silvestre remota y su litoral irregular. Planifique su visita El Parque Nacional y Reserva Katmai se extiende sobre casi 5 millones de acres (2 millones de ha) de un campo remoto espectacular. Los volcanes glaciales y los desolados escombros volcánicos se elevan por encima de los acantilados escarpados y los densos matorrales de alisos. El Valle de las Diez Mil Humaredas nos sirve para recordar la erupción volcánica increíblemente poderosa que se produjo en 1912 y se oyó hasta en Juneau. El parque y reserva presentan una población increíble de osos pardos (en un estudio reciente se calcularon más de 2,000 osos en el parque y reserva). Muchos de los osos son atraídos por la gran cantidad de peces durante las migraciones de salmón del verano. La pesca deportiva también es reconocida mundialmente en el parque ya que mucha gente llega en busca de la enorme trucha arco iris que nada en diversos ríos y arroyos. Los pescadores también vienen a pescar salmones rojos y plateados (coho), salvelinos y truchas de lago. Gran parte del parque es poco visitado y abundan las oportunidades para disfrutar la vida silvestre. A otras áreas, tales como Brooks Camp, se accede más fácilmente, y cuentan con diversas instalaciones. Horarios y temporadas de apertura El parque está abierto todo el año. En Brooks Camp se ofrecen servicios del Servicio de Parques Nacionales y de concesionarios desde el 1.º de junio hasta el 17 de septiembre. Las actividades en el interior agreste también son ideales durante esta época. Los meses ideales para observar a los osos en Brooks Camp son julio y septiembre, aunque algunos osos pueden permanecer en el área entre finales de mayo y diciembre. Cómo llegar El Parque Nacional y Reserva Katmai está ubicado en la península de Alaska, frente a la isla Kodiak. La oficina central del parque se encuentra en King Salmon, aproximadamente 290 millas (467 km) al sudoeste de Anchorage, en avión. Varias líneas comerciales vuelan diariamente a King Salmon debido a que no hay carreteras hacia el lugar. Brooks Camp, junto al río Brooks, aproximadamente 30 millas (48 km) en avión desde King Salmon, es un destino común para los visitantes del parque. A Brooks Camp sólo se puede acceder mediante un pequeño avión flotante o bote. Cómo recorrer el área Observar a los osos pardos en su hábitat natural y pescar son actividades muy populares en Katmai. La seguridad y la preparación para las condiciones variables son los factores más importantes al visitar un área silvestre como el Parque Nacional y Reserva Katmai. Los meses ideales para observar a los osos en Brooks Camp son julio y septiembre, aunque algunos osos pueden permanecer en el área entre finales de mayo y diciembre. Hay pocos osos, si alguno, cerca de Brooks en junio y agosto, pero sólo podrá verlos en escasas ocasiones.
